610	| **Timeline Zoom** slider | Timeline bar, between − and + | Sets the timeline zoom about the middle of the view. The slider is logarithmic, so the same distance always changes the zoom by the same ratio. |
611	| **Add Shape** | Timeline bar | Opens the shape menu. See [Add Shape](#add-shape). |
612	
613	These have their own control, and do the same as a **View** menu item:
614	
615	| Button | Where | The same as |
616	| --- | --- | --- |
617	| **Fit Timeline** | Timeline bar, after + | **View ▸ Fit Timeline** (<kbd>⇧Z</kbd>) |
618	| **Snap** | Timeline bar | **View ▸ Snapping** (<kbd>N</kbd>) |
619	| **S**, **M** and **L** | Timeline bar | **View ▸ Timeline Track Height**: Small, Medium and Large tracks |
620	| Zoom pop-up: **Fit**, **50%**, **100%**, **200%** | Toolbar | The canvas zoom. **View ▸ Zoom In**, **Zoom Out** and **Zoom to Fit** move through the same four steps. |
621	| **Safe** | Toolbar | **View ▸ Safe Areas** |
622	
623	## Add Shape
624	
625	The **Add Shape** button in the timeline bar is the only way to add a shape clip. There's no menu bar item for it.
626	
627	<Steps>
628	
629	1. Move the playhead to where the shape should start.
630	2. Click **Add Shape**.
631	3. Choose **Rectangle**, **Ellipse**, **Line** or **Arrow**.
632	
633	</Steps>
634	
635	The shape goes on the front track at the playhead. If it doesn't fit there, Frame Job adds a new track above everything and puts it on that. The new clip is selected, and the undo step names the shape, for example **Add Ellipse**. See [Shape clips](/text-and-shapes/shape-clips/).
636	
637	## Context menus
638	
639	Right-click or <kbd>⌃</kbd>-click opens a menu in four places in the editor:
640	
641	- [A track's header, or the empty part of its lane](#track-header-or-empty-lane)
642	- [A row in the Media tab](#media-row)
643	- [A row in the inspector](#inspector-row)
644	- [A channel in the Color tab's curves strip](#curves-channel-strip)
645	
646	A right-click on a clip, the ruler or the timeline's corner opens no menu.
647	
648	A menu acts on what you clicked, not on the selection or the current track.
649	
650	While you record, the [recording status item](#recording-status-item) in the macOS menu bar has a menu too, and a plain click opens it.
651	
652	### Track header or empty lane
653	
654	Right-click a track's header, one of the buttons on it, or the empty part of its lane. The menu is for that track, and its checkmarks show that track's own state.
655	
656	| Item | What it does | Undo step |
657	| --- | --- | --- |
658	| **Hide Video** | Turns the track's picture off or on. See [Hide and lock tracks](/timeline/hide-and-lock-tracks/). | Hide Track |
659	| **Mute Audio** | Turns the track's sound off or on. | Mute Track |
660	| **Lock Track** | Locks or unlocks the track. | Lock Track |
661	| **Solo** | Solos the track, or stops soloing it. See [Mute and solo tracks](/audio/mute-and-solo/). | Solo Track |
662	| **Mix…** | Opens the track's mix panel. See [Track volume and pan](/audio/track-volume-and-pan/). | |
663	| **Matte ▸** | **Off**, **Alpha**, **Inverted Alpha**, **Luma** or **Inverted Luma**, with a checkmark on the track's mode. Choosing the mode it already has beeps. See [Matte tracks](/canvas/matte-tracks/). | Track Matte |
664	| **Remove Track** | Removes the track. If it holds clips, Frame Job asks first and says how many go with it. Greyed when it's the only track. | Remove Track |
665	
666	**Remove Track** here is the way to delete one empty track that isn't the front-most one, because an empty track has no clip to select. **Track ▸ Remove Empty Tracks** deletes every empty track at once.
667	
668	### Media row
669	
670	Right-click a row in the [Media tab](/projects/media-tab/). The menu acts on that file, whatever the list's selection is.
671	
672	| Item | What it does |
673	| --- | --- |
674	| **Insert at Playhead** | Places the file at the playhead, pushing later clips along, and selects its row. Greyed for a LUT. See [Insert and overwrite](/editing/insert-and-overwrite/). |
675	| **Overwrite at Playhead** | Places the file at the playhead, replacing what's in the way, and selects its row. Greyed for a LUT. |
676	| **Reveal in Timeline** | Selects the clips that use the file, scrolls to the first one and switches to the Clip tab. Greyed when no clip on the timeline itself uses the file, which includes a file no clip uses and one used only inside a [nest](/editing/nests/). |
677	| **Reveal in Finder** | Shows the file in the Finder: the original, or the project's copy when there's no original. It beeps when it has neither. |
678	| **Relink…** | Points this entry at a file you choose. It takes the new file's duration, size, frame rate and its audio, video and alpha flags. Frame Job won't relink to a file of another kind, and a clip past the end of a shorter file is shortened to end with it. See [Relink missing media](/projects/relink-media/). |
679	| **Remove** | Removes the file from the project. An unused file goes at once. A used file asks first, and its clips go with it, including clips inside nests. When the file is a LUT, the clips using it keep their place and lose the look, and any file it converts loses its Camera Log. See [Remove media](/projects/remove-media/). |
680	
681	### Inspector row
682	
683	Right-click a row's label, slider or checkbox, or the space beside them. The menu shows only what applies to that row, and with nothing that applies there's no menu. A text field or a pop-up keeps its own menu.
684	
685	| Item | When it's there | What it does |
686	| --- | --- | --- |
687	| **Remove from action N** | The selected action changes this row | Takes the row out of that action. |
688	| **Go to action M** | Another action changes this row | Selects that action. |
689	| **Reset to default** | The row has a default | Puts the row back to its default. Greyed when it's already there. |
690	| **Set end value to default** | The row has a default and animates, and an action is selected | Takes the place of **Reset to default**, and sets the row's value at the action's end. Greyed when it's already there. |
691	
692	On a row the selected action changes, the ◆ in the left gutter turns into × when you hover over it. Click it to remove the row from the action, the same as **Remove from action N**. See [Set what an action animates to](/motion/edit-an-action/).
693	
694	### Curves channel strip
695	
696	Right-click a cell of the curve editor's channel strip in the Color tab. **Reset Master**, **Reset Red**, **Reset Green**, **Reset Blue**, **Reset Hue** or **Reset Sat** puts that one curve back to flat, and is greyed when it already is.
697	
698	### Recording status item
699	
700	This one is in the macOS menu bar, not the editor. While a recording runs its time shows there, and a click opens its menu:
701	
702	- **Recording keyboard shortcuts**, a dimmed row shown only while shortcuts are being recorded
703	- **Pause Recording**, or **Resume Recording** while paused
704	- **Stop Recording**
705	
706	Its tooltip says whether Frame Job is recording or paused. If you quit while a display or window recording is running with the recorder panel hidden, Frame Job opens this menu so you can stop it.
707	
708	If macOS hides the item, for example behind the notch, **File ▸ Stop Recording** and **Pause Recording** still work. See [The menu-bar item](/recording/menu-bar-item/).
709

720	10:- **Action.** An animation on a clip: a span on its action lane with an end state its properties ease to. See [Actions](/motion/actions/).
721	11:- **Adjustment clip.** A clip with no picture of its own that grades every track behind it. See [Adjustment clips](/color/adjustment-clips/).
722	12:- **Canvas.** The fixed frame every clip is drawn into. Every export starts from its size. See [The canvas](/canvas/the-canvas/).
723	13:- **Clip.** One placed piece on a track: a stretch of a media file, or a text, shape, image, graphic, adjustment or nest clip. See [Core concepts](/getting-started/core-concepts/).
724	14:- **Current track.** The track of the first selected clip, or with nothing selected the front-most track. Track commands act on it. See [Menus](/reference/menus/).
725	15:- **Edit point.** A clip's start or end, where <kbd>↑</kbd> and <kbd>↓</kbd> stop. See [Jump around the timeline](/timeline/move-the-playhead/).
726	18:- **Linked pair.** A picture clip and its detached sound, which move, split and ripple together. See [Detach and Attach Audio](/audio/detach-and-attach/).
727	20:- **Nest.** A clip that wraps other clips into a timeline of its own. See [Nests](/editing/nests/).
728	26:- **Selected action.** The one action of the single selected clip that the Clip tab is editing. While it's chosen, the fields show and write its end state. See [Select an action](/motion/select-an-action/).
729	28:- **Track.** A lane of clips. The front track is the top lane, and it's drawn over those behind it. See [Tracks](/timeline/tracks/).
730	34:- **Cutout.** A clip with Remove Background on. See [Remove Background](/effects/remove-background/).
731	36:- **Ducking.** Lowering a clip's sound under another's. See [Ducking](/audio/ducking/).
732	39:- **Look.** A built-in grade or a `.cube` LUT on a clip. See [Looks](/color/looks/).
733	42:- **Matte.** A track that cuts the track behind it by its alpha or brightness. See [Matte tracks](/canvas/matte-tracks/).
734	43:- **Plate.** A clip that fills the canvas behind everything, such as a solid colour or a picture from **Add Background**. See [Backgrounds](/canvas/backgrounds/).
735	44:- **Qualifier.** An adjustment clip's pick of the pixels it grades, by hue, saturation and brightness. See [Qualifiers](/color/qualifiers/).
736	45:- **Ramp.** A speed change over time, a Speed action on the action lane. See [Speed ramps](/speed/speed-ramps/).
737	47:- **Slate.** What a clip draws in place of a picture it doesn't have, such as missing media. See [Relink missing media](/projects/relink-media/).
738	49:- **Transition.** The change from one clip to the next across their overlap on one track. See [Transitions](/motion/transitions/).
739	56:- **Graphic.** A clip whose picture is drawn by code. It's the clip's content, not an effect. See [What a graphic is](/graphics/what-is-a-graphic/).
740	63:- **Props.** The values a graphic is drawn with, stored on its clip. See [Graphic properties](/graphics/properties/).

4	description: "What the preview's canvas shows, how clips stack on it, and what you can do directly on the picture."
5	---
6	
7	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
8	import Shot from '@components/Shot.astro';
9	
10	The canvas is the fixed frame every clip is drawn into. It's where you place a clip's picture, and every export starts from it.
11	
12	<AtAGlance
13	  where={['The preview pane', 'Document tab, for its size, rate and background']}
14	  tools={['render_frame', 'set_video', 'set_selection']}
15	/>
16	
17	<Shot
18	  name="04-editor.window"
19	  alt="The editor with nothing selected. In the preview pane a black 960 × 540 canvas sits in a grey surround, showing a navy video clip smaller than the frame, the words Frame Job inside a white ellipse in front of it, and a lower-third title at the bottom left. The caption under the picture reads 960 × 540 · 30 fps."
20	/>
21	
22	## What the canvas shows
23	
24	The canvas shows the composition at the playhead, at the project's size, centred in the preview pane with a margin of 24 points round it. A thin line marks its edge, so a black canvas still shows against the area around it. Handles and guides stay on the picture however you zoom or pan.
25	
26	A clip smaller than the canvas leaves whatever is behind it showing, down to the background colour. A clip larger than the canvas is cut off at its edge.
27	
28	You don't set the canvas up here. Its size is on [Canvas size](/projects/canvas-size/), and its rate and background colour are on the [Document tab](/projects/document-tab/).
29	
30	## The caption
31	
32	The small line under the picture states the canvas size and frame rate, for example `1920 × 1080 · 30 fps`.
33	
34	## Layers
35	
36	Tracks stack back to front, so a track higher in the timeline draws in front of the ones below it. A track doesn't hold one kind of clip: video, image, still, text, shape, graphic and nest clips can share a track, and you place them all with the same Picture sections, apart from the exceptions on their own pages. All of them but the nest take the same gestures on the canvas.
37	
38	An adjustment clip has no picture of its own, so it has no box on the canvas. Select it on the timeline. See [Adjustment clips](/color/adjustment-clips/).
39	
40	A nest clip's picture is drawn, but it has no box on the canvas either, so a click passes through it. Select it on the timeline and place it on the [Picture tab](/canvas/picture-tab/), or [open it](/editing/inside-a-nest/) to work on the clips inside.
41	
42	## Working on the canvas
43	
44	Drag on the picture and the placement changes. The [Picture tab](/canvas/picture-tab/) shows the same placement as numbers.
45	
46	| To | Do this | More |
47	| --- | --- | --- |
48	| Select a clip | Click it. | [Select on the canvas](/canvas/select-on-canvas/) |
49	| Move a clip | Drag inside its box. | [Move](/canvas/move-scale-rotate/#move) |
50	| Resize a clip | Drag one of the eight square handles. | [Scale](/canvas/move-scale-rotate/#scale) |
51	| Rotate a clip | Drag the round grip above the top edge. | [Rotate](/canvas/move-scale-rotate/#rotate) |
52	| Crop a clip | Press <kbd>C</kbd>, or double-click a clip that isn't text. | [Crop](/canvas/crop/) |
53	| Change a title's words | Double-click a text clip. | [Edit text on the canvas](/text-and-shapes/edit-text-on-canvas/) |
54	| Move one end of a line or arrow | Drag its round end handle. | [Lines and arrows](/text-and-shapes/lines-and-arrows/) |
55	
56	Press <kbd>Esc</kbd> during a drag to [cancel it](/canvas/move-scale-rotate/#cancel-a-drag).
57	
58	### With an action selected
59	
60	While an action is selected on the clip, a move, scale, rotate or crop drag changes that action's end state, as the inspector's fields do. The box on screen still shows the frame at the playhead. See [Select an action](/motion/select-an-action/).
61	
62	Two things always change the clip itself: resizing a shape's box and dragging a line's end. Several clips selected at once have no selected action, so a drag on them changes the clips too.
63	
64	## Hidden and locked tracks
65	
66	Clips on a hidden track aren't drawn, so you can't click them. A clip with its [picture turned off](/editing/enable-picture-and-sound/) draws nothing either, and can't be clicked.
67	
68	Clips on a [locked track](/timeline/hide-and-lock-tracks/) are drawn, but you can't select or move them on the canvas. A click passes through to whatever is behind.
69	
70	- A locked clip you select on the timeline shows its outline on the canvas, with no handles.
71	- If the front-most selected clip is locked, nothing gets handles, even when an unlocked clip is selected behind it.
72	- A drag of several clips leaves any on a locked track where they are.
73	
74	## Canvas modes
75	
76	Some tools wait for a click or a drag on the picture. While one is on, the pointer is a crosshair, a hint at the top of the preview says what to do, and every click on the picture goes to that tool.
77	
78	| Mode | Turn it on with | The hint reads |
79	| --- | --- | --- |
80	| [Zoom to Region](/motion/zoom-to-region/) | <kbd>Z</kbd>, or the Zoom to Region button above the action lane | "Drag a rectangle to zoom to it · ⇧ fills · Esc to cancel" |
81	| [Place on Canvas](/effects/obscure/) | **Place on Canvas** in the Obscure section | "Drag a rectangle to obscure · Esc to cancel" |
82	| [Pick from Canvas](/effects/chroma-key/), for a chroma key | **Pick from Canvas** in the Chroma Key section | "Click to pick the key color · Esc to cancel" |
83	| [Pick from Canvas](/color/pick-from-canvas/), for a qualifier | **Pick from Canvas** in the Qualifier section | "Click to pick the colour to qualify · Esc to cancel" |
84	
85	Only one mode can be on at a time, and turning one on ends any other. A mode ends when:
86	
87	- you finish the drag or the pick
88	- you press <kbd>Esc</kbd>, which changes nothing
89	- you press its key or button a second time
90	- the selection changes so that it's no longer aimed at the same clips
91	
92	Zoom to Region and Place on Canvas need exactly one selected clip that's drawing at the playhead, has a box on the canvas and isn't on a locked track. Otherwise Frame Job beeps and the mode doesn't start. Place on Canvas also beeps when the clip already has four regions. The two pick modes beep the same way when nothing selected can use them.
93	
94	A pick that lands outside the canvas beeps and the mode stays on. So does a rectangle less than 6 canvas pixels wide or high.
95	
96	## With an agent
97	
98	`render_frame` writes the frame at a moment as a picture file, through the same path an export takes, so an agent can look at what it made. See [Check the picture: render_frame](/mcp/render-frame/).
99	
100	`set_video` changes a clip's placement, as a drag does, and `set_selection` selects clips, as a click does. See [Tools: picture and grade](/mcp/tools-set-video/) and [Tools: playhead, range and selection](/mcp/tools-view-state/).

118	
119	Click a clip in the preview to work on it there, without hunting for it on the timeline. It's the same selection the timeline and the inspector use.

122	
123	<Shot
124	  name="05-clip-picture.window"
125	  alt="A video clip selected in the editor. In the preview it has a thin coral outline with white square handles at its four corners and the middle of its four edges, and a round grip on a short stalk above its top edge. The inspector's Clip tab shows the clip's Picture sub-tab."

127	
128	## Click a layer
129	
130	Click the picture to select the front-most visible clip under the pointer at the playhead. The click follows the clip's rotation, so a turned clip is selected by the shape you can see, not by the box it would have upright.
131	
132	The selected clip's handles come first: a handle lying on top of another clip still grabs the handle, so you can resize a clip that has others in front of it.
133	
134	Clicking a clip that's already part of a multiple selection keeps the whole selection, so you can drag them together. To narrow it down to one clip, click empty canvas first or use the [timeline](/timeline/selecting-clips/).
135	
136	## Shift-click
137	
138	<kbd>⇧</kbd>-click adds a clip to the selection, or takes it out if it's already selected.
139	
140	## Clear the selection
141	
142	Click empty canvas, or the area around it, to clear the selection. This also leaves [crop mode](/canvas/crop/).
143	
144	With <kbd>⇧</kbd> held the selection stays, and crop mode still ends.
145	
146	## The selection frame
147	
148	Every selected clip that's drawing at the playhead gets a coral outline with a dark backing line, so it shows on both light and dark pictures. The front-most selected clip has a heavier outline and carries the handles:
149	
150	- Eight white square handles, at the corners and the middle of each edge, for [scaling](/canvas/move-scale-rotate/#scale).
151	- A round grip on a stalk above the top edge, for [rotating](/canvas/move-scale-rotate/#rotate).
152	- On a [line or arrow](/text-and-shapes/lines-and-arrows/), a round handle at each end as well.
153	
154	The handles stay the same size on screen at every zoom. The pointer shows what a handle does: a left-right or up-down resize pointer on an edge handle, and a crosshair on a corner.
155	
156	A selected clip that isn't at the playhead has no frame, because it isn't in the picture. An adjustment clip never has one, because it has no rectangle of its own. Nor does a nest clip, and a click on its picture goes through to whatever is behind. Select it on the timeline. See [Layers](/canvas/the-canvas/#layers).
157	
158	## Matte clips
159	
160	A clip on a [matte track](/canvas/matte-tracks/) can be selected and dragged inside its own box, even though it draws nothing there.
161	
162	Because it's in front of the clip it cuts, a click inside that box selects the matte clip. To select the clip it cuts, click outside the matte clip's box, or use the timeline.
163	
164	## Good to know
165	
166	Clips on hidden tracks can't be clicked, and clips on locked tracks are passed over. See [Hidden and locked tracks](/canvas/the-canvas/#hidden-and-locked-tracks).
167

174	=================== move-scale-rotate
175	---
176	title: "Move, scale and rotate"
177	description: "Place a clip directly on the picture by dragging it, its eight handles and its rotation grip."
178	---
179	
180	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
181	
182	Select a clip on the canvas, then drag it into place. The handles and the grip do the same job as the numbers on the [Picture tab](/canvas/transform/), with the picture in front of you.
183	
184	<AtAGlance
185	  keys={['⌥-drag', '⇧-drag', 'Esc']}
186	  where="The preview canvas"
187	  tools="set_video"
188	/>
189	
190	## Move
191	
192	Drag inside a clip's box to move it. Every selected clip moves by the same amount and keeps its place relative to the others, including a selected clip that isn't at the playhead. Clips on locked tracks stay where they are.
193	
194	The move [snaps](/canvas/canvas-snapping/) to the canvas and to other layers. Snapping goes by the clip you grabbed, so the whole selection clicks into place together.
195	
196	## Nudge
197	
198	To shift a clip by an exact number of pixels, type a new value into **Position X** or **Position Y** on the [Picture tab](/canvas/transform/).
199	
200	The arrow keys don't move a clip on the canvas, even with the canvas focused. They keep their usual job: <kbd>←</kbd> and <kbd>→</kbd> step the playhead by a frame, <kbd>⇧←</kbd> and <kbd>⇧→</kbd> by ten, and <kbd>↑</kbd> and <kbd>↓</kbd> go to the previous and next edit point.
201	
202	To shift a clip earlier or later in time, see [Nudge clips](/editing/nudge-clips/).
203	
204	## Scale
205	
206	Drag a corner or edge handle. The opposite handle stays pinned in place, and the clip moves as it scales to keep it there. This works on a rotated clip too. On a cropped clip, the point that stays pinned is on the uncropped picture, so the cropped edge opposite can shift.
207	
208	What a handle changes depends on the clip:
209	
210	| Clip | Corner handles | Edge handles |
211	| --- | --- | --- |
212	| Video, image, still, graphic | Scale the whole picture and keep its shape. | The same. A clip like this has one scale, so an edge handle can't stretch it. |
213	| [Shape](/text-and-shapes/shape-settings/) | Resize the box and keep its proportions. Hold <kbd>⇧</kbd> to free them. | Change only the width or only the height. |
214	| [Text](/text-and-shapes/text-box/) | Scale the text. | Left and right set the wrap width, with the clip's centre staying still. Top and bottom scale the text. |
215	
216	A drag scales between 1 % and 1000 %. A shape's box and a text clip's wrap width stay between 4 and 20,000 pixels.
217	
218	A drag acts on the front-most selected clip only, even with several selected.
219	
220	## Scale about the centre
221	
222	Hold <kbd>⌥</kbd> while you scale to keep the clip's centre still instead of the opposite handle.
223	
224	## Rotate
225	
226	Drag the round grip above the top edge to turn the clip about its centre. A positive angle turns it clockwise. However far you drag, the angle stays between −180° and 180°, so the inspector never shows a value like 540°.
227	
228	## Snap the angle
229	
230	Hold <kbd>⇧</kbd> while you rotate to snap the angle to 15° steps.
231	
232	## Cancel a drag
233	
234	Press <kbd>Esc</kbd> during a canvas drag to put everything back as it was before the drag, with no undo step. This covers move, scale, rotate, crop, line end and obscure region drags. Timeline drags have no such cancel.
235	
236	<kbd>⇧</kbd> can stay down, but <kbd>Esc</kbd> doesn't cancel while <kbd>⌥</kbd>, <kbd>⌃</kbd> or <kbd>⌘</kbd> is held, so let go of those first.
237	
238	## The pivot
239	
240	Rotation, the Picture tab's **Scale** field and a <kbd>⌥</kbd> scale drag all pivot on the centre of the clip's uncropped picture. There's no separate anchor-point control. Because the pivot is the uncropped centre, cropping never moves it.
241	
242	## One undo step per drag
243	
244	Each canvas drag is one undo step, however many clips it moved, and a click that moves nothing adds no step. The steps are named Move, Scale, Rotate and Crop, so the Edit menu reads **Undo Move**, for example.
245	
246	## Good to know
247	
248	- With an action selected, these gestures change that action's end state rather than the clip. See [With an action selected](/canvas/the-canvas/#with-an-action-selected).
249	- In [crop mode](/canvas/crop/) the eight handles crop the clip instead of scaling it.
250	- A nest clip has no box on the canvas, so none of these gestures reach it. Place it on the [Picture tab](/canvas/transform/).
251

260	=================== transform
261	---
262	title: Position, scale, rotation and opacity
263	description: Set a clip's exact size, place, angle and transparency in the Transform section, or make it fit or fill the canvas.
264	---
265	
266	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
267	import Shot from '@components/Shot.astro';
268	
269	The Transform section holds the numbers behind a clip's place in the frame. Use it when you want an exact value, or when a button can do the work of a drag.
270	
271	<AtAGlance
272	  where={['Clip tab ▸ Picture ▸ Transform', 'Handles on the canvas']}
273	  tools="set_video"
274	/>
275	
276	<Shot
277	  name="05-clip-picture.inspector"
278	  alt="The Transform section at its defaults: Scale 100.0%, Position X 0 px, Position Y 0 px, Rotation 0.0°, Opacity 100%, Blend Normal and Motion Blur 0%, with the Fit to Canvas and Fill Canvas buttons underneath."
279	/>
280	
281	## The Transform section
282	
283	Every clip that draws has Transform, text and shapes included, and it's the one section on the [Picture tab](/canvas/picture-tab/) that starts open. Closed, its summary reads the scale, and the rotation when there is one: `150% · 45°`.
284	
285	| Row | What it does | Default | Range | Quick picks |
286	| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
287	| **Scale** | The clip's size | 100 % | 1 to 1000 % | 25, 50, 75, 100, 150, 200, 400 |
288	| **Position X** | Distance right of the canvas centre | 0 px | −20,000 to 20,000 px | |
289	| **Position Y** | Distance below the canvas centre | 0 px | −20,000 to 20,000 px | |
290	| **Rotation** | The clip's angle | 0° | −180° to 180° | −90, −45, 0, 45, 90, 180 |
291	| **Opacity** | How solid the clip is | 100 % | 0 to 100 % | 0, 25, 50, 75, 100 |
292	| **Blend** | How the clip combines with what's under it. See [Blend modes](/canvas/blend-modes/). | Normal | Eight modes | |
293	| **Motion Blur** | Smear on fast movement. See [Motion blur](/motion/motion-blur/). | 0 % | 0 to 100 % | 0, 25, 50, 100 |
294	
295	Under the rows are [Fit to Canvas and Fill Canvas](#fit-and-fill). [Inspector fields](/getting-started/inspector-fields/) covers typing in a field, its slider and its quick picks.
296	
297	To do the same by hand on the picture, see [Move, scale and rotate](/canvas/move-scale-rotate/).
298	
299	## Scale
300	
301	At 100 % a video or picture draws at its native pixels, one source pixel to one canvas pixel, so a 1920 × 1080 clip on a 3840 × 2160 canvas covers a quarter of it. The field shows one decimal place.
302	
303	A new clip bigger than the canvas doesn't start at 100 %. **Fit new clips to canvas** on the [Document tab](/projects/document-tab/) is on unless you change it, and while it's on the clip starts at the scale that fits.
304	
305	Scale pivots on the centre of the uncropped picture. It works on every clip that draws, text, shapes and graphics included.
306	
307	## Position
308	
309	Position places the clip's centre in canvas pixels, measured from the centre of the canvas. At 0, 0 the clip sits in the middle. **Position X** runs right and **Position Y** runs down, so negative values go left and up.
310	
311	Both are typed fields, shown in whole pixels, with no slider. To place a clip by eye, drag it on the canvas. On a [cropped](/canvas/crop/) clip the fields still measure the centre of the uncropped picture.
312	
313	## Rotation
314	
315	Rotation turns the clip about its centre, and a positive angle turns it clockwise on screen. The field shows one decimal place, and the rotation grip on the canvas sets the same value by hand.
316	
317	## Opacity
318	
319	Opacity sets how see-through the clip is: at 100 % it's solid, and at 0 % it's fully transparent.
320	
321	## Fit and fill
322	
323	Both buttons scale each selected clip and centre it, setting its position to 0, 0.
324	
325	- **Fit to Canvas** makes the whole picture fit inside the canvas, so you may see the background at two edges.
326	- **Fill Canvas** makes the picture cover the whole canvas, so its edges may run off two sides.
327	
328	Each clip gets its own scale from its own size, and all of them together are one undo step. A shape uses its box, a graphic its size and a nest its own canvas.
329	
330	Good to know:
331	
332	- Text clips are skipped, because their size comes from the words. So is any clip with no known size. If that leaves nothing to scale, Frame Job beeps.
333	- Both buttons measure the uncropped picture, so a [cropped](/canvas/crop/) clip can leave a gap after **Fill Canvas**.
334	- Rotation stays as it is and isn't counted, so a rotated clip may not fit or fill the way it would upright.
335	- A scale past the 1 to 1000 % range isn't applied, so a very small picture on a large canvas can get an error from **Fill Canvas** instead.
336	
337	## Reset
338	
339	**Reset** in the section's header puts position, scale, rotation, opacity, blend and motion blur back to their defaults in one step. It shows only while the section differs from its default.
340	
341	It leaves the [crop](/canvas/crop/) alone, which has its own **Reset**. To put back a single row, right-click its label and choose **Reset to default**.
342	
343	## Animate these values
344	
345	With an [action](/motion/actions/) selected, Scale, Position, Rotation, Opacity and Motion Blur set the action's end state, and the clip ramps there along the action's curve. Blend switches at the action's end instead. **Reset** is hidden while you edit an action. **Clear** appears there once the action changes one of these rows, and takes the section out of the action.
346	
347	See [Set what an action animates to](/motion/edit-an-action/).
348	
349	## No stretching
350	
351	Scale is uniform for pictures. A video, image or nest always keeps its proportions, and there's no separate width and height. **Scale** and the canvas handles keep a graphic's proportions too.
352	
353	Three kinds of clip can change on one axis: a shape, through its box's width and height, text, through its wrap width, and a graphic, through **Width** and **Height** in its Size section, which draw it at the new size rather than stretching it. See [Shape fill, stroke and size](/text-and-shapes/shape-settings/), [Text box and wrapping](/text-and-shapes/text-box/) and [Graphic size and timing](/graphics/size-and-timing/#width-and-height).
354	
355	## With an agent
356	
357	`set_video` sets these with `x`, `y`, `scale`, `rotation`, `opacity` and `blend`. Some of its numbers differ from the inspector's:
358	
359	| Key | Takes |
360	| --- | --- |
361	| `scale` | 0.01 to 10, where 1 is native pixels, the inspector's 100 % |
362	| `opacity` | 0 to 1 |
363	| `x`, `y`, `rotation` | Any finite number, with no limit like the inspector's |
364	
365	A value outside its range gets an error rather than being pulled back into the range. See [Tools: picture and grade](/mcp/tools-set-video/#transform-position-scale-rotation-opacity-and-blend).
366	
367	## Related

371	- [Crop](/canvas/crop/)
372	- [Motion blur](/motion/motion-blur/)

380	import Shot from '@components/Shot.astro';
381	
382	The Picture tab is where you place a clip in the frame and style what it draws. It's one sub-tab of the inspector's **Clip** tab, and the sections it shows depend on what you've selected.
383

385

Behind Subject and Layout sit below it."

390	
391	## Open the Picture tab
392	
393	Select a clip, open the inspector's **Clip** tab and choose **Picture**. A video or image clip opens on it, while a text clip opens on **Text**, a shape on **Shape** and a graphic on **Graphic**.
394	
395	The sub-tabs you get depend on the clip:
396	
397	| Selected | Sub-tabs |
398	| --- | --- |
399	| Video, image or still clip | Picture, Color, Clip |
400	| Text clip | Text, Picture, Clip |
401	| Shape clip | Shape, Picture, Clip |
402	| Graphic clip | Graphic, Picture, Clip |
403	| Nest clip | Picture, Clip |
404	| Adjustment clip | Color, Clip |
405	| Clip of an audio-only file | Sound, Clip |
406	
407	**Sound** joins the list, before **Clip**, on any clip with live audio, such as a video clip with its sound on or a nest with sound inside.
408	
409	A selection with an [adjustment clip](/color/adjustment-clips/) in it has no Picture tab, because an adjustment clip draws nothing of its own.
410	
411	## Sections in order
412	
413	The sections run top to bottom in this order. **Blend** and **Motion Blur** are rows inside Transform.
414	
415	| Section | What it's for | Shown for |
416	| --- | --- | --- |
417	| [Transform](/canvas/transform/) | Scale, position, rotation, opacity, [blend](/canvas/blend-modes/) and [motion blur](/motion/motion-blur/) | Every clip that draws |
418	| [Behind Subject](/effects/text-behind-subject/) | Drawing a clip behind the person in the shot | Every clip that draws except adjustment and nest clips, and only while no nest is open |
419	| [Layout](/framing/layout-section/) | How a camera and a screen recording share the frame | One selected clip of a movie with a known picture size |
420	| [Hide While Silent](/effects/hide-while-silent/) | Fading a camera out while nobody's talking | Every clip that draws except nests |
421	| [Crop](/canvas/crop/) | Trimming the picture's edges | Video, image and still clips |
422	| [Corner Radius](/canvas/corner-radius/) | Rounding the picture's corners | Video, image and still clips |
423	| [Chroma Key](/effects/chroma-key/) | Keying out a green screen | Video, image and still clips |
424	| [Background](/effects/remove-background/) | Removing the background behind a person or subject | Clips of a video file, freeze frames of one, and image clips |
425	| [Cursor](/recording/cursor-settings/) | Styling a recorded pointer | Clips of a movie with a cursor file its picture doesn't already show |
426	| [Shadow](/effects/shadow/) | A drop shadow | Every clip that draws |
427	| [Filters](/effects/filters/) | A stack of up to four filters | Every clip that draws |
428	| [Reflection](/effects/reflection/) | A mirrored copy under the clip | Every clip that draws |
429	| [Spotlight](/effects/spotlight/) | Dimming the canvas outside one area | Every clip that draws |
430	| [Obscure](/effects/obscure/) | Blurring or pixelating regions of the picture | Every clip that draws |
431	
432	Every clip that draws includes text, shapes, graphics and nests. A section that doesn't apply isn't there at all, rather than greyed out. With several clips selected, a section shows only when it applies to all of them.
433	
434	A graphic clip can be moved, scaled, faded and blended here. It has no Crop, Corner Radius or Chroma Key, and no Color tab.
435	
436	## How sections behave
437	
438	**Fold a section.** Click its header to open or close it. Transform starts open and the rest start closed, and Frame Job remembers what you open and close. A closed section still shows a short summary of its settings.
439	
440	**Reset a section.** **Reset** appears in a section's header only while the section differs from its default. It puts the whole section back. To put back a single row, right-click its label and choose **Reset to default**.
441	
442	**Edit several clips at once.** With several clips selected, a field shows the first clip's value, with a `mixed` badge when the others differ. An edit applies to every selected clip.
443	
444	**Pick a colour.** A colour swatch opens the macOS Colors panel, with opacity.
445	
446	**Edit inside an action.** With an [action](/motion/actions/) selected, the rows that can animate read and write the action's end state, and the sections it animates open by themselves. In a section with such rows, **Reset** is hidden, and **Clear** appears once the action changes something there. **Clear** takes that section out of the action. See [Set what an action animates to](/motion/edit-an-action/).
447	
448	[Inspector fields](/getting-started/inspector-fields/) covers typing, sliders and the quick picks in a field's menu.
449	
450	## Good to know
451	
452	A nest clip has no picture of its own, so most of this tab doesn't reach it. Position, scale, rotation and opacity apply to the clips inside. Blend is greyed, and Shadow, Filters, Reflection, Spotlight and Obscure show but have no effect on the nest clip. Set those on the clips inside the [nest](/editing/nests/). A nest's opacity fades each clip inside separately, rather than the group as one picture.
453	
454	## With an agent
455	
456	`set_video` changes the placement and look of as many clips as you name. You send only the settings to change, at any depth, and everything you leave out keeps its value. An optional group such as `shadow` clears when you set it to `null`, and the `filters` and `obscure` lists are replaced whole.
457	
458	An unknown key or a bad value gets an error naming it, and nothing is dropped or pulled back into its range. Animating a property takes an action, and reaching a clip inside a nest takes `scope`. See [Tools: picture and grade](/mcp/tools-set-video/).
459	
460	## Related

465	=================== crop
466	---
467	title: Crop
468	description: Trim a picture's edges by dragging handles on the canvas or by typing an exact number of pixels.
469	---
470	
471	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
472	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
473	
474	Crop cuts pixels off the edges of a video, image or still clip. Drag the edges on the canvas when you're working by eye, or type the amounts when you need them exact.
475	
476	<AtAGlance
477	  keys="C"
478	  where={['Double-click a clip in the preview', 'Clip tab ▸ Picture ▸ Crop']}
479	  tools="set_video"
480	/>
481	
482	## Crop mode
483	
484	Crop mode turns the handles on the canvas into crop edges.
485	
486	<Steps>
487	
488	1. Select the clip, with the playhead somewhere it's showing.
489	
490	2. Press <kbd>C</kbd>, double-click the clip in the preview, or choose **Crop on Canvas** in the Crop section.
491	
492	3. Drag the [crop handles](#crop-handles).
493	
494	4. Press <kbd>↩</kbd> to [leave crop mode](#leaving-crop-mode).
495	
496	</Steps>
497	
498	<kbd>C</kbd> beeps when no selected clip is showing at the playhead, because there's nothing on the canvas to crop. Double-clicking a text clip opens its text editor instead.
499	
500	Going in and out of crop mode isn't an edit, so it adds nothing to undo.
501	
502	## Crop handles
503	
504	In crop mode the eight square handles become crop edges and the rotation grip goes away. A corner handle moves two edges, and a side handle moves one.
505	
506	The area you're cutting away shows as a faint white shape, inside a dashed outline of the uncropped frame.
507	
508	- A drag changes the crop and nothing else. The clip's position stays put, and the picture doesn't shift.
509	- A crop drag doesn't snap.
510	- At least one source pixel always remains in each direction, however far you drag.
511	- Press <kbd>Esc</kbd> during a drag to cancel it. The crop goes back to where it was, with no undo step.
512	- Each finished drag is one undo step.
513	
514	Dragging inside the box still moves the clip, as it does outside crop mode. With several clips selected, the handles belong to the front-most one and crop only that clip.
515	
516	## Leaving crop mode
517	
518	Your crop stays when you leave. Any of these leaves crop mode:
519	
520	| Do this | Good to know |
521	| --- | --- |
522	| Press <kbd>↩</kbd> or keypad <kbd>Enter</kbd> | Needs the canvas to have focus. |
523	| Press <kbd>Esc</kbd> | Needs the canvas to have focus. During a drag, the first <kbd>Esc</kbd> cancels the drag and the next one leaves the mode. |
524	| Press <kbd>C</kbd> or choose **Crop on Canvas** | <kbd>C</kbd> works wherever the focus is, except while you're typing in a field. |
525	| Click empty canvas | This also clears the selection, unless you hold <kbd>⇧</kbd>. |
526	
527	The canvas has focus once you've clicked or dragged on it. If you pressed <kbd>C</kbd> and haven't touched the canvas yet, press <kbd>C</kbd> again to leave.
528	
529	Clicking a clip that isn't selected doesn't leave crop mode. That clip becomes the selection, and the crop handles move to it.
530	
531	Crop mode also ends if nothing selected is left on the canvas, for example when you clear the selection in the timeline.
532	
533	## The Crop section
534	
535	The **Crop** section on the [Picture tab](/canvas/picture-tab/) has the same four edges as fields, for when you want an exact number. It shows only for video, image and still clips.
536	
537	| Field | What it does | Default | Range |
538	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
539	| **Left** | Source pixels cut from the left edge | 0 px | 0 to 20,000 px |
540	| **Top** | Source pixels cut from the top edge | 0 px | 0 to 20,000 px |
541	| **Right** | Source pixels cut from the right edge | 0 px | 0 to 20,000 px |
542	| **Bottom** | Source pixels cut from the bottom edge | 0 px | 0 to 20,000 px |
543	
544	These are typed fields, with no slider. Each change is one undo step. **Crop on Canvas** under them goes in and out of crop mode.
545	
546	Closed, the section's summary reads `none`, or the four amounts in field order, such as `100·0·100·0`. **Reset** appears in the section's header while there's a crop, and takes all four edges back to 0.
547	
548	Left and Right together must stay under the picture's width, and Top and Bottom under its height. Outside an action, if a number would use up the whole picture, Frame Job shows an error and keeps the crop you had.
549	
550	:::caution
551	With several clips selected, editing one field gives every clip all four of the first clip's amounts, not only the edge you changed. Crop clips of different sizes one at a time.
552	:::
553	
554	## How a crop works
555	
556	A crop removes edges in place. The picture you keep stays exactly where it was on the canvas, so cropping the left edge opens a gap on the left rather than sliding the picture over.
557	
558	The amounts are in the source's own pixels, not canvas pixels, so they stay correct when you scale the clip later. Cutting 100 px from a clip at 50 % takes 50 canvas pixels off it, and the same 100 px at 200 % takes 200.
559	
560	Position, scale and rotation go on measuring from the centre of the uncropped picture. A crop doesn't recentre what's left, so move the clip if you want that.
561	
562	- [Fit to Canvas and Fill Canvas](/canvas/transform/#fit-and-fill) measure the uncropped picture too.
563	- [Corner radius](/canvas/corner-radius/) and the [shadow](/effects/shadow/) follow the cropped edge.
564	- [Reset in Transform](/canvas/transform/#reset) leaves the crop alone.
565	
566	## Animate a crop
567	
568	A crop can change over time. With an [action](/motion/actions/) selected on a single clip, a crop handle or a field sets the crop at the action's end, and the edges move there along the action's curve. See [Set what an action animates to](/motion/edit-an-action/).
569	
570	While you're editing an action, the section's **Reset** is hidden. **Clear** appears there once the action sets a crop, and takes the crop out of that action.
571	
572	## Good to know
573	
574	- Crop mode has no menu item. It's <kbd>C</kbd>, a double-click, or the **Crop on Canvas** button.
575	- <kbd>C</kbd> also opens crop mode on a text, shape or graphic clip, and a double-click does on a shape or graphic. They have no Crop section, so there are no fields and no **Reset**. To take that crop off, undo or drag the handles back.
576	- A nest clip has no box on the canvas, so <kbd>C</kbd> beeps on it.
577	- A clip on a [locked track](/timeline/hide-and-lock-tracks/) shows no crop handles.
578	
579	## With an agent
580	
581	`set_video` sets a crop with `crop`, which holds `l`, `t`, `r` and `b`, each 0 or more, in source pixels. `l` plus `r` must stay under the source's width and `t` plus `b` under its height, or the call gets an error and the crop stays as it was. See [Tools: picture and grade](/mcp/tools-set-video/#crop-and-corners).
582	
583	## Related
584

591	title: Corner radius
592	description: Round the corners of a video, image or still clip, from a soft edge to a pill or a circle.
593	---
594	
595	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
596	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
597	
598	Corner radius rounds the corners of a picture, which is handy for a picture-in-picture or a screen recording sitting on a background.
599	
600	<AtAGlance where="Clip tab ▸ Picture ▸ Corner Radius ▸ Radius" tools="set_video" />
601	
602	## Round the corners
603	
604	<Steps>
605	
606	1. Select a video, image or still clip and open the [Picture tab](/canvas/picture-tab/).
607	
608	2. Open the **Corner Radius** section.
609	
610	3. Drag **Radius**, type a value, or click the chevron for a [quick pick](/getting-started/inspector-fields/#use-a-quick-pick).
611	
612	</Steps>
613	
614	| Row | What it does | Default | Range | Quick picks |
615	| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
616	| **Radius** | How round the corners are, in source pixels | 0 px | 0 to 500 px | 0, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64 |
617	
618	Each change is one undo step. Closed, the section's summary reads the radius, such as `32 px`. **Reset** appears in its header while the radius isn't 0.
619	
620	## How the radius is measured
621	
622	The radius is in the source's own pixels, so it scales with the clip. A radius of 32 px on a clip at 50 % looks like 16 px on the canvas.
623	
624	It rounds the [cropped](/canvas/crop/) picture, so the curve follows the crop rather than the original frame. A [shadow](/effects/shadow/) follows the rounded shape.
625	
626	A radius can't be more than half the picture's shorter side, and anything above that draws as that half. So a big enough radius turns a wide picture into a pill and a square picture into a circle. **Radius** stops at 500 px, so it gets there only when the picture's shorter side, after any crop, is 1,000 px or less.
627	
628	## Animate the radius
629	
630	With an [action](/motion/actions/) selected, **Radius** sets the action's end state, and the corners ramp there along the action's curve. See [Set what an action animates to](/motion/edit-an-action/).
631	
632	## Good to know
633	
634	Only video, image and still clips have this section. A rectangle shape has its own radius: see [Shape fill, stroke and size](/text-and-shapes/shape-settings/).
635	
636	## With an agent
637	
638	`set_video` sets this with `corner_radius`, in source pixels. It takes any value of 0 or more, without the inspector's 500 px stop. See [Tools: picture and grade](/mcp/tools-set-video/#crop-and-corners).

645	=================== canvas-snapping
646	---
647	title: "Canvas snapping"
648	description: "Line a clip up with the canvas and other layers as you move it, and turn the pull off for one drag."
649	---
650	
651	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
652	
653	While you move a clip on the canvas, its box pulls into line with the canvas and with the other layers, and a guide line shows what it lined up with.
654	
655	<AtAGlance
656	  menu="View ▸ Snapping"
657	  keys={['N', '⌘-drag']}
658	  where="The Snap checkbox in the timeline bar"
659	/>
660	
661	## What snaps
662	
663	Only a move snaps. While you drag a clip, its box snaps to:
664	
665	- the canvas's edges, its centre lines and its thirds
666	- the edges and centres of every other clip with a box on the canvas at the playhead, including clips on locked tracks
667	
668	A nest clip has no box, so nothing snaps to it.
669	
670	Frame Job checks the clip's edges and its centre on each axis, and the smallest correction wins. The pull reaches 8 points on screen at any zoom, so it covers fewer canvas pixels the further you zoom in. A snap always lands on a whole canvas pixel.
671	
672	A turned clip snaps by the bounds of its rotated box. With several clips selected, the clip you grabbed is the one checked, and the others in the drag aren't snapped to.
673	
674	Scaling, rotating and cropping don't snap. <kbd>⇧</kbd> while rotating [snaps the angle](/canvas/move-scale-rotate/#snap-the-angle) instead.
675	
676	## Guide lines
677	
678	A guide line is drawn across the whole canvas on each axis that snapped, so you can see what the clip lined up with. It's only there during the drag.
679	
680	## Suspend for one drag
681	
682	Hold <kbd>⌘</kbd> during a drag to stop snapping for as long as it's down. You can hold it from the start or press it partway through, and snapping comes back when you let go of <kbd>⌘</kbd>.
683	
684	## Turn snapping off
685	
686	Press <kbd>N</kbd>, choose **View ▸ Snapping**, or use the **Snap** checkbox in the timeline bar. Snapping is on to begin with, and Frame Job remembers your choice. The canvas and the timeline share the one setting. See [Snapping](/timeline/snapping/).

693	=================== safe-areas
694	---
695	title: "Safe areas"
696	description: "Show guide frames over the picture to keep titles and action clear of the canvas's edges."
697	---

699	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
700	
701	Safe areas are two guide frames over the picture. Use them to keep titles and important action away from the edges, where a screen or a player's controls can cover them.
702	
703	<AtAGlance
704	  menu="View ▸ Safe Areas"
705	  where="The Safe checkbox in the toolbar"
706	/>

708	## Safe area guides
709	
710	Choose **View ▸ Safe Areas**, or tick **Safe** in the toolbar. Two centred frames appear, one at 90 % of the canvas's width and height and one at 80 %. On a 1920 × 1080 canvas that's 1728 × 972 and 1536 × 864.
711	
712	The frames aren't labelled, and the inner one is drawn fainter. The menu item has a checkmark while they show.
713	
714	The guides are off to begin with, and Frame Job remembers your choice between launches.
715	
716	## Good to know
717	
718	- The percentages are of the canvas, not the pane, so the frames zoom and pan with the picture.
719	- They take no clicks, so everything under them still works.
720	- They're guides only. They never appear in an export or a saved frame.

727	=================== zoom-and-pan
728	---
729	title: "Zoom and pan the preview"
730	description: "Look closer at the picture with the zoom popup, the View menu or a pinch, and move around a canvas bigger than the pane."
731	---
732	
733	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
734	
735	Zoom the preview to look closely at the picture or to place something precisely, then pan to reach the part you want. Zooming is only a way of looking: it changes nothing in the project, makes no undo step and is never exported.
736	
737	<AtAGlance
738	  menu={['View ▸ Zoom In', 'View ▸ Zoom Out', 'View ▸ Zoom to Fit']}
739	  keys={['⌘+', '⌘=', '⌘-', '⌘0']}
740	  where={['The zoom popup in the toolbar', 'Pinch, ⌥-scroll or ⌘-scroll over the preview', 'Scroll or Space-drag to pan']}
741	/>
742	
743	## The zoom popup
744	
745	The popup in the toolbar sets how large the picture appears. Its stops are **Fit**, **50%**, **100%** and **200%**. It always shows the zoom the canvas is at, however you got there.
746	
747	**Fit** sizes the canvas to the pane and follows the pane as it changes. At **100%**, one canvas pixel takes one point on screen.
748	
749	Each window starts at **Fit**, and the zoom isn't saved with the project.
750	
751	## View menu commands
752	
753	| Command | Key | What it does |
754	| --- | --- | --- |
755	| **View ▸ Zoom In** | <kbd>⌘+</kbd> or <kbd>⌘=</kbd> | Goes to the next stop up. Greyed at 200%. |
756	| **View ▸ Zoom Out** | <kbd>⌘-</kbd> | Goes to the next stop down. Greyed at Fit. |
757	| **View ▸ Zoom to Fit** | <kbd>⌘0</kbd> | Goes straight back to Fit and centres the canvas. Greyed at Fit. |
758	
759	These zoom the preview. To zoom the timeline, see [Zoom and scroll the timeline](/timeline/zoom-and-scroll/).
760	
761	## Pinch and scroll
762	
763	Pinch on a trackpad over the preview, or scroll with <kbd>⌥</kbd> or <kbd>⌘</kbd> held, to step through the same four stops. The stops are separate steps, so a gesture has to build up a little before it takes the next one.
764	
765	## Panning
766	
767	When the zoomed canvas is bigger than the pane, there are two ways to move it:
768	
769	- Scroll over the preview.
770	- Hold <kbd>Space</kbd> and drag. If you've been working elsewhere, click the canvas first, or <kbd>Space</kbd> plays and pauses instead of panning.
771	
772	You can only pan in a direction where the canvas overflows the pane, so you can't drag the canvas out of view. While the canvas fits, a plain scroll does nothing.
773	
774	Moving between stops keeps your pan, pulled back if it no longer fits. Going back to **Fit** centres the canvas again.
775	
776	## Space on the canvas
777	
778	After you've clicked the canvas, <kbd>Space</kbd> still plays and pauses. Frame Job can't tell a tap from a pan until you let go, so playback starts or stops on the release rather than the press. If you panned while <kbd>Space</kbd> was down, the release does nothing to playback.
779	
780	## Good to know
781	
782	- The stops count up from **Fit** in order, whatever size Fit happens to be. On a small canvas in a large pane, **50%** can be smaller than **Fit**.
783	- While the canvas fits, holding <kbd>Space</kbd> and dragging a clip moves the clip as usual, and playback toggles when you let go of <kbd>Space</kbd>.
784

791	=================== backgrounds
792	---
793	title: Backgrounds
794	description: Fill the space around your footage with a colour, a picture or a blurred copy of the clip, on a new track behind everything.
795	---
796	
797	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
798	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
799	
800	A screen recording that doesn't fill the frame, a phone clip on a landscape canvas or a title standing on nothing all leave the canvas showing. A background fills that space with a colour, a picture or a blurred copy of the clip itself.
801	
802	To change the colour of the canvas itself, see [Canvas background and timecode](/projects/background-and-timecode/).
803	
804	<AtAGlance
805	  menu={[
806	    'Clip ▸ Add Background ▸ Solid Color',
807	    'Clip ▸ Add Background ▸ Image…',
808	    'Clip ▸ Add Blurred Background',
809	  ]}
810	  tools={['add_background', 'add_blurred_background']}
811	/>
812	
813	## Solid Color
814	
815	Choose **Clip ▸ Add Background ▸ Solid Color**. You don't need a selection, and there's no key for it.
816	
817	Frame Job adds a canvas-sized white rectangle named "Background", starting at 0 and as long as the timeline. It's white because the canvas is black by default, and a black background would seem to do nothing.
818	
819	Recolour it in the **Fill** row of the **Shape** tab, or turn on **Gradient** there for a full-canvas ramp. See [Shape fill, stroke and size](/text-and-shapes/shape-settings/) and [Gradient fills](/text-and-shapes/gradients/).
820	
821	## Image
822	
823	<Steps>
824	
825	1. Choose **Clip ▸ Add Background ▸ Image…**. You don't need a selection, and there's no key for it.
826	
827	2. Pick a picture. The panel offers any image type macOS can read, and only image files.
828	
829	</Steps>
830	
831	The picture goes behind everything, scaled to fill the canvas and as long as the timeline. It's named "Background". Fill means it covers the whole canvas and any overflow is cut off at the edges, whatever [**Fit new clips to canvas**](/projects/background-and-timecode/#fit-new-clips-to-canvas) says. To see the whole picture instead, scale it down afterwards.
832	
833	The picture joins the [Media tab](/projects/media-tab/) in the same undo step. If it's already there, the existing entry is reused.
834	
835	If the file can't be read, an alert says so and nothing is added. "Could Not Add the Picture" means it couldn't join the project's media list.
836	
837	## Blurred background
838	
839	This is the usual backdrop for a screen recording or a vertical video: the clip's own picture, blown up past the frame and blurred, so the colours always match.
840	
841	<Steps>
842	
843	1. Select one clip.
844	
845	2. Choose **Clip ▸ Add Blurred Background**. There's no key for it.
846	
847	</Steps>
848	
849	Frame Job puts a copy behind everything, named "Blurred Background", and selects the copy rather than the original, so you can adjust its blur or its scale straight away. The copy is:
850	
851	- at the same start and length, with the same speed and the same part of the source, so both play the same frames
852	- scaled to fill the canvas, centred and uncropped
853	- blended **Normal**, whatever the original uses
854	- blurred by one full-strength Blur [filter](/effects/filters/), which replaces any filters on the original
855	- muted, so the sound doesn't play twice
856	
857	The command works on video, image, still, shape and graphic clips. It's dimmed for a text clip, an adjustment clip and a clip of an audio-only file, which have no picture size to scale to the canvas. It's also dimmed for a nest clip, because a blurred copy of a nest would come out sharp, and when you've selected no clips or more than one.
858	
859	## What a blurred background follows
860	
861	The copy matches the clip at the moment you add it. After that it's a separate clip: moving or trimming the original doesn't move or trim the copy.
862	
863	| The copy leaves behind | So |
864	| --- | --- |
865	| Transition | It's alone on its track, with nothing to transition from. |
866	| Actions | A zoom on the foreground doesn't zoom the backdrop. A speed ramp is an action too, so a copy of a ramped clip plays at the clip's steady speed and doesn't stay in step with it. |
867	| Motion presets and Motion Blur | The backdrop doesn't slide, spin or pulse with the clip in front. |
868	| Remove Background and Behind Subject | The backdrop stays whole. |
869	| Label and ducking | The label isn't copied, and the copy doesn't lower the rest of the mix. |
870	
871	Every other picture setting carries over, including opacity, rotation, corner radius, the colour controls, the drop shadow and the reflection. A rotated clip gives a rotated backdrop, and the fill is worked out as if the picture were square to the canvas, so a large rotation can leave the corners showing.
872	
873	The copy's picture is always on, even if the original's is [turned off](/editing/enable-picture-and-sound/).
874	
875	## A new back-most track
876	
877	Each of the three commands puts one clip on a new track behind every other track, and selects it. A new track is the only place that's sure to be behind everything, with no overlap to check.
878	
879	The track gets the next numbered name, such as "Track 4". One undo step takes the clip and the track away again. The steps are called **Add Background** and **Add Blurred Background**.
880	
881	## Good to know
882	
883	- A colour or picture background is as long as the timeline when you add it, and it doesn't grow with the timeline. Drag its end to [trim](/editing/trimming/) it longer.
884	- On an empty timeline, a colour or picture background is one frame long.
885	- Fill stops at a scale of 1000%, so a picture less than a tenth of the canvas's width or height can't reach the edges.
886	- With a nest open, a background goes on the nest's own tracks, behind everything inside the nest.
887	- A project holds up to 64 tracks, counting the tracks inside nests, and Frame Job won't add a background past that.
888	
889	## With an agent
890	
891	`add_background` with no arguments adds the white background, and `add_blurred_background` takes the `clip` to copy.
892	
893	An agent can do two things the menu can't. It can give the background a `color` and a `duration` of its own, at least one frame long, and it can pass the `media` of a movie that's already in the project instead of a picture. It can't pass `media` and `color` together, and a file with no picture, such as a LUT, can't be a background.
894	
895	A movie background keeps its sound and stops where its file ends, so only a picture or a colour runs the whole timeline. See [Tools: adding clips](/mcp/tools-adding-clips/).
896

905	=================== blend-modes
906	---
907	title: Blend modes
908	description: Choose how a layer combines with what's under it, and understand why a blend can look like it isn't working.
909	---
910	
911	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
912	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
913	
914	A blend mode decides how a layer's colours combine with whatever is already on the canvas under it. Use one to lay a glow over a shot, darken with a texture, or mix two pictures.
915	
916	<AtAGlance where="Clip tab ▸ Picture ▸ Transform ▸ Blend" tools="set_video" />
917	
918	## The Blend popup
919	
920	<Steps>
921	
922	1. Put the layer you want to blend on a track in front of something to blend with.
923	
924	2. Select it and open the [Picture tab](/canvas/picture-tab/).
925	
926	3. In **Transform**, choose a mode from the **Blend** popup.
927	
928	</Steps>
929	
930	Every clip starts on **Normal**. The change is one undo step, and with several clips selected it applies to all of them.
931	
932	Hover over the popup for a reminder of what a blend needs behind it.
933	
934	## The eight modes
935	
936	These are in the popup's order. "Underneath" means every layer behind this one, and the canvas background.
937	
938	| Mode | What it does |
939	| --- | --- |
940	| **Normal** | Draws over what's underneath. |
941	| **Multiply** | Darkens, by multiplying with what's underneath. |
942	| **Screen** | Lightens, the inverse of Multiply. A screened white blob reads as a glow. |
943	| **Add** | Adds the colours together. |
944	| **Overlay** | Multiplies where what's underneath is dark, and screens where it's light. |
945	| **Darken** | Keeps the darker of the two colours. |
946	| **Lighten** | Keeps the lighter of the two colours. |
947	| **Difference** | Gives the absolute difference of the two colours. |
948	
949	## Nothing behind
950	
951	A blend needs something under the layer, and over the empty black canvas it can't do much:
952	
953	| Mode | Over the empty black canvas |
954	| --- | --- |
955	| **Multiply**, **Darken**, **Overlay** | The layer reads black. |
956	| **Screen**, **Add**, **Lighten**, **Difference** | The layer looks unchanged. |
957	
958	The Transform section warns you when that's what's happening, for example "Nothing behind this clip — multiply reads black here." or "Nothing behind this clip — add changes nothing here."
959	
960	The note looks at the clip's whole span, not only the frame at the playhead, so it stays away if anything sits behind any part of the clip. Hidden tracks don't count, and neither do clips with their video turned off. With several clips selected, it's about the first one.
961	
962	It appears only while the canvas background is opaque black. Over a transparent canvas, a blend draws the layer untouched.
963	
964	To give the layer something to blend against:
965	
966	- Use **Clip ▸ Add Background** to put a plate on a new track at the back. See [Backgrounds](/canvas/backgrounds/).
967	- Set a non-black **Background** on the Document tab. See [Canvas background and timecode](/projects/background-and-timecode/).
968	
969	## During a transition
970	
971	A layer always draws as **Normal** for as long as it's in a [transition](/motion/transitions/), whatever blend mode it has. The popup keeps showing the clip's own mode during the overlap. Only the frames in the overlap draw as Normal.
972	
973	## Animate a blend mode
974	
975	An [action](/motion/actions/) can change the mode. It doesn't ramp from one to the other: it holds, then switches at the action's end, and the row shows `at end` while you're editing that action.
976	
977	## Good to know
978	
979	- **Nest clips.** The popup is greyed on a nest clip, with the note "A nest has no pixels of its own to blend — un-group it (⇧⌘G) to blend the clips inside." Use **Clip ▸ Un-nest**, blend the clip you wanted, and nest again.
980	- **Clips inside a nest.** You can blend a clip inside a nest. It blends against the canvas below the whole nest, not against the nest's own clips under it.
981	- **Adjustment clips.** An [adjustment clip](/color/adjustment-clips/) takes no blend mode.
982	- **Matte tracks.** A clip on a [matte track](/canvas/matte-tracks/) keeps its blend mode, but it has no effect while the track is a matte.
983	- **Encoded or linear light.** A project can blend in either. See [Blending: encoded or linear light](/hdr/blending/).
984	
985	## With an agent
986	
987	`set_video` sets the mode with `blend`, one of `normal`, `multiply`, `screen`, `add`, `overlay`, `darken`, `lighten` or `difference`. Any mode but `normal` on a nest clip gets the error "clip 7 shows a nest and cannot take a blend mode". See [Tools: picture and grade](/mcp/tools-set-video/#transform-position-scale-rotation-opacity-and-blend).
988	
989	## Related
990	
991	- [Position, scale, rotation and opacity](/canvas/transform/)
992	- [Backgrounds](/canvas/backgrounds/)
993	- [Blending: encoded or linear light](/hdr/blending/)

995	=================== matte-tracks
996	---
997	title: Matte tracks
998	description: Make one track cut the track behind it, so text, a shape or a movie becomes a window onto your footage.
999	---
1000	
1001	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
1002	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
1003	import Shot from '@components/Shot.astro';
1004	
1005	A matte track cuts the track directly behind it. Its own clips are never drawn. Instead, what they show decides where the track behind can be seen, which turns a title or a shape into a window onto your footage.
1006	
1007	<AtAGlance
1008	  menu="Track ▸ Matte"
1009	  where="Right-click a track's header or the empty part of its lane ▸ Matte"
1010	  tools={['set_track', 'add_adjustment_clip']}
1011	/>
1012	
1013	<Shot
1014	  name="10c-matte-track.window"
1015	  alt="The editor with three tracks. The Window track carries a Matte · Alpha tag and its rectangle clip is drawn pale with a bracket joining it to the Video track below, so the preview shows the video only inside the rectangle, on a black canvas. The Stray track in front reads Matte · nothing behind. The inspector's Picture sub-tab opens with the note: Matte for the track below (Alpha). Not drawn: its blend mode, drop shadow and reflection have no effect."
1016	/>
1017	
1018	## What a matte does
1019	
1020	Any clip that draws can be a matte: text, a shape, a graphic, an image, a movie or a nest.
1021	
1022	A matte belongs to the track, not the clip. Move a clip off the track and it's an ordinary clip again, and move one on and it becomes part of the matte.
1023	
1024	Only the track directly behind is cut, so tracks further back and the canvas show through the hole. Adding, moving or removing a track can change which track that is.
1025	
1026	The cut applies to everything the clip behind draws. Its drop shadow follows the cut-out shape, and its reflection is cut where it lands. It all works in the preview, in rendered frames, at every [Preview Quality](/timeline/preview-quality/) and in every export.
1027	
1028	## Setting a matte
1029	
1030	<Steps>
1031	
1032	1. Put the clips that will do the cutting, such as a text clip, on the track directly in front of the track you want to cut. On the timeline, that's the track directly above it.
1033	
1034	2. Select one of those clips, or right-click that track's header.
1035	
1036	3. Choose a mode from **Track ▸ Matte**, or from the **Matte** submenu of the track's context menu.
1037	
1038	</Steps>
1039	
1040	**Track ▸ Matte** works on the track holding the first selected clip, or the front-most track when nothing is selected. The context menu works on the track you clicked. Right-click or <kbd>⌃</kbd>-click its header or the empty part of its lane to open it.
1041	
1042	A checkmark shows the track's mode. Choosing the mode it already has beeps and makes no undo step. There's no key for a matte, and the undo step is called **Track Matte**.
1043	
1044	## The modes
1045	
1046	| Mode | The track behind shows where the matte clip is |
1047	| --- | --- |
1048	| **Off** | Not a matte. This is an ordinary track, and every track's default. |
1049	| **Alpha** | Opaque |
1050	| **Inverted Alpha** | Transparent |
1051	| **Luma** | Bright |
1052	| **Inverted Luma** | Dark |
1053	
1054	Brightness is Rec. 709 luma, and transparent counts as black, so a half-transparent white counts as half bright.
1055	
1056	Everything outside a matte clip's box is transparent. So at any moment a matte clip is playing, **Alpha** and **Luma** hide the track behind outside the clip, and **Inverted Alpha** and **Inverted Luma** show it there.
1057	
1058	For text, a shape or anything else with see-through parts, start with **Alpha**. A movie or a photo usually fills its box, so **Alpha** would only give you a rectangle. Use **Luma** for those, so their light and dark areas do the cutting.
1059	
1060	## Gaps
1061	
1062	Where the matte track has no clip, the track behind shows uncut, whatever the mode.
1063	
1064	A matte is read moment by moment and no clip is tied to another, so splitting, moving, deleting or pasting can't break a link between them.
1065	
1066	## Turning a matte off
1067	
1068	To turn a cut off for a while, use [**Hide Video**](/timeline/hide-and-lock-tracks/) on the matte track, or [turn off a matte clip's picture](/editing/enable-picture-and-sound/). Either way the track behind shows whole, as it does in a gap. To end the matte for good, choose **Off**.
1069	
1070	## Nothing to cut
1071	
1072	A matte with no target cuts nothing, and its clips still draw nothing. That happens on the back-most track, and on a track directly in front of another matte track. So two matte tracks in a row don't combine: only the one nearest the track behind cuts anything.
1073	
1074	## Matte properties
1075	
1076	A matte clip is drawn like any other clip, into the matte instead of onto the canvas, so most of its settings shape the cut:
1077	
1078	- position, scale, rotation and crop
1079	- corner radius and opacity
1080	- colour, chroma key and filters
1081	- spotlight and obscured regions
1082	- motion presets and actions
1083	- transitions between two matte clips
1084	
1085	Animate the clip and the cut moves with it, so a moving title can wipe footage on.
1086	
1087	A matte clip's blend mode, drop shadow and reflection have no effect. They're kept, and apply again when the track stops being a matte.
1088	
1089	**Motion Blur** has no effect either, on a matte clip or on a clip a matte is cutting. Both draw sharp.
1090	
1091	A matte clip isn't drawn, but it's still there on the canvas. Click inside its box to select it, and drag it like any clip.
1092	
1093	## Sound
1094	
1095	A matte clip's sound still plays. A matte only changes the picture, so **Mute Audio** silences the track as it would any other, and **Hide Video** doesn't.
1096	
1097	## Adjustment clips
1098	
1099	An [adjustment clip](/color/adjustment-clips/) on a track cut by a matte grades only inside the matte. This is how you confine a grade to one area: put the adjustment clip on a track, and make the track directly in front of it a matte.
1100	
1101	An adjustment clip on a matte track does nothing, and the Clip tab says so. Its settings are kept.
1102	
1103	## The note on the Clip tab
1104	
1105	When every selected clip is on a matte track and those tracks share one mode, every sub-tab of the **Clip** tab shows a note under its strip. Every control stays live, and its value comes back into play when the track stops being a matte.
1106	
1107	| Selection | Note |
1108	| --- | --- |
1109	| Clips on a matte track that has a track to cut | "Matte for the track below (Alpha). Not drawn: its blend mode, drop shadow and reflection have no effect." The note names the track's mode. |
1110	| Clips on a matte track with nothing to cut | "Nothing is behind this matte track, so it cuts nothing." |
1111	| Only adjustment clips, on matte tracks of any mode | "An adjustment clip on a matte track has no effect." |
1112	
1113	## On the timeline
1114	
1115	A matte track's header carries a tag such as "Matte · Alpha", under the track name. With nothing to cut, the tag is dimmed and reads "Matte · nothing behind".
1116	
1117	On a short row the tag shares the name's line, and it shortens to "Matte" when the name would lose its room.
1118	
1119	The track's clips are drawn at half opacity with dashed outlines, and a bracket joins the track to the track it cuts. A matte that cuts nothing keeps its dashed outlines and has no bracket.
1120	
1121	## With an agent
1122	
1123	`set_track` sets a track's `matte` to `none`, `alpha`, `alpha_inverted`, `luma` or `luma_inverted`. See [Tools: tracks, markers and canvas](/mcp/tools-tracks-and-markers/#track-mattes). `add_adjustment_clip` adds the adjustment clip, as in [Tools: adding clips](/mcp/tools-adding-clips/).
1124

1133	title: Mattes inside nests
1134	description: See what happens to a matte when you nest or un-nest its tracks, and when a transition crosses them.
1135	---
1136

1138	
1139	A [matte track](/canvas/matte-tracks/) works inside a [nest](/editing/nests/) the same way it does on the timeline. This page covers what happens where the two meet: a clip inside a nest, nesting and un-nesting matted tracks, and transitions across them.
1140	
1141	<AtAGlance
1142	  menu={['Clip ▸ Nest', 'Clip ▸ Un-nest']}
1143	  keys={['⌘G', '⇧⌘G']}
1144	  tools={['nest', 'unnest']}
1145	/>
1146	
1147	## Inside a nest
1148	
1149	With a nest open, **Track ▸ Matte** works on the nest's own tracks, and a matte cuts the track directly behind it among them.
1150	
1151	A nest clip, the one clip that stands for a nest on the timeline, can also sit on a matte track or on a track a matte cuts:
1152	
1153	| Where the nest clip sits | What happens |
1154	| --- | --- |
1155	| On a matte track | Its whole picture is the matte, including any matte inside it. |
1156	| On a track cut by a matte | Every layer it draws is cut. At a soft edge, overlapping layers inside the nest show through each other. |
1157	
1158	A clip inside a nest can come under more than one matte. Frame Job starts at the clip's own track and works outward through each nest around it, out to the timeline:
1159	
1160	- A matte that cuts a track on the way cuts the clip. With several, the clip shows only where all of them let it through, and at soft edges their strengths multiply.
1161	- The first matte track it reaches, whether the clip sits on it or a nest clip around it does, makes the clip part of that matte. Nothing further out applies to it.
1162	
1163	Two clips showing the same nest at the same moment each have their own matte.
1164	
1165	Mattes inside nests work with shadows and reflections, at every [Preview Quality](/timeline/preview-quality/) and in every export.
1166	
1167	## Nest
1168	
1169	**Clip ▸ Nest** keeps a track's matte only when the track it cuts is nested with it. Select clips on both tracks and the pair carries into the nest, so the picture stays the same.
1170	
1171	A matte nested without its target becomes an ordinary track inside the nest. Its clips draw there, so the picture changes unless the nest clip itself lands on a matte track. Undo restores it.
1172	
1173	The nest clip goes on the front-most of the nested clips' tracks that isn't a matte track, which is where a matte pair's picture was drawn. If every nested clip came from a matte track, it goes on the front-most of them, and the whole nest becomes a matte.
1174	
1175	## Un-nest
1176	
1177	**Clip ▸ Un-nest** lines the nest's front-most non-matte track up with the nest clip's track, so the picture comes back as it was. Matte tracks carried in the nest land on the tracks in front of it.
1178	
1179	Un-nest never makes a track a matte. A carried matte clip is a matte again only if the track it lands on is one, as it is when you un-nest straight after nesting. With no track in front, or no room on it, the clip goes on a new ordinary track in front and draws as an ordinary clip.
1180	
1181	## Transitions
1182	
1183	Mattes work through transitions. A dissolve between two clips on a track a matte cuts stays correct under a soft matte, because the same matte cuts both clips.
1184	
1185	A **Cross Dissolve** or **Zoom** works differently when one of its two clips is a nest clip, or when both clips are inside a nest. Frame Job draws each side whole, with its shadows, reflections and mattes, and then mixes the two pictures, matte or not. That means:
1186	
1187	- Layers inside one side don't show through each other part-way through.
1188	- A matte inside a nest clip is drawn whole, and fades once with its side.
1189	- A **Zoom** treats a nest clip as one picture, zooming about the nest clip's centre.
1190	- Clips inside the transition draw without [motion blur](/motion/motion-blur/).
1191	
1192	Push, slide, wipe and fade transitions aren't mixed this way. They apply to each layer on its own.
1193
