8	`set_video` is the one tool behind everything a clip's picture does: where it sits, how it's cropped, its effects, its motion and its grade. It takes a list of clips and a patch, an object holding only the properties you want to change. This page lists every key a patch can hold.
9	
10	<AtAGlance
11	  tools="set_video"
12	  where={['Clip tab ▸ Picture sub-tab', 'Clip tab ▸ Color sub-tab', 'Dragging on the canvas']}
13	/>
14	
15	## `set_video`
16	
17	Merges a patch into each clip's own video properties, as one undo step however many clips it names. It mirrors the Clip tab's [Picture sub-tab](/canvas/picture-tab/) and [Color sub-tab](/color/color-tab/).
18	
19	| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
20	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
21	| `clips` | array of integers | Yes | The clips to change, at least one. `get_project` lists their ids. |
22	| `patch` | object | Yes | The properties to change. The rest of this page lists its keys. |
23	| `scope` | integer | No | A nest id, to edit inside that nest. See [Editing inside a nest](/mcp/nests/). |
24	| `project` | string | No | The path of the open project to act on, as `get_project` reports it. Leave it out for the frontmost one. |
25	
26	```json
27	{ "clips": [12, 14], "patch": { "opacity": 0.8, "shadow": { "blur": 20 } } }
28	```
29	
30	**How a patch merges.** A key you leave out keeps its value, inside a nested object too, so `{shadow: {blur: 20}}` keeps the shadow's colour, angle and distance. On a clip that has no shadow yet, the keys you left out take the defaults listed below. `shadow`, `chroma`, `reflection`, `spotlight`, `motion`, `look`, `cursor`, `cutout` and `hide_silent` set to `null` clear that property. `filters` and `obscure` are lists, so each replaces whole: send the full list, or `[]` to clear it. See [Patches](/mcp/patches/).
31	
32	**Colours.** A colour is four numbers, `[r, g, b, a]`, each 0 to 1. Three numbers are refused, and so is a value outside the range. Two keys differ: the chroma key's colour is three numbers with no alpha, and the cursor's `click_color` is a CSS colour.
33	
34	**What it answers.** `ok` and the `project` summary. If the patch changes nothing, the call says so and leaves no undo step. See [What a call answers](/mcp/what-a-call-answers/).
35	
36	**When it refuses.**
37	
38	- A key or value the patch doesn't know is an error naming its dotted path, array indices included, and the value you sent, such as `filters[1].kind`. Nothing is dropped, corrected or clamped.
39	- A number outside its range is an error naming the key, the range and the number.
40	- A clip with no video properties is an error: "clip 7 has no video properties".
41	- The sections below list what a particular kind of clip can't take.
42	
43	### Which key does what
44	
45	| Keys | Section |
46	| --- | --- |
47	| `x`, `y`, `scale`, `rotation`, `opacity`, `blend` | [Transform](#transform-position-scale-rotation-opacity-and-blend) |
48	| `crop`, `corner_radius` | [Crop and corners](#crop-and-corners) |
49	| `shadow`, `chroma`, `filters`, `reflection`, `spotlight`, `obscure` | [Effects](#effects-shadow-chroma-key-filters-reflection-spotlight-and-obscure) |
50	| `cutout` | [Remove Background](#cutout) |
51	| `behind_subject` | [Text Behind Subject](#behind_subject) |
52	| `cursor` | [The recorded cursor](#cursor) |
53	| `motion` | [Motion presets](#motion) |
54	| `motion_blur` | [Motion blur](#motion_blur) |
55	| `hide_silent` | [Hide While Silent](#hide_silent) |
56	| `color`, `wheels`, `curves`, `look`, `qualifier` | [Light and colour](#color), [wheels](#wheels), [curves](#curves), [looks and LUTs](#look), [the qualifier](#qualifier) |
57	
58	### On an adjustment clip
59	
60	An [adjustment clip](/color/adjustment-clips/) has no picture of its own. Only `color`, `wheels`, `curves`, `look`, the sepia, noir, vignette and invert filters, and `opacity` (the grade's strength) do anything there, and `qualifier` narrows which pixels they reach. The blur, sharpen and pixelate filters and any blend mode are errors, such as "clip 7 is an adjustment clip and cannot take the blur filter".
61	
62	### Animate a property
63	
64	`set_video` changes the clip's base value, which holds for the clip's whole length. To change a value over time, use `add_action` then `set_action_end`. See [Tools: animation](/mcp/tools-animation/). `motion` and `hide_silent` can't be animated.
65	
66	## Transform: position, scale, rotation, opacity and blend
67	
68	The clip's picture is centred on the canvas centre plus `x` and `y`, scaled, then rotated about that same centre. The [Transform section](/canvas/transform/) and dragging on the canvas change the same values.
69	
70	| Key | What it does | Range |
71	| --- | --- | --- |
72	| `x`, `y` | The clip's centre, in canvas pixels from the canvas centre. `y` runs down. | Any number |
73	| `scale` | The size. 1 is native pixels. | 0.01 to 10 |
74	| `rotation` | Degrees about the clip's centre. Positive turns clockwise on screen. | Any number |
75	| `opacity` | How solid the clip is. | 0 to 1 |
76	| `blend` | How the clip combines with what's already on the canvas. | `normal`, `multiply`, `screen`, `add`, `overlay`, `darken`, `lighten`, `difference` |
77	
78	`normal` is the default. A blend mode needs something under it. Over an empty black canvas, `multiply`, `darken` and `overlay` read black, while `screen`, `add`, `lighten` and `difference` change nothing, so `add_background` is usually the call to make first.
79	
80	A blend is forced to `normal` for the length of any transition, and on a clip on a matte track, so the frame there can differ from the value `get_project` reports. A nest clip can't take a blend mode other than `normal`. See [Blend modes](/canvas/blend-modes/).
81	
82	## Crop and corners
83	
84	| Key | What it does | Range |
85	| --- | --- | --- |
86	| `crop` | `{l, t, r, b}`, the pixels to remove from each edge of the source. Cropping never shifts what's left. | Each 0 or more |
87	| `corner_radius` | Rounds the corners of the cropped picture, in source pixels, before it's rotated. | 0 or more |
88	
89	The opposite edges have to leave something behind: `l` plus `r` must be less than the source's width, and `t` plus `b` less than its height. See [Crop](/canvas/crop/) and [Corner radius](/canvas/corner-radius/).
90	
91	## Effects: shadow, chroma key, filters, reflection, spotlight and obscure
92	
93	Each of these is off until you set it. `shadow`, `chroma`, `reflection` and `spotlight` are objects that merge, and `null` clears one. `filters` and `obscure` are lists that replace whole.
94	
95	### Shadow
96	
97	`shadow` is `null` or an object. See [Shadow](/effects/shadow/).
98	
99	| Key | What it does | Range | Default |
100	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
101	| `color` | The shadow's colour. | Four numbers | Black |
102	| `opacity` | How strong it is. | 0 to 1 | 0.5 |
103	| `blur` | How soft it is, in source pixels. | 0 or more | 12 |
104	| `angle` | The direction, in degrees. 0 is to the right, turning anticlockwise. | Any number | 315 |
105	| `distance` | How far it falls, in source pixels. | 0 or more | 8 |
106	
107	### Chroma key
108	
109	`chroma` is `null` or an object. See [Chroma Key](/effects/chroma-key/).
110	
111	| Key | What it does | Range | Default |
112	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
113	| `key` | The colour to remove, as three numbers with no alpha. | Each 0 to 1 | Green, `[0, 1, 0]` |
114	| `tolerance` | How far from the key a colour can be and still go. | 0 to 1 | 0.2 |
115	| `softness` | How gradually the edge falls off. | 0 to 1 | 0.1 |
116	| `spill` | How much of the key's colour to take off what's left. | 0 to 1 | 0.5 |
117	
118	### Filters
119	
120	`filters` is a list of up to four `{kind, amount}` objects. `kind` is `blur`, `sharpen`, `pixelate`, `sepia`, `noir`, `vignette` or `invert`. `amount` is 0 to 1, where 0 does nothing. Each entry must name both keys: leaving one out is an error. A fifth filter is an error, never dropped. Sepia, noir, vignette and invert run in list order. Blur, sharpen and pixelate always run before them, wherever they sit in the list. See [Filters](/effects/filters/).
121	
122	```json
123	{ "filters": [{ "kind": "noir", "amount": 1 }, { "kind": "vignette", "amount": 0.4 }] }
124	```
125	
126	### Reflection
127	
128	`reflection` is `null` or an object. See [Reflection](/effects/reflection/).
129	
130	| Key | What it does | Range | Default |
131	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
132	| `opacity` | How strong the reflection is where it touches the clip. | 0 to 1 | 0.35 |
133	| `height` | How much of the clip is mirrored, as a fraction of its cropped height. | 0 to 1 | 0.5 |
134	| `gap` | The space between the clip and the reflection, in source pixels. | 0 or more | 0 |
135	| `falloff` | How fast it fades, as a fraction of the cropped height. 0 doesn't fade, and 1 reaches transparent exactly at `height`. | 0 to 1 | 1 |
136	
137	### Spotlight
138	
139	`spotlight` is `null` or an object. It dims everything outside a shape and can magnify what's inside it. See [Spotlight](/effects/spotlight/).
140	
141	| Key | What it does | Range | Default |
142	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
143	| `shape` | The shape. | `rect`, `ellipse` | `rect` |
144	| `x`, `y` | The shape's centre, in source pixels from the centre of the cropped picture, `y` down. It can sit outside the picture. | Any number | 0 |
145	| `width`, `height` | The shape's size, in source pixels. | Above 0 | 480, 270 |
146	| `feather` | How many source pixels the edge blurs over. | 0 or more | 40 |
147	| `dim` | How much darker it is outside. 0 changes nothing, and 1 is black. | 0 to 1 | 0.6 |
148	| `zoom` | How much to magnify what's inside. 1 is no zoom. | 1 to 2 | 1 |
149	
150	Because the box is in source pixels, it stays on the picture when the clip is moved, scaled or rotated.
151	
152	### Obscure
153	
154	`obscure` is a list of up to four regions, each hiding what's under it. It uses the spotlight's frame for its centre and box. See [Obscure](/effects/obscure/).
155	
156	| Key | What it does | Range | Default |
157	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
158	| `shape` | The shape. | `rect`, `ellipse` | `rect` |
159	| `x`, `y` | The region's centre, in source pixels from the centre of the cropped picture. | Any number | 0 |
160	| `width`, `height` | The region's size, in source pixels. | Above 0 | 480, 270 |
161	| `feather` | How many source pixels the effect ramps in over. | 0 or more | 20 |
162	| `kind` | How it hides. | `blur`, `pixelate` | `pixelate` |
163	| `amount` | How strongly it hides. | 0 to 1 | 1 |
164	
165	## `cutout`
166	
167	Remove Background: draws the clip as its subject alone, from masks made on your Mac. It mirrors **Clip ▸ Remove Background** and the Picture sub-tab's **Background** section. See [Remove Background](/effects/remove-background/).
168	
169	`cutout` is `null` or an object. `{cutout: {}}` turns it on with all five defaults, an object merges, and `null` removes it.
170	
171	| Key | What it does | Range | Default |
172	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
173	| `subject` | What to keep. `foreground` is the picture's foreground object, and only an image clip can take it. | `person`, `foreground` | `person` |
174	| `quality` | The mask quality. Only `standard` works, and `best` is refused. | `standard` | `standard` |
175	| `background` | `remove` draws only the subject. `keep` draws the clip whole, which [Text Behind Subject](#behind_subject) uses. | `remove`, `keep` | `remove` |
176	| `edge` | Shrinks or grows the outline. | −1 to 1 | 0 |
177	| `feather` | Softens the outline. | 0 to 1 | 0 |
178	
179	A media, still or image clip can take a cutout. A text, shape, graphic, adjustment or nest clip is refused, and so is `foreground` on a media or still clip.
180	
181	**When the masks are made.** They're made as soon as the cutout is set, and `analyze_cutout` says where they stand. See [Tools: reading analysis](/mcp/tools-analysis/). The cut-out draws in the preview, `render_frame` and every export:
182	
183	- The preview draws a frame whole while its mask isn't made yet.
184	- `render_frame` waits up to 30 s for its masks, then draws the clip uncut and says so.
185	- An export waits for every mask it draws.
186	- A stretch of the clip where no person was found draws uncut.
187	
188	**In an action.** `edge` and `feather` animate, and `background` switches when the action ends. `subject` and `quality` are refused there, and an action can't switch the cutout off. On a clip with no cutout, an action's cutout keys do nothing.
189	
190	## `behind_subject`
191	
192	Text Behind Subject: `true` makes the person in a cut-out clip stand in front of this clip, by cutting this clip away wherever that person is at each moment. It looks at every cut-out clip on a track behind it, on the same timeline or in the same nest, and inside any nest on such a track. A cut-out clip in front of it doesn't cut it. Any clip with a `cutout` counts, with `background` set to `remove` or `keep`. The default is `false`. It mirrors the Picture sub-tab's **Behind Subject** section. See [Text Behind Subject](/effects/text-behind-subject/).
193	
194	Any clip that draws a picture can take it, except an adjustment clip or a nest clip, which are refused. In an action it switches when the action ends. [`text_behind_subject`](/mcp/tools-clip-properties/) places a title this way in one step.
195	
196	## `cursor`
197	
198	Styles the pointer Frame Job recorded beside a screen recording, in the movie's [cursor file](/recording/cursor-files/), as it's drawn on this clip. It mirrors the Picture sub-tab's **Cursor** section. See [Style the recorded cursor](/recording/cursor-settings/).
199	
200	`cursor` is `null` or an object. `{cursor: {}}` stores all eight defaults, and an object merges. A value out of range is refused, never clamped.
201	
202	| Key | What it does | Range | Default |
203	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
204	| `show` | Whether the cursor is drawn. | `true`, `false` | `true` |
205	| `scale` | Its size. | 0.25 to 8 | 1 |
206	| `style` | `recorded` draws the recorded image, and `arrow` draws Frame Job's own arrow. `recorded` also draws the arrow at a moment the file holds no cursor image. | `recorded`, `arrow` | `recorded` |
207	| `smoothing` | How much the path is smoothed. | 0 to 1 | 0 |
208	| `hide_idle` | Seconds of no activity before it hides. `null` never hides it. | `null`, 0.5 to 30 | `null` |
209	| `clicks` | What a click draws. | `none`, `ripple` | `none` |
210	| `click_color` | The ripple's colour, as a CSS colour. | Any CSS colour | `#ffffffcc` |
211	| `click_size` | The ripple's size. | 0.25 to 4 | 1 |
212	
213	**In an action.** `scale` and `click_size` animate. `show`, `style`, `clicks` and `click_color` switch when the action ends. `smoothing` and `hide_idle` have no effect in an action, so write them here. On a clip with no cursor, every cursor key in an action switches at the end, so give the clip one first with `{cursor: {}}` if you want them to animate.
214	
215	## `motion`
216	
217	What the clip does on its way in, on its way out and all the way through. It mirrors **Clip ▸ Motion ▸**. See [Motion presets](/motion/motion-presets/).
218	
219	`motion` is `null` or `{in, out, during}`. The three slots merge: a slot you leave out keeps what's stored, a slot set to `null` clears that slot, and `{motion: null}` clears all three.
220	
221	| Slot | Keys | Values |
222	| --- | --- | --- |
223	| `in`, `out` | `kind`, `duration` | `kind` is `fade`, `zoom_in`, `zoom_out`, `slide_left`, `slide_right`, `slide_up`, `slide_down`, `spin` or `pop`. `duration` is in ticks, measured from the clip's first or last frame. |
224	| `during` | `kind`, `amount`, `period` | `kind` is `pulse`, `shake`, `spin`, `bounce` or `drift`. `amount` is 0 to 1. `period` is in ticks, and `drift` ignores it. |
225	
226	```json
227	{ "motion": { "in": { "kind": "fade", "duration": 300000 }, "during": null } }
228	```
229	
230	A slot you name without its keys starts from a half-second `fade`, or for `during` a `pulse` of amount 0.5 and period 1 s.
231	
232	The durations snap to the frame grid, and the period snaps with a floor of one frame, so `get_project` can answer with a number near the one you sent. `in` plus `out` longer than the clip scales both down to meet, rather than being refused. A negative duration, or a period under one tick, is an error.
233	
234	`motion` can't be animated: `set_action_end` refuses it. `get_project` reports the clip as if it weren't moving, because the preset only becomes placement when a frame is drawn.
235	
236	## `motion_blur`
237	
238	Blurs the clip, and its moving cursor, along their motion. It mirrors the **Motion Blur** row in the Picture sub-tab's **Transform** section. See [Motion blur](/motion/motion-blur/).
239	
240	`motion_blur` is 0 to 1, the shutter as a fraction of one canvas frame. 0 is off and the default, and 0.5 is a 180° shutter. It animates in an action, and draws in the preview, `render_frame` and every export.
241	
242	Anything above 0 is refused on a nest clip, so set it on the clips inside, and on an adjustment clip. The clip draws sharp during a transition, including inside a nest clip that's in one, on a matte track or cut by a matte, when Behind Subject cuts it, and with a drop shadow. The value stays stored. See [Where it stays sharp](/motion/motion-blur/#where-it-stays-sharp).
243	
244	## `hide_silent`
245	
246	Fades a clip, usually a camera, out while a media's speech is silent, and back in ahead of the next words. It mirrors the Picture sub-tab's **Hide While Silent** section. See [Hide While Silent](/effects/hide-while-silent/).
247	
248	`hide_silent` is `null` or an object.
249	
250	| Key | What it does | Range | Default |
251	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
252	| `media` | Required. The id of the media, with sound, whose speech the clip follows. | A media id | |
253	| `pre_roll` | How long before speech the clip is fully in, in ticks. | 0 to 3,000,000 (5 s) | 120,000 (0.2 s) |
254	| `hold` | How long after speech it stays, in ticks. | 0 to 3,000,000 (5 s) | 900,000 (1.5 s) |
255	| `fade` | How long the fade takes, in ticks. | 0 to 3,000,000 (5 s) | 180,000 (0.3 s) |
256	
257	```json
258	{ "hide_silent": { "media": 3, "hold": 600000 } }
259	```
260	
261	The fade follows the clips of that media on the clip's own timeline or nest, then in each nest around it, working outwards until it finds one playing. Where none plays, the clip stays visible. These three times don't snap to the frame grid.
262	
263	If the media has no saved speech, this call saves it from the on-device voice detection first, in the same undo step. It's refused when the media has no sound, when its speech hasn't been detected yet ("Try again in a moment."), and on a nest clip, so set it on the clips inside.
264	
265	Only the drawn frame sees the fade: `get_project` reads the clip's opacity without it. `hide_silent` can't be animated.
266	
267	## `color`
268	
269	The thirteen values of the Color sub-tab's **Light** and **Color** sections, in one object. Each is 0 for unchanged, and any subset merges. See [Light](/color/light/) and [Brightness, contrast, saturation and hue](/color/color-section/).
270	
271	| Key | What it does | Range |
272	| --- | --- | --- |
273	| `exposure` | Exposure, in stops. | −3 to 3 |
274	| `temperature` | Positive is warmer. | −1 to 1 |
275	| `tint` | Positive is more magenta. | −1 to 1 |
276	| `highlights` | The upper half of the brightness range. | −1 to 1 |
277	| `shadows` | The lower half of the brightness range. | −1 to 1 |
278	| `whites` | Stretches the picture, held at black. | −1 to 1 |
279	| `blacks` | Stretches the picture, held at white. | −1 to 1 |
280	| `vibrance` | Saturation on the colours that have little. | −1 to 1 |
281	| `fade` | Lifts black towards 10 % and lowers white towards 95 %. | 0 to 1 |
282	| `brightness` | Brightness. | Any number. The inspector's row runs −1 to 1. |
283	| `contrast` | Contrast. | Any number. The inspector's row runs −1 to 1. |
284	| `saturation` | Saturation. | Any number. The inspector's row runs −1 to 1. |
285	| `hue` | Turns every colour's hue this many degrees, red towards yellow towards green, keeping its brightness. | Any number. The inspector's row runs −180 to 180. |
286	
287	A value outside a stated range is refused.
288	
289	The grade runs in this order: `color`, `wheels`, `curves`, `look`, then the sepia, noir, vignette and invert filters.
290	
291	## `wheels`
292	
293	Lift, gamma and gain: three colour pushes, each with its own brightness. An agent can set a push as exact numbers, which the [Wheels section](/color/wheels/) has no field for.
294	
295	`wheels` is `{lift, gamma, gain}`, each `{x, y, master}`, each −1 to 1, with 0 unchanged. Any subset merges, so `{wheels: {lift: {x: 0.2, y: -0.1}}}` keeps lift's `master` and the other two wheels.
296	
297	| Key | What it does |
298	| --- | --- |
299	| `x`, `y` | The colour push. Its angle is the hue (0° red, 120° green, 240° blue), and its length is the strength. It must lie inside the unit circle, so `x²` plus `y²` is at most 1. |
300	| `master` | The brightness. |
301	
302	`lift` moves black and holds white, `gain` moves white and holds black, and `gamma` moves the middle and holds both ends. A value outside these limits is refused, never clamped.
303	
304	## `curves`
305	
306	Writes the curves of the Color sub-tab's **Curves** section, one list of points per channel. See [Master and RGB curves](/color/curves/) and [Hue vs Hue and Hue vs Sat curves](/color/hue-curves/).
307	
308	`curves` is an object with up to six channels. A list replaces that channel whole, and `null` removes it. Each list is 2 to 16 `[x, y]` points with `x` strictly rising.
309	
310	| Channel | `x` | `y` | No change |
311	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
312	| `master`, `red`, `green`, `blue` | 0 to 1 | 0 to 1 | `y` equals `x` from 0 to 1 |
313	| `hue_hue` | Hue in degrees, 0 up to but not including 360 | A shift in degrees, −180 to 180 | Every `y` is 0 |
314	| `hue_sat` | Hue in degrees, 0 up to but not including 360 | A saturation gain, 0 to 2 | Every `y` is 1 |
315	
316	```json
317	{ "curves": { "master": [[0, 0.05], [0.5, 0.55], [1, 1]], "hue_sat": null } }
318	```
319	
320	A curve that changes nothing is stored as no curve. A point outside these limits is refused, never clamped.
321	
322	The tone channels are smooth monotone curves through their points, flat outside the first and last `x`, and a colour goes through `master` first, then its own channel. The two hue curves are smooth curves that wrap at 0 and 360. They run after the tone channels, and both look up the colour's original hue, so `hue_sat` doesn't see the shift `hue_hue` made. A positive shift turns red towards yellow towards green, keeping brightness, and the gain scales saturation. Greys are left alone: a colour whose strongest and weakest channels are within 0.02 of each other doesn't change, and the effect reaches full strength at 0.06.
323	
324	In an action, a curve that changes nothing animates to neutral, and two curves with different point counts blend their values across the action.
325	
326	## `look`
327	
328	Applies one of the eight built-in looks, or an imported `.cube` LUT, at an amount. It mirrors the Color sub-tab's **Look** section and **Clip ▸ Look ▸**. See [Looks](/color/looks/) and [.cube LUTs](/color/luts/).
329	
330	`look` is `null` or an object. `{look: null}` removes it.
331	
332	| Key | What it does | Range | Default |
333	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
334	| `kind` | Which look. | `warm`, `cool`, `teal_orange`, `vivid`, `faded`, `vintage`, `dramatic`, `black_white`, `lut` | |
335	| `media` | The media id of the `.cube` file. Required with `lut`, and refused with any other kind. | A LUT's media id | |
336	| `amount` | How much of it. | 0 to 1 | 1 |
337	
338	```json
339	{ "look": { "kind": "teal_orange", "amount": 0.6 } }
340	```
341	
342	For a LUT, bring the file in with `import_media`, then send `{look: {kind: "lut", media: 9}}` with the id it answers.
343	
344	A new kind keeps the clip's amount, and a built-in kind replaces a LUT. An amount alone needs a clip that already has a look. In an action the amount animates, and a change of kind or of LUT switches when the action ends.
345	
346	## `qualifier`
347	
348	Narrows which pixels an adjustment clip's grade reaches, by hue, saturation and luma. It mirrors the Color sub-tab's **Qualifier** section. See [Qualifiers](/color/qualifiers/).
349	
350	The qualifier is for adjustment clips only. On any other clip it's an error naming the clip. It reads the picture behind the clip, before the grade.
351	
352	`qualifier` is `{hue, saturation, luma, invert, blur}`.
353	
354	| Key | Keys inside it | What it does |
355	| --- | --- | --- |
356	| `hue` | `center`, `width`, `softness` | In degrees. `center` is 0 to 360 and wraps. `width` is 0 to 360, fully selected about the centre. `softness` is 0 to 180, the fall-off outside each edge. A colour's selection fades out as its chroma falls from 0.06 to 0.02, and at 0.02 or under it's never selected. |
357	| `saturation` | `low`, `high`, `softness` | Each 0 to 1, with `low` no more than `high`. Near-black reads as 0. |
358	| `luma` | `low`, `high`, `softness` | Each 0 to 1, with `low` no more than `high`. Rec. 709 luma, or BT.2020 luma in an HLG project. |
359	| `invert` | | `true` selects everything else. |
360	| `blur` | | 0 to 1, 0 being off. Softens the selection by a Gaussian of 24 × `blur` canvas pixels. It never softens a matte cutting the clip, and does nothing while no range is on. |
361	
362	A range merges: `{hue: {}}` turns hue on at centre 30, width 50, softness 25, and saturation and luma turn on at low 0, high 1, softness 0.1. A partial range keeps the rest, and `null` turns a range off. The selection is the product of the ranges that are on. A value outside its bounds is refused, never clamped.
363	
364	In an action the numbers animate, the hue centre taking the short way round, so 350 to 10 passes 0. A range turned on or off, and `invert`, switch when the action ends.
365	
366	`render_frame` with `selection` set to the adjustment clip's id draws what the qualifier selects, as [Show Selection](/color/show-selection/) does. See [Check the picture: render_frame](/mcp/render-frame/).

See [Patches](/mcp/patches/). A colour is four numbers, `[r, g, b, a]`, each 0 to 1. Three numbers are refused, and so is a value outside the range. 390	## `set_text`
391	
392	Changes a text clip's words and typography. It mirrors the Clip tab's Text sub-tab. See [Text clips](/text-and-shapes/text-clips/).
393	
394	| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
395	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
396	| `clips` | array of integers | Yes | The text clips to change, at least one. `get_project` lists their ids. |
397	| `patch` | object | Yes | The text properties to change. The table below lists its keys. |
398	| `scope` | integer | No | A nest id, to edit inside that nest. See [Editing inside a nest](/mcp/nests/). |
399	| `project` | string | No | The path of the open project to act on, as `get_project` reports it. Leave it out for the frontmost one. |
400	
401	| Patch key | What it does | Values |
402	| --- | --- | --- |
403	| `content` | The words. | A string |
404	| `font` | The font, by its PostScript name. | A string |
405	| `size` | The size, in pixels. | Above 0 |
406	| `color` | The text's colour. | Four numbers |
407	| `align` | Horizontal alignment. | `left`, `center`, `right` |
408	| `valign` | Vertical alignment. | `top`, `middle`, `bottom` |
409	| `line_spacing` | The space between lines. | Above 0 |
410	| `tracking` | The space between letters. | Any number |
411	| `outline` | An outline around the letters. | `null`, or `{width, color}` |
412	| `backdrop` | A coloured box behind the text. | `null`, or `{color, padding, radius}` |
413	| `width` | The width to wrap at, in pixels. `null` restores auto-sizing. | `null`, or above 0 |
414	| `animation` | How the words arrive and leave. | `null`, or `{kind, in, out}` |
415	| `case` | `upper` sets the text in capitals before layout, and never changes the word count. | `as_written`, `upper` |
416	| `words` | When each word of a caption page is said. See [Word timings and word style](#word-timings-and-word-style). | A list, or `[]` |
417	| `word_style` | How the word being said is drawn. See [Word timings and word style](#word-timings-and-word-style). | `null`, or an object |
418	
419	```json
420	{ "clips": [21], "patch": { "content": "Chapter two", "size": 96, "outline": { "width": 3 } } }
421	```
422	
423	**Outline and backdrop.** `outline` starts from a width of 2 in black, and `backdrop` from black at 0.6 alpha with padding 12 and radius 8. Width, padding and radius are 0 or more. See [Text outline and backdrop](/text-and-shapes/text-outline-and-backdrop/).
424	
425	**Animation.** `kind` is `typewriter`, `word_fade` or `line_rise`. `in` and `out` are durations in ticks, measured from the clip's first and last frame, and both snap to the frame grid. Either can be 0 for no ramp at that end, and `in` plus `out` longer than the clip shows a partial reveal. It merges, `{animation: null}` clears it, and it starts from a one-second `typewriter` with no `out`. A negative duration is an error. See [Text reveals](/text-and-shapes/text-reveal/).
426	
427	**When it refuses.** A key the patch doesn't know, a value outside its range, or a clip that isn't a text clip ("clip 7 has no text properties") is an error naming what's wrong.
428	
429	## Word timings and word style
430	
431	A caption page is a text clip with a time on each word. `set_text` edits these like any other text key. See [Edit captions](/captions/edit-captions/) and [Word caption styles](/captions/word-caption-styles/).
432	
433	### Word timings
434	
435	`words` is one `{start, end}` per whitespace-separated word of `content`, in ticks from the clip's start, or `[]` for an untimed page.
436	
437	- When the list isn't empty, it must hold exactly one timing for each word. If not, the call answers "this text is timed word by word: 5 timings for 6 words".
438	- A change to `content` that alters the word count must send `words: []` in the same patch.
439	- A word's `end` can't come before its `start`, and each `start` can't come before the one before it. Two words can start together.
440	- A negative `start` is allowed. It means the word was already being said when the clip began.
441	- The times snap to the frame grid, so two words can land on one frame.
442	
443	`words` can't be animated: `set_action_end` refuses it.
444	
445	### Word style
446	
447	`word_style` is `null` or an object. It replaces `animation` on the page.
448	
449	| Key | What it does | Values | Default |
450	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
451	| `mode` | `highlight` draws the whole page and picks out the active word. `build` makes words appear as they're said. | `highlight`, `build` | `highlight` |
452	| `active_color` | The active word's colour. | Four numbers | The text's colour |
453	| `active_scale` | Where the active word's pop settles. 1 is no pop. | 1 to 1.5 | 1 |
454	| `active_pill` | A rounded plate behind the active word. | `null`, or `{color, padding, radius, glide}` | No plate |
455	| `spoken_color` | The colour of words already said. | Four numbers | The text's colour |
456	| `upcoming_color` | The colour of words not yet said, in `highlight` mode. | Four numbers | The text's colour |
457	| `active_fill` | Fills the active word left to right as it's said. | `true`, `false` | `false` |
458	| `pause_dim` | How far the words and pill fade in a pause. | 0 to 1 | 0 |
459	
460	**The pill.** Its `padding` and `radius` are fractions of the text's `size`, starting from 0.2 and 0.25, and its `color` starts as purple. `glide` set to `true` slides the pill from the word before to the active one over 0.2 s, or sooner when the next word starts sooner, instead of jumping.
461	
462	**The fill.** `active_fill` runs from the word's start to its end, taking 0.6 s at most. The part already said draws in `active_color` and the rest in `upcoming_color`, or isn't drawn yet in `build` mode. In `highlight` mode it shows only where those two colours differ.
463	
464	**The pause dim.** `pause_dim` fades the words and the pill to 1 minus `pause_dim` of their opacity, over 0.1 s each way, in a pause of 0.25 s or more. A pause runs from one word's end to the next one's start, before a late first word, and after the last word until the clip ends.
465	
466	```json
467	{ "word_style": { "active_pill": { "glide": true }, "pause_dim": 0.5 } }
468	```
469	
470	## `set_shape`
471	
472	Changes a shape clip's geometry and paint. It mirrors the Clip tab's Shape sub-tab. See [Shape fill, stroke and size](/text-and-shapes/shape-settings/).
473	
474	| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
475	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
476	| `clips` | array of integers | Yes | The shape clips to change, at least one. `get_project` lists their ids. |
477	| `patch` | object | Yes | The shape properties to change. The table below lists its keys. |
478	| `scope` | integer | No | A nest id, to edit inside that nest. See [Editing inside a nest](/mcp/nests/). |
479	| `project` | string | No | The path of the open project to act on, as `get_project` reports it. Leave it out for the frontmost one. |
480	
481	| Patch key | What it does | Values |
482	| --- | --- | --- |
483	| `kind` | The shape. Changing it changes only the kind. | `rectangle`, `ellipse`, `line`, `arrow` |
484	| `width`, `height` | The box, in source pixels. | Above 0 |
485	| `stroke` | The outline. `null` removes it. | `null`, or `{width, color}` |
486	| `fill` | The flat fill. `null` removes it. | `null`, or a colour |
487	| `radius` | A rectangle's corners. | 0 or more |
488	| `arrow_start`, `arrow_end` | Whether a line or arrow has a head at that end. | `true`, `false` |
489	| `from`, `to` | A line's or arrow's ends, as unit coordinates in its box. | Two numbers each, such as `[0, 1]` and `[1, 0]` |
490	| `gradient` | A gradient fill. | `null`, or `{kind, stops, angle}` |
491	
492	```json
493	{ "clips": [30], "patch": { "fill": [0.1, 0.2, 0.9, 1], "stroke": null, "radius": 24 } }
494	```
495	
496	Because changing `kind` changes only the kind, an arrow made this way keeps whatever `arrow_end` it had, unlike one created by `add_shape_clip`. See [Lines and arrows](/text-and-shapes/lines-and-arrows/).
497	
498	**Gradient.** A gradient takes precedence over `fill` while it's set and leaves `fill` in place, so `{gradient: null}` brings the flat colour back. `{gradient: {}}` starts a black-to-white ramp running left to right. See [Gradient fills](/text-and-shapes/gradients/).
499	
500	| Key | What it does | Values |
501	| --- | --- | --- |
502	| `kind` | The ramp's form. A radial gradient is an ellipse inscribed in the box. | `linear`, `radial` |
503	| `stops` | 2 to 8 `{at, color}` objects, `at` being 0 to 1 along the ramp. They needn't be sorted. Sending `stops` replaces them all. | A list |
504	| `angle` | Degrees from the right, turning anticlockwise. It means nothing for `radial`. | Any number |
505	
506	A `line` or `arrow` has no area and ignores the gradient.
507	
508	**When it refuses.** A key the patch doesn't know, a value outside its range, or a clip that isn't a shape clip ("clip 7 has no shape properties") is an error naming what's wrong. Shapes can't be animated: an action's end has no shape group.

510	## `set_clip`
511	
512	Sets a clip's name and colour label. It mirrors the timeline's inline rename, the Clip tab's name field, **Clip ▸ Rename…** (<kbd>⇧⌘R</kbd>) and **Clip ▸ Label ▸**. See [Clip names and labels](/timeline/names-and-labels/).
513	
514	| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
515	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
516	| `clips` | array of integers | Yes | The clips to change, at least one. `get_project` lists their ids. |
517	| `patch` | object | Yes | `name`, `label` or both. A key left out keeps its value, and `null` clears it. |
518	| `scope` | integer | No | A nest id, to edit inside that nest. See [Editing inside a nest](/mcp/nests/). |
519	| `project` | string | No | The path of the open project to act on, as `get_project` reports it. Leave it out for the frontmost one. |
520	
521	```json
522	{ "clips": [12], "patch": { "name": "Intro", "label": "green" } }
523	```
524	
525	**Names.** Names are trimmed, and an empty or blank name clears the name, as `null` does. A clip with no name of its own shows what it holds: the nest, the media file, a text clip's words, or its kind.
526	
527	**Labels.** The six labels are `red`, `orange`, `yellow`, `green`, `blue` and `purple`, drawn as a dot on the clip. The label is stored as given, so keep to these names. Any other name draws in the neutral text colour.
528	
529	A split, duplicate, detach or paste carries the name and label along. `paste_attributes` never does.
530	
531	**When it refuses.** A key other than `name` or `label`, or a value that's neither a string nor `null`, is an error.
532	
533	## `text_behind_subject`
534	
535	Puts a title behind the person in a clip of a video file or a picture, in one undo step. It mirrors **Insert ▸ Text Behind Subject**. See [Text Behind Subject](/effects/text-behind-subject/).
536	
537	| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
538	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
539	| `clip` | integer | No | The clip to put the title behind. Left out, it's picked at `at`. |
540	| `content` | string | No | The title's text. Left out, it's the Title preset's. |
541	| `at` | integer | No | Where the title starts, in ticks, snapped to the frame grid. Left out, it's the playhead. |
542	| `project` | string | No | The path of the open project to act on, as `get_project` reports it. Leave it out for the frontmost one. |
543	
544	The step does four things:
545	
546	- It adds a track named "Behind Subject" directly above the clip's track, and above any matte tracks in front of it.
547	- It adds a text clip with the Title preset at `at`, for 4 s or the rest of the clip if that's shorter.
548	- It sets `behind_subject` on the title.
549	- If the clip has no cutout yet, it sets `{cutout: {background: keep}}` on it, so the camera stays whole and the person still hides the title.
550	
551	The person's masks are made on your Mac, with no key. `analyze_cutout` says where they stand. See [Tools: reading analysis](/mcp/tools-analysis/).
552	
553	**Which clip it picks.** Without `clip`, it looks at the clips of a video file or a picture, with their video on, playing at `at`, on a shown track that isn't a matte track. It takes the front-most selected one, else the front-most with a cutout, else the front-most. The selection is left as it was.
554	
555	**What it answers.**
556	
557	| Key | What it is |
558	| --- | --- |
559	| `ok` | `true`. |
560	| `clip` | The clip the title is behind. |
561	| `track` | The new track's id. |
562	| `text` | The title's clip id. |
563	| `duration` | The title's length, in ticks. |
564	| `cutout_added` | Whether the clip was given a cutout. |
565	| `project` | The project summary. |
566	
567	**When it refuses.** Nothing is done when:
568	
569	- A nest is open. It works on the top-level timeline only, so call `set_scope` with no nest first.
570	- `content` is empty.
571	- No clip of a video file or a picture, with its video on, plays at `at` on a shown track that isn't a matte track.
572	- The named clip isn't a clip of a video file or a picture, with its video on, on a shown track that isn't a matte track.
573	- The named clip doesn't play at `at`.
574	
575	To put any other drawing clip behind the subject by hand, use `set_video` with [`behind_subject`](/mcp/tools-set-video/). An adjustment or nest clip can't take it.

623	## Add Shape
624	
625	The **Add Shape** button in the timeline bar is the only way to add a shape clip. There's no menu bar item for it.
626	
627	<Steps>
628	
629	1. Move the playhead to where the shape should start.
630	2. Click **Add Shape**.
631	3. Choose **Rectangle**, **Ellipse**, **Line** or **Arrow**.
632	
633	</Steps>
634	
635	The shape goes on the front track at the playhead. If it doesn't fit there, Frame Job adds a new track above everything and puts it on that. The new clip is selected, and the undo step names the shape, for example **Add Ellipse**. See [Shape clips](/text-and-shapes/shape-clips/).
636	
637	## Context menus
638	
639	Right-click or <kbd>⌃</kbd>-click opens a menu in four places in the editor:
640	
641	- [A track's header, or the empty part of its lane](#track-header-or-empty-lane)
642	- [A row in the Media tab](#media-row)
643	- [A row in the inspector](#inspector-row)
644	- [A channel in the Color tab's curves strip](#curves-channel-strip)
645	
646	A right-click on a clip, the ruler or the timeline's corner opens no menu.
647	
648	A menu acts on what you clicked, not on the selection or the current track.
649	
650	While you record, the [recording status item](#recording-status-item) in the macOS menu bar has a menu too, and a plain click opens it.
651	
652	### Track header or empty lane
653	
654	Right-click a track's header, one of the buttons on it, or the empty part of its lane. The menu is for that track, and its checkmarks show that track's own state.
655	
656	| Item | What it does | Undo step |
657	| --- | --- | --- |
658	| **Hide Video** | Turns the track's picture off or on. See [Hide and lock tracks](/timeline/hide-and-lock-tracks/). | Hide Track |
659	| **Mute Audio** | Turns the track's sound off or on. | Mute Track |
660	| **Lock Track** | Locks or unlocks the track. | Lock Track |
661	| **Solo** | Solos the track, or stops soloing it. See [Mute and solo tracks](/audio/mute-and-solo/). | Solo Track |
662	| **Mix…** | Opens the track's mix panel. See [Track volume and pan](/audio/track-volume-and-pan/). | |
663	| **Matte ▸** | **Off**, **Alpha**, **Inverted Alpha**, **Luma** or **Inverted Luma**, with a checkmark on the track's mode. Choosing the mode it already has beeps. See [Matte tracks](/canvas/matte-tracks/). | Track Matte |
664	| **Remove Track** | Removes the track. If it holds clips, Frame Job asks first and says how many go with it. Greyed when it's the only track. | Remove Track |
665	
666	**Remove Track** here is the way to delete one empty track that isn't the front-most one, because an empty track has no clip to select. **Track ▸ Remove Empty Tracks** deletes every empty track at once.
667	
668	### Media row
669	
670	Right-click a row in the [Media tab](/projects/media-tab/). The menu acts on that file, whatever the list's selection is.
671	
672	| Item | What it does |
673	| --- | --- |
674	| **Insert at Playhead** | Places the file at the playhead, pushing later clips along, and selects its row. Greyed for a LUT. See [Insert and overwrite](/editing/insert-and-overwrite/). |
675	| **Overwrite at Playhead** | Places the file at the playhead, replacing what's in the way, and selects its row. Greyed for a LUT. |
676	| **Reveal in Timeline** | Selects the clips that use the file, scrolls to the first one and switches to the Clip tab. Greyed when no clip on the timeline itself uses the file, which includes a file no clip uses and one used only inside a [nest](/editing/nests/). |
677	| **Reveal in Finder** | Shows the file in the Finder: the original, or the project's copy when there's no original. It beeps when it has neither. |
678	| **Relink…** | Points this entry at a file you choose. It takes the new file's duration, size, frame rate and its audio, video and alpha flags. Frame Job won't relink to a file of another kind, and a clip past the end of a shorter file is shortened to end with it. See [Relink missing media](/projects/relink-media/). |
679	| **Remove** | Removes the file from the project. An unused file goes at once. A used file asks first, and its clips go with it, including clips inside nests. When the file is a LUT, the clips using it keep their place and lose the look, and any file it converts loses its Camera Log. See [Remove media](/projects/remove-media/). |
680	
681	### Inspector row
682	
683	Right-click a row's label, slider or checkbox, or the space beside them. The menu shows only what applies to that row, and with nothing that applies there's no menu. A text field or a pop-up keeps its own menu.
684	
685	| Item | When it's there | What it does |
686	| --- | --- | --- |
687	| **Remove from action N** | The selected action changes this row | Takes the row out of that action. |
688	| **Go to action M** | Another action changes this row | Selects that action. |
689	| **Reset to default** | The row has a default | Puts the row back to its default. Greyed when it's already there. |
690	| **Set end value to default** | The row has a default and animates, and an action is selected | Takes the place of **Reset to default**, and sets the row's value at the action's end. Greyed when it's already there. |
691	
692	On a row the selected action changes, the ◆ in the left gutter turns into × when you hover over it. Click it to remove the row from the action, the same as **Remove from action N**. See [Set what an action animates to](/motion/edit-an-action/).
693	
694	### Curves channel strip
695	
696	Right-click a cell of the curve editor's channel strip in the Color tab. **Reset Master**, **Reset Red**, **Reset Green**, **Reset Blue**, **Reset Hue** or **Reset Sat** puts that one curve back to flat, and is greyed when it already is.
697	
698	### Recording status item
699	
700	This one is in the macOS menu bar, not the editor. While a recording runs its time shows there, and a click opens its menu:
701	
702	- **Recording keyboard shortcuts**, a dimmed row shown only while shortcuts are being recorded
703	- **Pause Recording**, or **Resume Recording** while paused
704	- **Stop Recording**
705	
706	Its tooltip says whether Frame Job is recording or paused. If you quit while a display or window recording is running with the recorder panel hidden, Frame Job opens this menu so you can stop it.
707	
708	If macOS hides the item, for example behind the notch, **File ▸ Stop Recording** and **Pause Recording** still work. See [The menu-bar item](/recording/menu-bar-item/).
709

720	10:- **Action.** An animation on a clip: a span on its action lane with an end state its properties ease to. See [Actions](/motion/actions/).
721	11:- **Adjustment clip.** A clip with no picture of its own that grades every track behind it. See [Adjustment clips](/color/adjustment-clips/).
722	12:- **Canvas.** The fixed frame every clip is drawn into. Every export starts from its size. See [The canvas](/canvas/the-canvas/).
723	13:- **Clip.** One placed piece on a track: a stretch of a media file, or a text, shape, image, graphic, adjustment or nest clip. See [Core concepts](/getting-started/core-concepts/).
724	14:- **Current track.** The track of the first selected clip, or with nothing selected the front-most track. Track commands act on it. See [Menus](/reference/menus/).
725	15:- **Edit point.** A clip's start or end, where <kbd>↑</kbd> and <kbd>↓</kbd> stop. See [Jump around the timeline](/timeline/move-the-playhead/).
726	18:- **Linked pair.** A picture clip and its detached sound, which move, split and ripple together. See [Detach and Attach Audio](/audio/detach-and-attach/).
727	20:- **Nest.** A clip that wraps other clips into a timeline of its own. See [Nests](/editing/nests/).
728	26:- **Selected action.** The one action of the single selected clip that the Clip tab is editing. While it's chosen, the fields show and write its end state. See [Select an action](/motion/select-an-action/).
729	28:- **Track.** A lane of clips. The front track is the top lane, and it's drawn over those behind it. See [Tracks](/timeline/tracks/).
730	34:- **Cutout.** A clip with Remove Background on. See [Remove Background](/effects/remove-background/).
731	36:- **Ducking.** Lowering a clip's sound under another's. See [Ducking](/audio/ducking/).
732	39:- **Look.** A built-in grade or a `.cube` LUT on a clip. See [Looks](/color/looks/).
733	42:- **Matte.** A track that cuts the track behind it by its alpha or brightness. See [Matte tracks](/canvas/matte-tracks/).
734	43:- **Plate.** A clip that fills the canvas behind everything, such as a solid colour or a picture from **Add Background**. See [Backgrounds](/canvas/backgrounds/).
735	44:- **Qualifier.** An adjustment clip's pick of the pixels it grades, by hue, saturation and brightness. See [Qualifiers](/color/qualifiers/).
736	45:- **Ramp.** A speed change over time, a Speed action on the action lane. See [Speed ramps](/speed/speed-ramps/).
737	47:- **Slate.** What a clip draws in place of a picture it doesn't have, such as missing media. See [Relink missing media](/projects/relink-media/).
738	49:- **Transition.** The change from one clip to the next across their overlap on one track. See [Transitions](/motion/transitions/).
739	56:- **Graphic.** A clip whose picture is drawn by code. It's the clip's content, not an effect. See [What a graphic is](/graphics/what-is-a-graphic/).
740	63:- **Props.** The values a graphic is drawn with, stored on its clip. See [Graphic properties](/graphics/properties/).

1	=================== edit-text-on-canvas.mdx
2	---
3	title: Edit text on the canvas
4	description: Double-click a text clip in the preview to type into it, then apply, add new lines or back out.
5	---
6	
7	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
8	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
9	
10	You can type straight into a text clip in the preview, and see the words wrap where they'll sit in the picture.
11	
12	<AtAGlance
13	  keys={['Return', '⇧Return', 'Esc']}
14	  where="Double-click a text clip in the preview"
15	  tools="set_text"
16	/>
17	
18	## Type on the canvas
19	
20	<Steps>
21	
22	1. Move the playhead so the clip is on the canvas.
23	
24	2. Double-click the clip. The editor opens over it with all the text selected.
25	
26	3. Type. The editor grows and wraps as you go, the way the text will once applied.
27	
28	4. Press <kbd>Return</kbd> to apply.
29	
30	</Steps>
31	
32	The editor uses the clip's own font, tracking and line spacing at the canvas's zoom, so the lines break where they will in the picture. It draws in the interface's own colours, not the clip's, so you can always read what you're typing.
33	
34	**UPPERCASE** text shows as you typed it. A rotated clip's editor stays upright, and the text you apply is the same either way.
35	
36	Opening the editor leaves [crop mode](/canvas/crop/). Double-clicking any other kind of clip enters it.
37	
38	## Apply the text
39	
40	Any of these applies the text and closes the editor:
41	
42	- <kbd>Return</kbd> or keypad <kbd>Enter</kbd>
43	- <kbd>Tab</kbd>, unless Full Keyboard Access is on in System Settings
44	- A click elsewhere in the window, below its title bar
45	
46	Applying is one undo step, **Edit Text**. If the words haven't changed, there's no undo step. After <kbd>Return</kbd> the keys go back to the canvas, so its single-letter keys work again.
47	
48	## Start a new line
49	
50	<kbd>⇧Return</kbd>, <kbd>⌥Return</kbd>, <kbd>⌘Return</kbd> and <kbd>⌃Return</kbd> all start a new line. Caps Lock and <kbd>fn</kbd> don't count, so <kbd>Return</kbd> with either of those still applies.
51	
52	## Leave with Esc
53	
54	Over unchanged text, <kbd>Esc</kbd> closes the editor at once.
55	
56	Over changed text, a sheet asks "Apply your changes to this text?", and reminds you that "Return applies while you type; ⇧Return starts a new line."
57	
58	| Button | What it does |
59	| --- | --- |
60	| **Apply** | Keeps your text and closes the editor. It's the default, on <kbd>Return</kbd>. |
61	| **Revert** | Closes the editor and drops your changes. |
62	| **Cancel** | Goes back to editing. <kbd>Esc</kbd> in the sheet does the same. |
63	
64	While the sheet is up, clicking away doesn't apply the text behind your back.
65	
66	## Use an input method
67	
68	While an input method is composing, <kbd>Return</kbd>, keypad <kbd>Enter</kbd> and <kbd>Esc</kbd> go to the input method, not the editor. They do their usual jobs again once the composition ends.
69	
70	## Good to know
71	
72	- You can only double-click what's on the canvas, and a clip on a [locked track](/timeline/hide-and-lock-tracks/) can't be picked there. To change those words, use **Content** in the [Text sub-tab](/text-and-shapes/text-clips/#write-the-words).
73	- The editor always changes the clip's own words, even with an [action](/motion/actions/) selected. To change the words at an action's end, use **Content**.
74	- On a caption timed word by word, changing the number of words drops the page's timing. See [Text clips](/text-and-shapes/text-clips/#good-to-know).
75	
76	## Related
77	
78	- [Text clips](/text-and-shapes/text-clips/)
79	- [Font and text style](/text-and-shapes/text-style/)
80	- [Text box and wrapping](/text-and-shapes/text-box/)
81	=================== fonts.mdx
82	---
83	title: "Fonts"
84	description: "Which fonts a text clip can use, the faces Frame Job ships with, and what happens when a project's font isn't on this Mac."
85	---
86	
87	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
88	
89	A text clip can use any font installed on your Mac, or one of the faces that come with Frame Job. Both appear in the same list, so there's nothing to set up.
90	
91	<AtAGlance where="Clip tab ▸ Text ▸ Font ▸ Family" />
92	
93	To choose a font, see [Font and text style](/text-and-shapes/text-style/).
94	
95	## Fonts the app ships with
96	
97	These faces are always in the **Family** list. They need no installing, so a project that uses them draws the same on any Mac.
98	
99	| Family | Weights |
100	| --- | --- |
101	| Anton | Regular |
102	| Bebas Neue | Regular |
103	| Darker Grotesque | Light to Black |
104	| IBM Plex Mono | Regular, Medium |
105	| Montserrat | ExtraBold, Black |
106	| Source Sans 3 | ExtraLight to Black |
107	| Source Serif 4 | ExtraLight to Black |
108	
109	All seven are under the SIL Open Font License.
110	
111	## Installed fonts
112	
113	The **Family** list holds every font family on your Mac, in alphabetical order. Frame Job reads it once each time it launches, so a font you install while it's running appears after you quit and reopen it.
114	
115	## When a project's font is missing
116	
117	A project remembers a font by name and doesn't hold the font file. If you open it on a Mac without that font, the project still opens and the **Text** sub-tab still works.
118	
119	- macOS draws the text in a stand-in font.
120	- **Family** shows the first family in the list, which isn't the font the project asked for.
121	- Picking a **Family** or **Style** replaces the missing font on that clip.
122	
123	Until you pick something, the clip keeps the name of its font, so it draws correctly again once the font is installed.
124	
125	:::tip
126	For a project you'll open on more than one Mac, use a font Frame Job ships with, or install the same font on each Mac.
127	:::
128	
129	## Fonts in graphics
130	
131	Graphics work differently. A graphic draws only with the fonts Frame Job ships with and fonts you add to the project, never with the fonts installed on your Mac. A font Frame Job ships with is never packed into a `.fjgraphic` package, because every copy of the app already has it. See [Fonts and pictures in graphics](/graphics/fonts-and-pictures/).
132

138	=================== gradients.mdx
139	---
140	title: "Gradient fills"
141	description: "Fill a rectangle or ellipse with a linear or radial ramp of up to eight colours."
142	---
143	
144	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
145	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
146	
147	A gradient fills a rectangle or ellipse with a ramp of colours in place of a flat fill. Use one for a sky behind a title, or a plate that fades out at one side.
148	
149	<AtAGlance
150	  where="Clip tab ▸ Shape ▸ Gradient"
151	  tools="set_shape"
152	/>
153	
154	## Add a gradient
155	
156	<Steps>
157	
158	1. Select a rectangle or ellipse. The **Shape** sub-tab opens. If you don't have one yet, [add a shape clip](/text-and-shapes/shape-clips/#add-a-shape-clip).
159	
160	2. Open the **Gradient** section. It starts closed, and its header reads "off".
161	
162	3. Tick **Gradient**.
163	
164	4. Set the [kind](#kind), the [angle](#angle) and the colours of the [stops](#stops).
165	
166	</Steps>
167	
168	A new gradient is **Linear**, black to white, at 0°, so it runs from black on the left to white on the right. It's clipped to the shape, rounded corners included.
169	
170	Once it's on, the section's header reads the kind and the number of stops, such as "linear, 2 stops".
171	
172	### The fill and the stroke
173	
174	A gradient covers the [flat fill](/text-and-shapes/shape-settings/#fill-the-shape) but doesn't remove it, so the fill's rows stay live. While both are on, the section says "The gradient covers the Fill colour above; Reset brings it back."
175	
176	The stroke is drawn over the gradient in its own colour.
177	
178	### Turn it off
179	
180	Untick **Gradient** or choose **Reset** in the section's header. Either one brings the flat fill back, or leaves the shape hollow if it had none.
181	
182	Turning the gradient off forgets it. Ticking **Gradient** again starts over at black to white, so use **Edit ▸ Undo** to get a ramp back.
183	
184	## Kind
185	
186	| Kind | How the ramp runs |
187	| --- | --- |
188	| **Linear** | In a straight line across the shape, in the direction of **Angle**. The first and last positions land on the box's edges at every angle. |
189	| **Radial** | Outward from the centre of the box, in an ellipse with the box's proportions. 0 % is the centre and 100 % touches the middle of each side, so a rectangle's corners are past the end of the ramp. |
190	
191	**Kind** starts on **Linear**.
192	
193	## Angle
194	
195	**Angle** points a linear gradient. It runs from 0 to 360°, with quick picks every 45°, and it starts at 0°.
196	
197	0° runs to the right, and the angle turns counter-clockwise.
198	
199	| Angle | The ramp runs |
200	| --- | --- |
201	| 0° | Left to right |
202	| 90° | Bottom to top |
203	| 180° | Right to left |
204	| 270° | Top to bottom |
205	
206	A radial gradient has no direction, so **Angle** is greyed for **Radial**. It keeps its number for when you switch back to **Linear**.
207	
208	## Stops
209	
210	A stop is one colour at one place on the ramp. Each stop has a row, **Stop 1**, **Stop 2** and so on, with three controls.
211	
212	| Control | What it does | Range |
213	| --- | --- | --- |
214	| Swatch | The stop's colour. Lower its opacity in the colour panel to let what's behind show through. | |
215	| Position | How far along the ramp the stop sits. Quick picks 0, 25, 50, 75 and 100. | 0 to 100 % |
216	| **Remove** | Takes the stop off the ramp. Greyed at two stops, because a gradient keeps at least two. | |
217	
218	Rows keep their order when you change a position, so a stop can move past another one. Frame Job sorts the stops by position when it draws, so the order of the rows doesn't change the picture.
219	
220	Past the first and last stops, the end colours carry on to the shape's edge. A ramp whose stops sit at 40 % and 60 % is solid at both sides, with the change in the middle.
221	
222	### Add Stop
223	
224	**Add Stop** puts a new stop in the middle of the widest gap between two stops, in the colour the ramp already has there. The picture doesn't change until you recolour or move the new stop. When two gaps tie, it uses the one nearer 0 %. The new row goes just under the row of the stop at the gap's lower end.
225	
226	A gradient can have up to eight stops. The row says "8 at most", and **Add Stop** is greyed at eight or while the gradient is off.
227	
228	## Good to know
229	
230	- Lines and arrows have no area to fill. The section is greyed for them, and it says "Fills the rectangle or ellipse; a line or arrow keeps its stroke colour." A gradient isn't lost when you switch **Kind** to Line or Arrow, and it's there again when you switch back.
231	- A gradient can't be animated. Its rows always change the clip itself, even while an action is selected. See [Why shape colours don't animate](/text-and-shapes/shape-settings/#why-shape-colours-dont-animate).
232	- With several shapes selected, any change gives them all the same whole gradient, not only the row you changed.
233	- **Opacity** in the **Fill** section doesn't touch a gradient. Use each stop's colour, or **Opacity** in [Transform](/canvas/transform/) to fade the whole shape.
234	
235	## With an agent
236	
237	`set_shape` sets a gradient through its `gradient` key, which holds `kind`, `angle` and `stops`. Each stop is a colour and an `at` from 0 to 1, where the inspector shows 0 to 100 %. Sending `stops` replaces them all, and fewer than 2 or more than 8 is an error that names the count. `{gradient: null}` brings the flat fill back. See [Tools: text, shapes and clip names](/mcp/tools-clip-properties/).
238	
239	## Related
240	
241	- [Shape fill, stroke and size](/text-and-shapes/shape-settings/)
242	- [Shape clips](/text-and-shapes/shape-clips/)
243	- [Backgrounds](/canvas/backgrounds/)
244	=================== image-clips.mdx
245	---
246	title: "Image clips"
247	description: "Put a still picture on the timeline, set how long it stays, and use the same Picture and Color controls as a video clip."
248	---
249	
250	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
251	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
252	
253	An image clip puts a still picture on the timeline: a logo, a photo, a screenshot. It draws like a video clip but has no length of its own, so you decide how long it stays.
254	
255	<AtAGlance
256	  where={['Media tab ▸ drag a picture onto a track or the canvas', 'Clip tab ▸ Picture', 'Clip tab ▸ Color']}
257	  tools={['import_media', 'add_clip']}
258	/>
259	
260	## Place an image
261	
262	<Steps>
263	
264	1. [Import](/projects/import-media/) the picture the way you'd import a movie, with **File ▸ Add Media…** or by dropping it on the Media tab.
265	
266	2. Drag its row onto a track, or onto the preview canvas.
267	
268	</Steps>
269	
270	The picture lands as a five-second clip. A drop on a track puts it at the pointer, and a drop on the canvas puts it at the playhead on a new track in front. See [Add clips to the timeline](/editing/add-clips/) for what stops a drop, and [Insert and overwrite](/editing/insert-and-overwrite/) to make room for it.
271	
272	The picture formats Frame Job can read, and how each one comes in, are on [Supported file formats](/reference/file-formats/).
273	
274	## Length
275	
276	An image clip starts at 5 seconds. A picture has no end to run out of, so you can [trim](/editing/trimming/) it to any length, down to one frame. Drag either edge on the timeline, or type a time into **In** or **Out** in the **Timing** section of the **Clip** sub-tab.
277	
278	There's no footage to retime or turn around, so the **Clip** sub-tab has no **Speed** section and **Timing** has no **Reverse** row.
279	
280	## Starting size
281	
282	A picture bigger than the canvas on either side starts scaled down so all of it shows, while the Document tab's **Fit new clips to canvas** option is on, which it is by default. With the option off it starts at 100 %, its native size, and runs past the edges of the canvas.
283	
284	A picture the same size as the canvas or smaller starts at 100 % either way, because the option never scales a clip up. See [Fit new clips to canvas](/projects/background-and-timecode/#fit-new-clips-to-canvas).
285	
286	## Picture sections
287	
288	An image clip has three sub-tabs: **Picture**, **Color** and **Clip**. There's no **Sound** sub-tab, because a picture has no sound.
289	
290	The **Picture** sub-tab has these sections, in this order:
291	
292	- [Transform](/canvas/transform/)
293	- [Behind Subject](/effects/text-behind-subject/), on the top-level timeline only, so not while a nest is open
294	- [Hide While Silent](/effects/hide-while-silent/)
295	- [Crop](/canvas/crop/)
296	- [Corner Radius](/canvas/corner-radius/)
297	- [Chroma Key](/effects/chroma-key/)
298	- [Background](/effects/remove-background/), which is Remove Background
299	- [Shadow](/effects/shadow/)
300	- [Filters](/effects/filters/)
301	- [Reflection](/effects/reflection/)
302	- [Spotlight](/effects/spotlight/)
303	- [Obscure](/effects/obscure/)
304	
305	That's everything a video clip has but two. The **Layout** section is for a movie clip and the **Cursor** section for a screen recording, so neither shows here.
306	
307	Remove Background works on a picture too, keeping its person or its foreground subject. A picture gets a **Subject** row to choose between them. See [Remove Background](/effects/remove-background/).
308	
309	The [**Color** sub-tab](/color/color-tab/) grades a picture as it grades a movie, with **Light**, **Color**, **Wheels**, **Curves** and **Look**.
310	
311	The **Clip** sub-tab has **Timing** and **Motion presets**, plus **Transition** when the clip overlaps the one before it. To give a still some movement, use a [motion preset](/motion/motion-presets/) or an [action](/motion/actions/).
312	
313	## Good to know
314	
315	- An animated GIF or WebP shows its first frame only.
316	- A picture with transparency keeps it, so what's behind shows through.
317	- A picture more than 8,192 px on its long side is read at 8,192 px.
318	- Opening a PNG, JPEG or HEIC picture with **File ▸ Open…** builds a new project around it instead of adding it to the one you have open. See [Open a project](/projects/open-a-project/).
319	
320	## With an agent
321	
322	`import_media` adds the picture to the media list and `add_clip` places it, five seconds long at the size above. See [Tools: media](/mcp/tools-media/) and [Tools: adding clips](/mcp/tools-adding-clips/).

331	=================== lines-and-arrows.mdx
332	---
333	title: "Lines and arrows"
334	description: "Aim a line or arrow by dragging its ends on the canvas, and put a head on either end."
335	---
336	
337	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
338	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
339	
340	A line or arrow has two ends you can place by hand. Use them to point at a button, underline a word or connect two things on screen.
341	
342	<AtAGlance
343	  where={['Drag a round end handle on the canvas', 'Clip tab ▸ Shape ▸ Arrowheads']}
344	  tools="set_shape"
345	/>
346	
347	To add one, see [Shape clips](/text-and-shapes/shape-clips/#add-a-shape-clip).
348	
349	## Drag an endpoint
350	
351	<Steps>
352	
353	1. Select the line or arrow, with the playhead over it.
354	
355	2. Drag the round handle at either end.
356	
357	</Steps>
358	
359	Only that end moves. The other end stays where it is, and so does the shape's box. The drag is one undo step, "Move Endpoint". Press <kbd>Esc</kbd> during the drag to put the end back, with no undo step.
360	
361	A new line or arrow runs from the bottom-left corner of its box to the top-right corner. The start is the bottom-left end, and the end is the top-right one.
362	
363	## How the box limits an end
364	
365	An end lives inside the shape's box, so it stops at the box's edge however far you drag. To take an end further, make the box bigger first, with the square handles or with **Width** and **Height** in the [Shape section](/text-and-shapes/shape-settings/#set-the-size).
366	
367	An end is kept as a place in the box, not a place on the canvas. When you resize the box, the line stretches with it and each end keeps its place. Rotating the box with the rotation grip turns the line.
368	
369	The edge is also the easy way to get a level line. Drag both ends past the same edge of the box and they stop exactly in line. Nothing draws outside the box, though, so a line along its edge shows only half its stroke.
370	
371	The square handles and the rotation grip work on a line's box as they do on any shape. See [Resize with the handles](/text-and-shapes/shape-clips/#resize-with-the-handles).
372	
373	:::note
374	When an end sits on a corner of the box, its round handle covers the square one there and takes the click. On a new line that's the bottom-left and top-right corners, so use one of the other two corners or a side handle to resize.
375	:::
376	
377	## Set its arrowheads
378	
379	Tick **Arrowhead at start**, **Arrowhead at end** or both in the **Arrowheads** section of the **Shape** sub-tab. A head shows only when **Kind** is **Arrow**, so a Line keeps its boxes ticked but draws no head. The rows are covered on [Shape fill, stroke and size](/text-and-shapes/shape-settings/#add-arrowheads).
380	
381	A head's tip sits exactly on the end, and the line stops at the head's base. A head's length and its width are each four times the stroke's width, so a 6 px stroke gives a head 24 px long and 24 px wide. It takes the stroke's colour.
382	
383	## Good to know
384	
385	- An end can only be placed on the canvas. There's no field for it in the inspector.
386	- An end doesn't snap to the canvas, its centre or other clips.
387	- An [action](/motion/actions/) can't move an end. With an action selected, dragging an end still changes the clip itself. An action can move, scale, rotate or fade the whole line through [Transform](/canvas/transform/).
388	- With several clips selected, only the front-most selected clip shows handles.
389	- A clip on a [locked track](/timeline/hide-and-lock-tracks/) shows no handles.
390	
391	## With an agent
392	
393	An agent can place both ends exactly and set both heads in one `set_shape` call, with `from`, `to`, `arrow_start` and `arrow_end`. An end is two numbers measured across the box, where `[0, 0]` is the top-left corner and `[1, 1]` the bottom-right, so a new line runs from `[0, 1]` to `[1, 0]`. See [Tools: text, shapes and clip names](/mcp/tools-clip-properties/).
394	
395	## Related

398	- [Shape fill, stroke and size](/text-and-shapes/shape-settings/)
399	- [Move, scale and rotate](/canvas/move-scale-rotate/)
400	=================== shape-clips.mdx
401	---
402	title: "Shape clips"
403	description: "Add a rectangle, ellipse, line or arrow at the playhead, and resize its box on the canvas."
404	---
405	
406	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
407	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
408	import Shot from '@components/Shot.astro';
409	
410	A shape clip draws a rectangle, an ellipse, a line or an arrow over your video. Use one to frame something, point at it, or put a plate behind a title.
411	
412	<AtAGlance
413	  where={['Add Shape in the timeline bar', 'Clip tab ▸ Shape', 'Drag a shape\'s handles on the canvas']}
414	  tools={['add_shape_clip', 'set_shape']}
415	/>
416	
417	<Shot
418	  name="08-clip-shape.window"
419	  alt="The editor with an ellipse shape clip selected. In the preview a white ellipse outline has an orange frame with handles and a rotation handle, the Ellipse clip is outlined in the timeline, and the inspector shows the Shape sub-tab."
420	/>
421	
422	## Add a shape clip
423	
424	<Steps>
425	
426	1. Move the playhead to where the shape should start.
427	
428	2. Click **Add Shape** in the timeline bar.
429	
430	3. Choose **Rectangle**, **Ellipse**, **Line** or **Arrow**.
431	
432	</Steps>
433	
434	**Add Shape** has no menu item and no key. **Clip ▸ Add Background ▸ Solid Color** also makes a shape clip, a white rectangle the canvas's size on a new track at the back. See [Backgrounds](/canvas/backgrounds/).
435	
436	The shape goes on the front-most track if there's room at the playhead, and otherwise on a new track in front of everything. With a [nest](/editing/nests/) open, it goes in the nest. Adding it is one undo step, named after the kind, such as "Add Rectangle".
437	
438	A new shape:
439	
440	- lasts 5 seconds, and has no source file, so you can [trim](/editing/trimming/) it to any length
441	- is a 320 × 120 px box with a 6 px white stroke and no fill, so it shows up over any footage
442	- is selected, so the **Shape** sub-tab opens on it
443	
444	Everything about how it's drawn is on [Shape fill, stroke and size](/text-and-shapes/shape-settings/).
445	
446	## The four kinds
447	
448	You can change a shape's kind at any time with [**Kind**](/text-and-shapes/shape-settings/#change-the-kind).
449	
450	### Rectangle
451	
452	A rectangle that fills its box. A rounded rectangle is a Rectangle with a [corner radius](/text-and-shapes/shape-settings/#round-a-rectangles-corners), not a separate kind.
453	
454	### Ellipse
455	
456	An ellipse that fills its box. Make the box square for a circle.
457	
458	### Line
459	
460	A straight line. A new line runs diagonally across its box, from bottom left to top right. Drag the round handle at either end to move that end. See [Lines and arrows](/text-and-shapes/lines-and-arrows/).
461	
462	### Arrow
463	
464	A line with an arrowhead. A new arrow runs diagonally across its box like a line, with its head at the end turned on.
465	
466	## Resize with the handles
467	
468	Dragging a shape's handle changes the size of its box, not a scale factor, so the stroke stays the same thickness. The box's new size shows in the **Width** and **Height** fields.
469	
470	| Gesture | What it does |
471	| --- | --- |
472	| Drag a corner handle | Resizes the box and keeps its aspect ratio. |
473	| <kbd>⇧</kbd>-drag a corner handle | Frees the aspect ratio, so width and height move independently. |
474	| Drag a side handle | Changes only the width or only the height. |
475	| <kbd>⌥</kbd>-drag a handle | Resizes about the centre rather than pinning the opposite handle. |
476	
477	The drag holds each side of the box between 4 and 20,000 px.
478	
479	<kbd>⇧</kbd> is special to shapes here. A video or picture has one uniform scale, so <kbd>⇧</kbd> changes nothing on those. For the rest of the canvas gestures, see [Move, scale and rotate](/canvas/move-scale-rotate/).
480	
481	A box resize always changes the clip itself, even with an [action](/motion/actions/) selected. To animate a shape's size, use **Scale** in the [Transform](/canvas/transform/) section, which enlarges the whole drawing, stroke included.
482	
483	## Picture sections
484	
485	A shape clip has three sub-tabs: **Shape**, **Picture** and **Clip**. Its **Picture** sub-tab has these sections, in this order:
486	
487	- [Transform](/canvas/transform/)
488	- [Behind Subject](/effects/text-behind-subject/), on the top-level timeline only, so not while a nest is open
489	- [Hide While Silent](/effects/hide-while-silent/)
490	- [Shadow](/effects/shadow/)
491	- [Filters](/effects/filters/)
492	- [Reflection](/effects/reflection/)
493	- [Spotlight](/effects/spotlight/)
494	- [Obscure](/effects/obscure/)
495	
496	Crop, Corner Radius, Chroma Key and Background aren't offered, and neither is the **Color** sub-tab. To round a shape's corners, use **Corner radius** on the **Shape** sub-tab.
497	
498	## With an agent
499	
500	`add_shape_clip` puts a shape on the track and at the time you name, and can give it its length and look in the same step. It can also make a shape larger than the canvas, which starts scaled to fit when [**Fit new clips to canvas**](/projects/background-and-timecode/#fit-new-clips-to-canvas) is on. An arrow starts with its head on, so pass `arrow_end: false` for a bare diagonal. See [Tools: adding clips](/mcp/tools-adding-clips/#add_shape_clip).
501	
502	## Related

505	- [Lines and arrows](/text-and-shapes/lines-and-arrows/)
506	- [Gradient fills](/text-and-shapes/gradients/)
