509	=================== shape-settings.mdx
510	---
511	title: "Shape fill, stroke and size"
512	description: "Change a shape's kind and box, round its corners, set its stroke and fill, and add arrowheads on the Shape sub-tab."
513	---
514	
515	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
516	import Shot from '@components/Shot.astro';
517	
518	The **Shape** sub-tab sets what a [shape clip](/text-and-shapes/shape-clips/) is and how it's painted. Where it sits, how large it's scaled and how see-through it is as a whole are on the **Picture** sub-tab, in [Transform](/canvas/transform/).
519	
520	<AtAGlance where="Clip tab ▸ Shape" tools="set_shape" />
521	
522	<Shot
523	  name="08-clip-shape.inspector"
524	  alt="The Shape sub-tab for an ellipse. The Shape section is open with Kind set to Ellipse, Width 320 px, Height 120 px and a dimmed Corner radius at 0 px. Below it the closed sections read Stroke 6.0 px, Fill off, Gradient off and Arrowheads none."
525	/>
526	
527	## Change the kind
528	
529	**Kind** switches the shape between **Rectangle**, **Ellipse**, **Line** and **Arrow**. It changes only the kind, so everything else stays as it was.
530	
531	Rows that don't apply to the new kind are greyed, not lost, so flipping the kind back finds them as you left them.
532	
533	| Row | Available for |
534	| --- | --- |
535	| **Corner radius** | Rectangle |
536	| The **Gradient** section | Rectangle, Ellipse |
537	| The **Arrowheads** section | Line, Arrow |
538	
539	A shape switched to **Arrow** keeps its own arrowhead setting, so a rectangle switched to Arrow has no head until you tick one. Only a shape added as an Arrow starts with a head.
540	
541	## Set the size
542	
543	**Width** and **Height** set the shape's box in pixels, from 1 to 20,000 px each. A new shape is 320 × 120 px. A number typed outside the range is brought back to the nearest limit. However large the box is, a shape is drawn at no more than 8,192 px on a side.
544	
545	[Dragging a handle](/text-and-shapes/shape-clips/#resize-with-the-handles) on the canvas changes the same two numbers. **Scale** in [Transform](/canvas/transform/) is different: it enlarges the finished drawing, stroke included.
546	
547	## Round a rectangle's corners
548	
549	**Corner radius** rounds a rectangle's corners, from 0 to 2,000 px, with quick picks at 0, 4, 8, 16, 32 and 64. The default is 0. It's greyed for other kinds.
550	
551	A radius can't go past half the box's shorter side. At that point the short ends are fully round, and a larger number looks the same.
552	
553	The **Shape** section's **Reset** puts the corner radius back to 0, and leaves the kind and the box alone.
554	
555	## Draw an outline
556	
557	The **Stroke** section draws an outline around the shape. A new shape has one.
558	
559	| Control | What it does | Default | Range |
560	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
561	| **Stroke** | Turns the outline on or off. | On | |
562	| **Width** | How thick it is. Quick picks 1, 2, 4, 6, 12 and 24. | 6 px | 0.5 to 200 px |
563	| **Color** | Its colour. | White | |
564	
565	**Width** and **Color** are greyed while the stroke is off. Turning the stroke off forgets its width and colour, so turning it on again gives 6 px white. **Reset** also goes back to 6 px white rather than turning the stroke off.
566	
567	On a rectangle or ellipse the stroke sits inside the box, so a thicker stroke doesn't make the shape bigger.
568	
569	When the section is folded, its header reads the width, such as "6.0 px", or "off".
570	
571	## Fill the shape
572	
573	The **Fill** section paints the inside of a rectangle or ellipse with a flat colour. A new shape has no fill.
574	
575	| Control | What it does | Default | Range |
576	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
577	| **Fill** | Turns the fill on or off. | Off | |
578	| **Color** | The fill's colour. | White, once turned on | |
579	| **Opacity** | How solid the fill is. Quick picks 0, 25, 50, 75 and 100. | 100 % | 0 to 100 % |
580	
581	**Color** and **Opacity** are greyed while the fill is off. Turning the fill off forgets its colour, so turning it on again gives opaque white. **Reset** turns the fill off.
582	
583	**Opacity** belongs to the fill alone, so it doesn't fade the stroke. To fade the whole shape, use **Opacity** in [Transform](/canvas/transform/).
584	
585	When the section is folded, its header reads the fill's opacity, such as "100%", or "off".
586	
587	For a colour ramp in place of a flat colour, see [Gradient fills](/text-and-shapes/gradients/). A gradient covers the fill while it's on, and turning it off brings the fill back.
588	
589	## Add arrowheads
590	
591	The **Arrowheads** section has two separate boxes, **Arrowhead at start** and **Arrowhead at end**. They're available for lines and arrows, and greyed for rectangles and ellipses.
592	
593	:::note
594	Arrowheads are drawn only when **Kind** is **Arrow**. On a Line you can tick the boxes and they're kept, but no head appears until you switch the kind to Arrow.
595	:::
596	
597	When the section is folded, its header reads "both", "start", "end" or "none". See [Lines and arrows](/text-and-shapes/lines-and-arrows/) for moving the ends.
598	
599	A line or arrow is drawn with its stroke, so a Line with **Stroke** off shows nothing. **Fill** paints nothing on a line or arrow, although its rows stay available. The one exception is an Arrow with **Stroke** off, whose heads take the fill colour.
600	
601	## Why shape colours don't animate
602	
603	An [action](/motion/actions/) can't change a shape's kind, stroke, fill, gradient or arrowheads. These rows always change the clip itself, even while an action is selected, and they're marked ⊘ to show it.
604	
605	A shape's position, scale and opacity animate like any clip's. To move or fade a shape, select an action and use the [Transform](/canvas/transform/) rows on the **Picture** sub-tab. See [What an action can animate](/motion/what-can-animate/).
606	
607	## With an agent
608	
609	`set_shape` changes any of these settings in one call and leaves the rest as they are, including a line's two ends. Setting `stroke` or `fill` to `null` removes it. A shape's position and scale aren't part of it: those go through `set_video`. To change a shape inside a nest, see [Editing inside a nest](/mcp/nests/). For every key, see [Tools: text, shapes and clip names](/mcp/tools-clip-properties/#set_shape).
610	
611	## Related

614	- [Lines and arrows](/text-and-shapes/lines-and-arrows/)
615	- [Gradient fills](/text-and-shapes/gradients/)

617	=================== text-box.mdx
618	---
619	title: "Text box and wrapping"
620	description: "Let a text clip's box fit its words, or set a width and have the words wrap, from the inspector or by dragging on the canvas."
621	---
622	
623	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
624	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
625	
626	A text clip's box decides where its lines break. By default the box fits the words, and only your own line breaks start a new line. Give it a fixed width and the words wrap to fit.
627	
628	<AtAGlance
629	  where={['Clip tab ▸ Text ▸ Box', 'Drag a text clip\'s left or right handle on the canvas']}
630	  tools="set_text"
631	/>
632	
633	## Wrap text at a width
634	
635	<Steps>
636	
637	1. Select the text clip.
638	
639	2. In the inspector's **Clip** tab, open the **Box** section of the **Text** sub-tab.
640	
641	3. Set **Mode** to **Fixed width**. The width starts at 60 % of the canvas width, which is 1,152 px on a 1920-wide canvas.
642	
643	4. Type a **Width**, or drag a [side handle](#drag-the-width-on-the-canvas) on the canvas.
644	
645	</Steps>
646	
647	To go back, set **Mode** to **Auto-size** or choose the section's **Reset**.
648	
649	## The Box section
650	
651	| Control | What it does | Default | Range |
652	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
653	| **Mode** | **Auto-size** lays the text out without wrapping, so the box fits the words. **Fixed width** wraps the words at **Width**. | Auto-size | |
654	| **Width** | The width the words wrap at. It's greyed in Auto-size. | 60 % of the canvas width | 20 to 20,000 px |
655	
656	A number typed outside the range is brought back to the nearest limit. When the section is folded, its header reads "auto", or the width, such as "1152 px".
657	
658	## Drag the width on the canvas
659	
660	Drag a text clip's left or right handle in the preview to set its wrap width. If the box was on Auto-size, it becomes **Fixed width**, starting from the box's current width.
661	
662	The text stays centred on the same point and grows both ways, whichever handle you drag. The drag holds the width between 4 and 20,000 px, so it can go narrower than the 20 px the **Width** field lets you type.
663	
664	The other handles do something different. The corners and the top and bottom handles scale the text uniformly and leave the wrap width alone. See [Move, scale and rotate](/canvas/move-scale-rotate/).
665	
666	## What a fixed width changes
667	
668	- **The height follows the lines.** A fixed width sets only the width, and the box grows taller as the text wraps onto more lines.
669	- **Alignment works across the whole width.** Left, centre and right [alignment](/text-and-shapes/text-style/) line the words up against the width you set, not against the longest line.
670	- **A backdrop fills the whole box.** A [backdrop](/text-and-shapes/text-outline-and-backdrop/) is as wide as **Width** plus its padding, even when the words are shorter. **Width** measures the words, and the padding sits outside it.
671	
672	## Good to know
673	
674	- In Auto-size a long line never wraps, so it can run off the canvas. Press <kbd>⇧Return</kbd> in the [text area](/text-and-shapes/text-clips/) to start a new line yourself.
675	- Text is drawn at no more than 8,192 px on a side, so a box stops growing there whatever **Width** says.
676	- With an [action](/motion/edit-an-action/) selected, **Mode**, **Width** and the side handles set the action's end, like any other text property.
677	
678	## With an agent
679	
680	`set_text` sets the box through `width`: a wrap width in pixels, or `null` to go back to Auto-size. See [Tools: text, shapes and clip names](/mcp/tools-clip-properties/#set_text).
681	
682	## Related

684	- [Text clips](/text-and-shapes/text-clips/)

689	---
690	title: Text clips
691	description: Add a title to the timeline, type its words, and see what else a text clip can do.
692	---
693	
694	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
695	import Shot from '@components/Shot.astro';
696	
697	A text clip puts words on the canvas: a title, a name strap, a line of explanation. It sits on a track like any other clip, and it has no source file behind it.
698	
699	<AtAGlance
700	  keys="T"
701	  where={['The Add Text button in the timeline bar', 'Clip tab ▸ Text ▸ Content']}
702	  tools={['add_text_clip', 'set_text']}
703	/>
704	
705	<Shot
706	  name="06-clip-text.window"
707	  alt="A title reading Frame Job selected in the preview, with an orange frame and handles around it. Its clip is outlined in the timeline, and the inspector's Clip tab is open on the Text sub-tab."
708	/>
709	
710	## Add a text clip
711	
712	Press <kbd>T</kbd>, or click **Add Text** in the timeline bar, the **Aa** button. There's no menu item for it.
713	
714	The new clip reads "Title" in Source Sans 3 Bold at 72 px, in white, centred on the canvas, and it lasts 5 seconds. For a look sized to your canvas, use a [preset](/text-and-shapes/text-presets/).
715	
716	It lands at the playhead on the front-most track if it fits there, and on a new track in front of everything if it doesn't. Either way it's one undo step, **Add Text**. With a [nest](/editing/nests/) open, the front-most track is the nest's own.
717	
718	The clip comes in selected, so the canvas shows its handles and the **Clip** tab opens on its **Text** sub-tab. If the inspector is showing **Transcript** or **Assistant**, it stays there.
719	
720	## Change the length
721	
722	Five seconds is only where a text clip starts. With no source file to run out of, you can [trim](/editing/trimming/) it to any length.
723	
724	## Write the words
725	
726	There are two places to type:
727	
728	- **On the canvas.** Double-click the clip in the preview. See [Edit text on the canvas](/text-and-shapes/edit-text-on-canvas/).
729	- **In the inspector.** Select the clip and use the **Content** section at the top of the **Text** sub-tab. It's the one Text section that starts open. Its header shows the first line of the text, or "empty".
730	
731	In the **Content** box:
732	
733	| Key | What it does |
734	| --- | --- |
735	| <kbd>Return</kbd> | Applies the text, and the single-letter shortcuts work again |
736	| <kbd>Tab</kbd> | Applies the text the same way, unless Full Keyboard Access is on in System Settings |
737	| <kbd>⇧Return</kbd>, <kbd>⌘Return</kbd>, <kbd>⌥Return</kbd> or <kbd>⌃Return</kbd> | Starts a new line |
738	
739	A click elsewhere in the window, below its title bar, applies the text too. Changing the words is one undo step, **Edit Text**. If they haven't changed, there's no undo step.
740	
741	With an [action](/motion/actions/) selected, **Content** sets the words at that action's end. Words don't ease from one to another, so the text switches when the action ends.
742	
743	## Style the clip
744	
745	The **Text** sub-tab has the rest of a clip's look, and each section has its own page:
746	
747	| Section | Page |
748	| --- | --- |
749	| **Font** and **Style** | [Font and text style](/text-and-shapes/text-style/) |
750	| **Outline** and **Backdrop** | [Text outline and backdrop](/text-and-shapes/text-outline-and-backdrop/) |
751	| **Box** | [Text box and wrapping](/text-and-shapes/text-box/) |
752	| **Reveal** | [Text reveals](/text-and-shapes/text-reveal/) |
753	| **Presets** | [Text presets](/text-and-shapes/text-presets/) |
754	
755	The sub-tab shows only when every selected clip is a text clip. With several selected, a change goes to all of them.
756	
757	## Place it and add effects
758	
759	A text clip also has a **Picture** sub-tab, with these sections in this order:
760	
761	- [Transform](/canvas/transform/), for position, scale, rotation and opacity
762	- [Behind Subject](/effects/text-behind-subject/), which isn't shown while a nest is open
763	- [Hide While Silent](/effects/hide-while-silent/)
764	- [Shadow](/effects/shadow/)
765	- [Filters](/effects/filters/)
766	- [Reflection](/effects/reflection/)
767	- [Spotlight](/effects/spotlight/)
768	- [Obscure](/effects/obscure/)
769	
770	Crop, Corner Radius, Chroma Key and Background aren't offered, because they work on a clip's source pixels. A text clip has no **Color** or **Sound** sub-tab.
771	
772	## With an agent
773	
774	`add_text_clip` needs a track and a time. It can also set the length, 5 seconds if left out, and the words and the whole look in the same call. Unlike <kbd>T</kbd>, it doesn't fall back to a new track: if the clip would overlap another, Frame Job won't add it.
775	
776	`set_text` changes any mix of a clip's words and typography in one undo step. An agent isn't held to the ranges of the inspector's fields, so a size above 800 px is fine, for example. Position and scale go through `set_video`. Word timings sent for a caption must match its number of words, or the call fails and gives both numbers. See [Tools: adding clips](/mcp/tools-adding-clips/) and [Tools: text, shapes and clip names](/mcp/tools-clip-properties/).
777	
778	## Good to know
779	
780	A caption is a text clip too. If one is timed word by word, editing it keeps the timings while the number of words stays the same. Change the number of words and it loses its timing, so its words no longer change as they're spoken, and **Content** notes "Not timed — regenerate to time it again". See [Captions are text clips](/captions/how-captions-work/) and [Edit captions](/captions/edit-captions/).

788	=================== text-outline-and-backdrop.mdx
789	---
790	title: Text outline and backdrop
791	description: Draw a stroke around a text clip's letters, or put a rounded plate behind them, so the words stay readable over any picture.
792	---
793	
794	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
795	
796	White words get lost over a bright shot. An outline draws a stroke around each letter, and a backdrop puts a rounded plate behind the whole text. You can use either or both.
797	
798	<AtAGlance
799	  where={['Clip tab ▸ Text ▸ Outline', 'Clip tab ▸ Text ▸ Backdrop']}
800	  tools="set_text"
801	/>
802	
803	## Add an outline
804	
805	Select a text clip, click the **Outline** header in the **Text** sub-tab to open the section, and tick **Outline**. You get a 2 px black stroke.
806	
807	| Control | What it does | Default | Range |
808	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
809	| **Width** | The stroke's thickness. Quick picks: 1, 2, 4 and 8. | 2 px | 0 to 40 px |
810	| **Color** | The stroke's colour | Black | |
811	
812	Both are greyed while the outline is off. The section's header shows the width, or "off".
813	
814	The stroke sits on the edge of each letter, half inside and half outside, so a wide outline thins the letters.
815	
816	**Reset** in the section's header turns the outline off.
817	
818	## Add a backdrop
819	
820	Click the **Backdrop** header to open the section, and tick **Backdrop**. You get a black plate at 60 % opacity.
821	
822	| Control | What it does | Default | Range |
823	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
824	| **Fill** | The plate's colour and opacity | Black at 60 % | |
825	| **Padding** | The space between the text and the plate's edge. Quick picks: 0, 8, 12, 24 and 48. | 12 px | 0 to 200 px |
826	| **Radius** | How round the corners are. Quick picks: 0, 4, 8, 16 and 32. | 8 px | 0 to 200 px |
827	
828	All three are greyed while the backdrop is off. The section's header shows the padding, or "off".
829	
830	A radius can't go past half the plate's shorter side, so a large radius makes a pill shape and goes no further.
831	
832	**Reset** in the section's header turns the backdrop off.
833	
834	## Change them during a clip
835	
836	With an [action](/motion/actions/) selected, these controls set the look at that action's end. **Width**, **Padding**, **Radius** and the colours ease towards the new value, and colours [blend in OKLab](/motion/what-can-animate/#colours-blend-in-oklab). Turning an outline or a backdrop on or off switches when the action ends.
837	
838	## With an agent
839	
840	`set_text` sets both. `outline` takes `width` and `color`, and `backdrop` takes `color`, `padding` and `radius`. Send `null` for either to turn it off. An agent isn't held to the ranges above: a width, padding or radius only has to be 0 or more. See [Tools: text, shapes and clip names](/mcp/tools-clip-properties/).
841	
842	## Good to know
843	
844	- Turning an outline or a backdrop off forgets its settings. Turn it on again and it's back to the defaults.
845	- Both make the clip's box bigger. The margin around the words is whichever is larger, the outline's width or the backdrop's padding, not the two added together. The plate fills that whole box.
846	- During a [reveal](/text-and-shapes/text-reveal/), the backdrop is there at full strength from the first frame, and the words arrive on it. An outline comes and goes with its letters.
847

853	=================== text-presets.mdx
854	---
855	title: Text presets
856	description: Give a text clip a ready-made Title, Subtitle, Lower Third or Caption look, sized to your canvas.
857	---
858	
859	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
860	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
861	
862	A preset gives a text clip a finished look with one click: its font, size, alignment, backdrop and position, sized to fit your canvas.
863	
864	<AtAGlance
865	  where="Clip tab ▸ Text ▸ Presets"
866	  tools={['set_text', 'set_video']}
867	/>
868	
869	## Apply a preset
870	
871	<Steps>
872	
873	1. Select one or more text clips.
874	
875	2. Open the **Presets** section at the bottom of the **Text** sub-tab. It starts folded.
876	
877	3. Click **Title**, **Subtitle**, **Lower Third** or **Caption**.
878	
879	</Steps>
880	
881	It's one undo step, named after the preset.
882	
883	## The four presets
884	
885	| Preset | Font | Size | At 1920 × 1080 | Align | Position | Backdrop |
886	| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
887	| **Title** | Source Sans 3 Bold | 9 % | 97 px | Centre | Centre of the canvas | None |
888	| **Subtitle** | Source Sans 3 SemiBold | 5 % | 54 px | Centre | 18 % of the height below centre | None |
889	| **Lower Third** | Source Sans 3 SemiBold | 4.5 % | 49 px | Left | 20 % of the width left of centre, 28 % of the height below it | Black at 55 %, padding 18 px, radius 6 px |
890	| **Caption** | Source Sans 3 Regular | 3.5 % | 38 px | Centre | 38 % of the height below centre | Black at 60 %, padding 12 px, radius 8 px |
891	
892	The position is where the centre of the text's box sits, so a longer name on a **Lower Third** grows both ways from that point.
893	
894	**Title** isn't the look a new text clip starts with. That has the same font at a fixed 72 px, where **Title** works its size out from the canvas.
895	
896	On a canvas taller than wide, **Caption** sits higher, a quarter of the height below centre, clear of a phone's on-screen controls.
897	
898	[Subtitles](/captions/subtitles/) from **File ▸ Generate Captions…** and **File ▸ Import Captions…** use the **Caption** look, and they also wrap at 80 % of the canvas width. The **Caption** button itself leaves the [box](/text-and-shapes/text-box/) as it is.
899	
900	## How a preset fits the canvas
901	
902	Sizes are a share of the canvas's shorter side, and positions a share of its width and height. So a preset fits any canvas, and a vertical 1080 × 1920 canvas gets the same text height as a 1920 × 1080 one. A backdrop's padding and radius stay at the pixel values in the table.
903	
904	The size is worked out once, from the canvas at the moment you click. Changing the canvas afterwards doesn't apply the preset again.
905	
906	## What a preset changes
907	
908	As well as the settings in the table, a preset sets **Vertical** to middle and **Opacity** back to 100 %. **Title** and **Subtitle** take away any backdrop.
909	
910	It leaves everything else alone, including the words, the colour, the outline, tracking, line spacing, **UPPERCASE**, the box, the reveal, scale and rotation.
911	
912	With an [action](/motion/actions/) selected, a preset sets that action's end, like any other field.
913	
914	## With an agent
915	
916	There's no preset tool. An agent sends the same values through `set_text` and `set_video`. See [Tools: text, shapes and clip names](/mcp/tools-clip-properties/).
917

923	=================== text-reveal.mdx
924	---
925	title: "Text reveals"
926	description: "Make a text clip type on, fade in word by word or rise in line by line, and set how long it takes to arrive and leave."
927	---
928	
929	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
930	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
931	
932	A reveal decides how a text clip's words arrive and leave. It runs from the clip's own first and last frames, so it needs no [action](/motion/actions/) and it moves with the clip.
933	
934	<AtAGlance where="Clip tab ▸ Text ▸ Reveal" tools="set_text" />
935	
936	## Add a reveal
937	
938	<Steps>
939	
940	1. Select the text clip.
941	
942	2. In the inspector's **Clip** tab, open the **Reveal** section of the **Text** sub-tab.
943	
944	3. Choose **Typewriter**, **Word Fade** or **Line Rise** from the **Reveal** pop-up.
945	
946	4. Set [**In** and **Out**](#set-how-long-it-takes) if you want something other than one second in and no exit.
947	
948	</Steps>
949	
950	Switching from one reveal to another keeps the times you set. Choosing **None**, or the section's **Reset**, turns the reveal off and forgets them, so the next reveal starts at 1 s in and 0 s out.
951	
952	When the section is folded, its header reads "off", or the reveal and its **In** time, such as "typewriter · 1.00 s".
953	
954	The preview, a rendered frame and an export all work out each frame the same way, so what you see while scrubbing is what you'll export.
955	
956	## The three reveals
957	
958	### Typewriter
959	
960	The text types on, one character at a time. Spaces and line breaks count as characters, so the typing pauses at them. On the way out it backspaces, and the end of the text goes first.
961	
962	### Word Fade
963	
964	The words fade in one after another. Each word's fade overlaps the next by half, so it reads as a wave across the text rather than one word at a time. On the way out they leave in the same order, so the first word in is the first word out.
965	
966	### Line Rise
967	
968	Each line fades in as it rises into place, starting 35 % of its own height below where it ends up. The top line goes first and the others follow. On the way out each line sinks and fades, again from the top.
969	
970	A line on its way up is cut off at the edge of the text box. Over a [backdrop](/text-and-shapes/text-outline-and-backdrop/) that looks like a mask, and without one the line appears to slide out of nothing.
971	
972	Lines are what the box makes them. In [Auto-size](/text-and-shapes/text-box/) only your own line breaks start a new line, so a single line of text rises all at once.
973	
974	## Set how long it takes
975	
976	| Control | What it does | Default | Range | Quick picks |
977	| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
978	| **In** | How long the arrival takes, from the clip's first frame. | 1 s | 0 to 10 s | 0, 0.25, 0.5, 1, 2 |
979	| **Out** | How long the departure takes, counted back from the clip's last frame. | 0 s | 0 to 10 s | 0, 0.25, 0.5, 1, 2 |
980	
981	- A time of 0 means that end of the reveal doesn't happen. With **In** at 0 the text is whole on the first frame, and with **Out** at 0 it stays whole to the last.
982	- Both times snap to whole frames.
983	- Both rows are greyed while **Reveal** is **None**.
984	- If **In** and **Out** add up to more than the clip's length, the two overlap. The text never shows in full, and a short clip gets a partial reveal.
985	
986	A reveal has no easing control, because the motion is part of the reveal you choose.
987	
988	## Word styles take over
989	
990	On a caption page with a [word style](/captions/word-caption-styles/), the word style decides how the words appear. The **Reveal** section is greyed and notes "Word style wins; the reveal does not apply." The page is drawn without any reveal.
991	
992	## Good to know
993	
994	- **Backdrop and outline.** A backdrop stays at full strength for the whole clip, so the words type or fade onto it. An outline arrives and leaves with its letters.
995	- **Trimming.** **In** and **Out** are measured from the clip's edges, so a trim moves the reveal with the new edge and keeps its length.
996	- **Splitting.** After a [split](/editing/splitting/), the first piece keeps the arrival and loses the departure, and the second keeps the departure and loses the arrival. A piece left with neither has its reveal turned off.
997	- **Transitions.** A reveal starts on the clip's first frame, so a [transition](/motion/transitions/) into a text clip plays over the start of the reveal.
998	- **Nests.** Inside a [nest](/editing/nests/), the text clip's own edges count, not the nest clip's. If the nest clip's edge falls part way through a reveal, the reveal is cut off there.
999	- **Actions.** With an [action](/motion/edit-an-action/) selected, these rows set the action's end. A change of reveal switches at the action's end rather than blending. **In** and **Out** ramp like any number, which shifts the reveal's own timing while it plays, so it's usually better to set them on the clip.
1000	- **Right-to-left text.** Typewriter can show the wrong part of a line when the text is right-to-left or mixes directions.
1001	
1002	## With an agent
1003	
1004	`set_text` sets a reveal through `animation`: `null` turns it off, and `{kind, in, out}` sets it, with a `kind` of `typewriter`, `word_fade` or `line_rise`. On a page with a `word_style`, the word style is what's drawn and `animation` has no effect. See [Tools: text, shapes and clip names](/mcp/tools-clip-properties/#set_text).
1005

1012	=================== text-style.mdx
1013	---
1014	title: Font and text style
1015	description: Choose a text clip's font and size, then set its colour, alignment, capitals, line spacing and letter spacing.
1016	---
1017	
1018	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
1019	
1020	The **Font** and **Style** sections of the **Text** sub-tab set how a text clip's words look. Select a text clip to reach them. Both start folded, so click a header to open its section. The **Font** header shows the size and the **Style** header shows the alignment.
1021	
1022	<AtAGlance
1023	  where={['Clip tab ▸ Text ▸ Font', 'Clip tab ▸ Text ▸ Style']}
1024	  tools="set_text"
1025	/>
1026	
1027	## Choose a font
1028	
1029	**Family** lists every font family installed on your Mac, plus the ones Frame Job ships with: Source Sans 3, Source Serif 4, Montserrat, Anton, Bebas Neue, Darker Grotesque and IBM Plex Mono.
1030	
1031	**Style** lists the faces of that family, such as Regular or SemiBold.
1032	
1033	When you change **Family**, Frame Job keeps the current style if the new family has one of that name. Otherwise it uses Regular, or the family's first style if it has no Regular. Both controls make an undo step called **Font**.
1034	
1035	See [Fonts](/text-and-shapes/fonts/) for more on the faces.
1036	
1037	## Set the size
1038	
1039	**Size** runs from 6 to 800 px, and a new clip starts at 72 px. Type a value or use the quick picks: 24, 36, 48, 72, 96 and 144.
1040	
1041	The size is in canvas pixels, so the same number looks smaller on a larger canvas. For a size worked out from the canvas, use a [preset](/text-and-shapes/text-presets/).
1042	
1043	## Set the colour
1044	
1045	**Color** is white by default. Click its swatch to open the colour panel, and set the colour and its opacity there.
1046	
1047	## Align the text
1048	
1049	| Control | Choices | Default |
1050	| --- | --- | --- |
1051	| **Align** | **L**, **C** or **R** | Centre |
1052	| **Vertical** | Top, middle or bottom of the box | Middle |
1053	
1054	Both make an undo step called **Alignment**.
1055	
1056	With the box on **Auto-size**, the box is as wide as the longest line, so **Align** lines up the shorter lines and a single line doesn't move. In a [fixed-width box](/text-and-shapes/text-box/), it places every line in the box. To move the text itself, drag it on the canvas or use [Transform](/canvas/transform/).
1057	
1058	A text box is always as tall as its words, so **Vertical** moves the text by a pixel or two at most.
1059	
1060	## Show the text in capitals
1061	
1062	Tick **UPPERCASE** to draw the text in capitals. What you typed is kept as you typed it, so unticking the box brings it back. It never changes the number of words, so it's safe on captions timed word by word.
1063	
1064	The [canvas text editor](/text-and-shapes/edit-text-on-canvas/) shows the text as you typed it, not in capitals.
1065	
1066	## Adjust the spacing
1067	
1068	| Control | What it does | Default | Range |
1069	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
1070	| **Line spacing** | The space between lines, as a multiple of the font's line height | 1× | 0.5 to 4× |
1071	| **Tracking** | Extra space between letters. Below 0 pulls them together. | 0 px | −20 to 100 px |
1072	
1073	## Reset the style
1074	
1075	**Reset** in the **Style** section's header puts everything in that section back, in one undo step called **Text Style**:
1076	
1077	- **Color** to white
1078	- **Align** to centre and **Vertical** to middle
1079	- **UPPERCASE** off
1080	- **Line spacing** to 1× and **Tracking** to 0 px
1081	
1082	It shows while something in the section differs from those values and no action is selected. It doesn't touch the font or the size, and the **Font** section has no **Reset** of its own. To put **Size** back to 72 px, right-click its label and choose **Reset to default**.
1083	
1084	## Change the style during a clip
1085	
1086	With an [action](/motion/actions/) selected, these controls set the look at that action's end. **Size**, **Color**, **Line spacing** and **Tracking** ease towards the new value, and colours [blend in OKLab](/motion/what-can-animate/#colours-blend-in-oklab). **Family**, **Style**, **Align**, **Vertical** and **UPPERCASE** switch when the action ends.
1087	
1088	## With an agent
1089	
1090	An agent names a font by its one PostScript name, such as `SourceSans3-Bold`, rather than by family and style. A colour is four numbers from 0 to 1: red, green, blue and opacity. **Align** is `align` (`left`, `center` or `right`), **Vertical** is `valign` (`top`, `middle` or `bottom`), and **UPPERCASE** is `case` (`as_written` or `upper`).
1091	
1092	An agent isn't held to the ranges above: a size or line spacing only has to be above 0, and tracking can be any number. See [Tools: text, shapes and clip names](/mcp/tools-clip-properties/).
1093	
1094	## Good to know
1095	
1096	A project can name a font this Mac doesn't have. The **Text** sub-tab still opens, showing the first family in the list, and the text draws in a substitute until you install the font or choose another.
1097

1	=================== chroma-key.mdx
2	---
3	title: Chroma Key
4	description: Remove a background colour, such as a green screen, so whatever is on the tracks behind shows through.
5	---
6	
7	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
8	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
9	
10	Chroma Key removes one colour from a clip, such as a green screen, so whatever is on the tracks behind shows through.
11	
12	<AtAGlance
13	  where="Clip tab ▸ Picture ▸ Chroma Key"
14	  tools="set_video"
15	/>
16	
17	## Key out a color
18	
19	<Steps>
20	
21	1. Put the clip on a track in front of what should show through, and select it.
22	
23	2. In the Clip tab's **Picture** sub-tab, open the **Chroma Key** section. It comes after **Corner Radius** and is shut by default.
24	
25	3. Choose **Pick from Canvas** and click the background in the preview. That sets the colour and turns the key on. Or tick **Key out a color**, which keys pure green.
26	
27	4. Adjust [**Tolerance**](#tolerance), [**Softness**](#softness) and [**Spill**](#spill) until the edges look right.
28	
29	</Steps>
30	
31	Turning the key on gives pure green at 20 % Tolerance, 10 % Softness and 50 % Spill. **Key Color**, **Tolerance**, **Softness** and **Spill** stay dimmed until the key is on. **Pick from Canvas** doesn't. The section's header reads "off", or the Tolerance as a percentage. **Reset** takes the key off the clip.
32	
33	The section is there for clips of a video file, image clips and freeze frames. Text, shape, graphic, adjustment and nest clips don't have it. With several clips selected, an edit keys all of them.
34	
35	## Key color
36	
37	The colour to remove. It starts as pure green, and the swatch takes any colour. The opacity in the colour panel has no effect here, because a key colour has none.
38	
39	## Pick from Canvas
40	
41	Choose **Pick from Canvas** and the preview reads "Click to pick the key color · Esc to cancel". One click on the picture sets **Key Color**. The button works with the key off, and a pick turns it on.
42	
43	A pick reads the clip as the key sees it, without the clip's own key, grade and opacity. So picking again reads the same green the first pick did, even though that green is now a hole. A clip in front of it at that point still covers it, and you get what's visible there.
44	
45	Picking again changes only the colour. It keeps the **Tolerance**, **Softness** and **Spill** you set.
46	
47	To cancel, press the button again, press <kbd>⎋</kbd> or change the selection.
48	
49	| If | What happens |
50	| --- | --- |
51	| You click outside the picture | Frame Job beeps and stays ready for another click |
52	| You click where the canvas holds nothing | Frame Job beeps and changes nothing |
53	| The selection changes while the frame is being read | Frame Job beeps and changes nothing |
54	
55	Only one canvas tool is ready at a time. **Pick from Canvas** ends [Obscure](/effects/obscure/)'s **Place on Canvas**, [Zoom to Region](/motion/zoom-to-region/) and the [qualifier's Pick from Canvas](/color/pick-from-canvas/).
56	
57	## Tune the key
58	
59	Start with **Tolerance** to clear the background, then **Softness** for the edge, then **Spill** for any fringe of the key colour.
60	
61	### Tolerance
62	
63	How far from the key colour still counts as background. Everything that close is removed completely. Raise it if patches of background remain, and lower it if the key eats into your subject.
64	
65	The range is 0 to 100 %, and the default is 20 %. The quick picks are 0, 10, 20, 40 and 60.
66	
67	### Softness
68	
69	How gradual the edge of the key is. Past **Tolerance**, the picture fades back in over this distance, so a low value gives a hard edge.
70	
71	The range is 0 to 100 %, and the default is 10 %. The quick picks are 0, 5, 10, 25 and 50.
72	
73	### Spill
74	
75	How much of the key colour is removed from the edges that remain. Pixels in the soft edge are pulled toward a grey of their own brightness, which takes out a green fringe. It works only in that edge, so with **Softness** at 0 it has almost nothing to act on.
76	
77	The range is 0 to 100 %, and the default is 50 %. The quick picks are 0, 25, 50, 75 and 100.
78	
79	## Animate the key
80	
81	With an [action](/motion/edit-an-action/) selected, **Key Color**, **Tolerance**, **Softness** and **Spill** set the value at the action's end and animate toward it. The colour blends through the OKLab colour space along the action. **Pick from Canvas** also sends its colour to the action's end.
82	
83	## Good to know
84	
85	- The key runs before the grade, so [grading a clip](/color/color-tab/) doesn't change what's keyed. A [camera log](/hdr/camera-log/) conversion and the [source conversion](/hdr/how-sources-are-read/) come first, so the key sees the converted picture.
86	- [Show Ungraded](/color/show-ungraded/) leaves the key on.
87	- How a key behaves when a project switches between SDR and HDR is on [A project's dynamic range](/hdr/dynamic-range/).
88	
89	## With an agent
90	
91	An agent sets the key with `set_video`, using the same colour and the same three amounts written as 0 to 1. It has no **Pick from Canvas**, so it passes the colour as numbers. See [Tools: picture and grade](/mcp/tools-set-video/#chroma-key).

98	=================== filters.mdx
99	---
100	title: Filters
101	description: Stack up to four filters on a clip, from Blur and Pixelate to Sepia and Vignette, set how strong each one is, and animate them.
102	---
103	
104	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
105	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
106	
107	Filters change how a clip looks: soften it, break it into blocks, turn it black and white, darken its corners. A clip can carry up to four at once, and any clip that draws can have them, text, shapes and graphics included.
108	
109	<AtAGlance
110	  where="Clip tab ▸ Picture ▸ Filters"
111	  tools={['set_video', 'set_action_end', 'paste_attributes']}
112	/>
113	
114	## Add a filter
115	
116	<Steps>
117	
118	1. Select the clip and open the **Clip** tab's [**Picture**](/canvas/picture-tab/) sub-tab.
119	
120	2. Open the **Filters** section. On a clip with none it reads "No filters on this clip."
121	
122	3. Choose **Add Filter**. A Blur at 50 % joins the end of the stack.
123	
124	4. Pick the filter you want in the row's popup that reads **Blur**, and set its **Amount**.
125	
126	</Steps>
127	
128	Changing a filter's kind keeps its **Amount**. A clip can hold four, as the "4 at most" beside **Add Filter** says, and the button greys out at that point.
129	
130	Each change is one undo step. While the section is closed, its header shows `none`, the filter's name, or a count such as `3 filters`.
131	
132	## The seven filters
133	
134	| Filter | What it does | At 100 % |
135	| --- | --- | --- |
136	| **Blur** | Softens the picture. | A radius of 24 pixels |
137	| **Sharpen** | Crisps up edges and fine detail with an unsharp mask. | A gain of 2 |
138	| **Pixelate** | Breaks the picture into square blocks. The clip's edge and rounded corners stay clean. | Blocks 64 pixels across |
139	| **Sepia** | Gives the picture a warm old-photo tone. | The full tone |
140	| **Noir** | Turns the picture black and white and adds contrast. Taking **Saturation** to its lowest only removes the colour. | Fully black and white |
141	| **Vignette** | Darkens towards the edges in an ellipse fitted to the clip's cropped shape. The darkening starts a little under halfway from the centre to the corners. | Black corners |
142	| **Invert** | Turns the picture into its negative. | The full negative |
143	
144	Blur and Pixelate are measured in the clip's own pixels. Scale a clip up and the effect grows with it, and the same **Amount** looks finer on a 4K clip than on a 1080p one.
145	
146	## Set how strong a filter is
147	
148	**Amount** runs from 0 to 100 %, with quick picks at 0, 25, 50, 75 and 100. At 0 the filter stays on the clip and does nothing. Sepia, Noir and Invert mix from the original picture towards their full effect as the number rises.
149	
150	## Stack and reorder filters
151	
152	Each filter's row starts with a number popup, which is its place in the stack. Pick a different number to move the filter. You can't drag rows. A move is one undo step.
153	
154	The place doesn't decide everything, because Frame Job always works through a stack in this order:
155	
156	1. Pixelate, whatever its place.
157	2. The **Color** section of the [Color tab](/color/color-tab/): **Brightness**, **Contrast**, **Saturation** and **Hue**.
158	3. Blur and Sharpen, whatever their places.
159	4. The rest of the Color tab: **Light**, **Wheels**, **Curves** and **Look**.
160	5. Sepia, Noir, Vignette and Invert, in the order of their places.
161	
162	So the order only changes the picture among Sepia, Noir, Vignette and Invert. Noir then Sepia gives a warm black and white, while Sepia then Noir gives a plain one. Moving a Blur above or below a Sepia changes nothing.
163	
164	Filters of the same kind combine:
165	
166	| In one stack | You get |
167	| --- | --- |
168	| Two Blurs | One wider blur. Two at 100 % reach a radius of about 34 pixels, and four reach 48. |
169	| Two Sharpens | The sum of the two. |
170	| Two Pixelates | The coarser of the two. |
171	
172	## Remove a filter
173	
174	Choose **Remove** in the filter's row. **Reset** in the section's header takes off the whole stack, and it's there only while no action is selected.
175	
176	## Animate a filter
177	
178	An [action](/motion/actions/) can ramp a filter's **Amount**, for example a blur that builds across a clip.
179	
180	<Steps>
181	
182	1. Add the filter and set **Amount** to where the ramp should start.
183	
184	2. Add an action on the clip and keep it selected.
185	
186	3. Set **Amount** to where the ramp should end.
187	
188	</Steps>
189	
190	With an action selected, each control does something different:
191	
192	| You change | What happens |
193	| --- | --- |
194	| **Amount** | It ramps across the action. |
195	| The filter's kind | It switches at the action's end, and the row shows "at end". The other filters keep ramping. |
196	| The filter's place | It moves at the action's end. |
197	| **Add Filter** or **Remove** | It changes the clip itself rather than the action, so it isn't animated. |
198	
199	:::caution
200	Adding or removing a filter while an action already animates the stack leaves the two stacks different lengths. The action stops ramping them and the filters switch at its end instead. To get the ramp back, select the action, choose **Clear** in the section's header, then set the clip's amounts and the action's again.
201	:::
202	
203	See [Set what an action animates to](/motion/edit-an-action/) for how the rows behave in an action.
204	
205	## Filters on an adjustment clip
206	
207	An [adjustment clip](/color/adjustment-clips/) has no Picture tab, so it can't take a filter from the inspector. It gets one through [Paste Attributes](/editing/paste-attributes/) instead.
208	
209	<Steps>
210	
211	1. Put Sepia, Noir, Vignette or Invert on an ordinary clip and press <kbd>⌘C</kbd>.
212	
213	2. Select the adjustment clip.
214	
215	3. Press <kbd>⌥⌘V</kbd>, or choose **Edit ▸ Paste Attributes**.
216	
217	</Steps>
218	
219	The filter then applies to everything behind the adjustment clip for as long as it lasts, and to nothing on a track in front.
220	
221	Blur, Sharpen and Pixelate can't go on an adjustment clip, because it has no picture of its own to sample. Pasting from a clip that has one stops with an error naming the clip and the filter, and changes nothing.
222	
223	:::caution
224	Paste Attributes replaces the target's picture settings, not only its filters. Pasting onto an adjustment clip overwrites its grade and its Strength with the copied clip's, so paste first and grade afterwards.
225	:::
226	
227	## Good to know
228	
229	- A filter covers the whole picture for the whole clip. To blur or pixelate one region, such as a face, use [Obscure](/effects/obscure/).
230	- With several clips selected, the rows show the first clip's stack, and any edit gives every selected clip that whole stack.
231	- A [nest](/editing/nests/) clip shows the Filters section, but a filter on it has no effect. Put filters on the clips inside the nest.
232	- On a [matte track](/canvas/matte-tracks/), a clip's filters shape the cut it makes. **Alpha** and **Inverted Alpha** read only transparency, so Sharpen, Sepia, Noir, Vignette and Invert change nothing there.
233	- A clip's [reflection](/effects/reflection/) shows its filters too.
234	
235	## With an agent
236	
237	An agent sets a clip's filters with `set_video`, as a list of kinds and amounts, with each amount from 0 to 1. The list replaces the old one whole, so it sends every filter it wants to keep, and an empty list clears the stack. A fifth filter is an error, and nothing changes. It can put Sepia, Noir, Vignette or Invert straight onto an adjustment clip, with no paste. See [Tools: picture and grade](/mcp/tools-set-video/).
238	
239	With `set_action_end`, an agent can give an action a list of a different length, which switches at the action's end rather than ramping. See [Tools: animation](/mcp/tools-animation/).
240	
241	## Related

245	- [Adjustment clips](/color/adjustment-clips/)
246	- [Paste Attributes](/editing/paste-attributes/)

249	=================== hide-while-silent.mdx
250	---
251	title: Hide While Silent
252	description: Fade a clip out in the pauses of someone's speech and back in before they talk again.
253	---
254	
255	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
256	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
257	
258	Hide While Silent fades a clip out in the pauses of someone's speech and back in before they talk again. Use it on a camera over a screen recording, so the presenter is there while they're talking and out of the way when they aren't.
259	
260	<AtAGlance
261	  where="Clip tab ▸ Picture ▸ Hide While Silent"
262	  tools={['set_video', 'set_media_speech']}
263	  needs="Nothing. Frame Job finds the speech on your Mac, with no key and no upload."
264	/>
265	
266	## Turn it on
267	
268	<Steps>
269	
270	1. Select the clip that should come and go, such as the camera.
271	
272	2. In the Clip tab's **Picture** sub-tab, open the **Hide While Silent** section. It's shut until you open it.
273	
274	3. Tick **Hide while silent**.
275	
276	</Steps>
277	
278	The clip now follows the first file in [**Speech from**](#choose-which-file-to-follow), with the default [timing](#adjust-the-timing). The fade shows in the preview and in every export.
279	
280	The section's header reads **off**, **on** or the name of the file the clip follows. With several clips selected, ticking the box turns it on for each clip that's off, all following the same file.
281	
282	To turn it off, untick the box or choose **Reset** in the section's header.
283	
284	The checkbox is greyed in two cases, and its tooltip says which:
285	
286	| Tooltip | What it means |
287	| --- | --- |
288	| "No clip with sound plays under the selection." | Nothing with sound plays at the same time as the clip, so there's no speech to follow. |
289	| "… speech has not been detected yet, so a clip cannot hide while it is silent. Try again in a moment." | Frame Job is still working through the file, which often happens straight after an import. |
290	
291	## Choose which file to follow
292	
293	**Speech from** lists the files with sound that play at the same time as the clip, on any track, one row each. The clip's own file is there too if it has sound. It's dimmed until **Hide while silent** is on.
294	
295	Files with no picture, such as a microphone recording, come first, then the file that plays alongside the clip for longest. A file you've already chosen stays in the list even if it no longer plays with the clip.
296	
297	If you pick a file whose speech Frame Job hasn't found yet, nothing changes and a note in the section says why.
298	
299	## Adjust the timing
300	
301	| Control | What it does | Default | Range | Quick picks |
302	| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
303	| **Pre-roll** | How long before each run of words the clip is fully back. | 0.2 s | 0 to 5 s | 0, 0.1, 0.2, 0.5 |
304	| **Hold** | How long the clip stays after each run of words. | 1.5 s | 0 to 5 s | 0.5, 1, 1.5, 3 |
305	| **Fade** | How long the clip takes to fade out and in. At 0 it's a straight cut. | 0.3 s | 0 to 5 s | 0, 0.15, 0.3, 0.5 |
306	
307	**Fade** comes on top of the other two. The clip starts to fade out when **Hold** ends, and it finishes fading in **Pre-roll** before the first word.
308	
309	That means short pauses never hide the clip. A pause no longer than **Pre-roll** plus **Hold** leaves it on screen, which is 1.7 s at the defaults. The clip only fades all the way out in a pause of at least **Pre-roll** plus **Hold** plus two **Fades**, which is 2.3 s. Anything in between is a partial dip.
310	
311	Each change is one undo step, called Hide While Silent. These rows belong to the clip, even with an [action](/motion/actions/) selected.
312	
313	## See it on the timeline
314	
315	A teal line runs across the picture part of the clip. Where it's at the top, the clip shows. Where it's at the bottom, the clip is hidden. The clip has to be [tall enough](/timeline/track-height/) to show the line.
316	
317	Inside an open [nest](/editing/nests/), the line of a clip that follows a file outside the nest stays flat at the top, though the clip still fades. See [Reading a clip on the timeline](/timeline/reading-a-clip/).
318	
319	## When the followed file stops playing
320	
321	Where the file doesn't play at all, the clip shows. There's no fade at that edge, so a hidden clip comes straight back when the file's clip ends. The clip also shows wherever the file has no saved speech.
322	
323	With [nests](/editing/nests/), Frame Job reads the file in the nearest place that plays it at that moment: the clip's own timeline, then each enclosing nest outward. So when a camera is inside a nest and the microphone isn't, the microphone outside is followed.
324	
325	## The fade stays out of Opacity
326	
327	The fade only touches the picture Frame Job draws. The clip's own **Opacity** in the [Transform section](/canvas/transform/) keeps its value. A clip at 50 % Opacity peaks at 50 % and fades from there.
328	
329	An [action](/motion/actions/) can't animate Hide While Silent, though it can still animate the clip's Opacity.
330	
331	## Good to know
332	
333	- **Where the speech comes from.** It's the same as [Duck by Speech](/audio/duck-by-speech/): the runs of words Frame Job finds in the file on this Mac when it's added. The first time a file is followed, those runs are saved in the project in the same undo step.
334	- **Only what plays counts.** Speech in a part of the file you've trimmed or cut away doesn't bring the clip back. A muted clip of the file still counts, because the speech is read from the file, not the mix.
335	- **Nest clips.** A nest clip has no picture of its own, so the section isn't offered for it, or for a selection that includes one. Set it on the clips inside.
336	- **Removing the file.** [Removing the followed file](/projects/remove-media/) from the project turns Hide While Silent off on every clip that followed it.
337	- **Copying.** A pasted clip keeps Hide While Silent only when the file it follows comes along too, and Frame Job brings that file with it. [Paste Attributes](/editing/paste-attributes/) works the same way.
338	
339	## With an agent
340	
341	`set_video` can point a clip at any file in the project that has sound, not only one playing alongside it. It fails on a file with no sound, on a file whose speech hasn't been found yet, and on a nest clip. `set_media_speech` saves runs of speech you supply for a file, in place of the ones Frame Job found.
342	
343	`get_project` reads the clip's own opacity, without the fade, and `set_action_end` doesn't accept Hide While Silent. See [Tools: picture and grade](/mcp/tools-set-video/) and [Tools: media](/mcp/tools-media/).
344	
345	## Related

347	- [Record a camera beside the screen](/recording/camera-beside-the-screen/)
348	- [Duck by Speech](/audio/duck-by-speech/)
349	- [Reading a clip on the timeline](/timeline/reading-a-clip/)
350	- [Position, scale, rotation and opacity](/canvas/transform/)
351	=================== obscure.mdx
352	---
353	title: Obscure
354	description: Hide a face, a password or a phone number behind pixelated or blurred regions that stay on the clip as it moves.
355	---
356	
357	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
358	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
359	
360	Obscure hides part of a clip's picture, such as a face, a password field or a phone number, behind a pixelated or blurred region. A clip can carry up to four regions.
361	
362	<AtAGlance
363	  where="Clip tab ▸ Picture ▸ Obscure"
364	  tools={['set_video', 'set_action_end']}
365	/>
366	
367	## Draw a region on the picture
368	
369	<Steps>
370	
371	1. Select the clip, and move the playhead to a frame that shows what you want to hide.
372	
373	2. In the Clip tab's **Picture** sub-tab, open the **Obscure** section. It's shut until you open it.
374	
375	3. Choose **Place on Canvas**. The preview reads "Drag a rectangle to obscure · Esc to cancel".
376	
377	4. Drag a rectangle over what you want to hide.
378	
379	</Steps>
380	
381	The region lands pixelated at full strength, and it's one undo step, called Obscure Region. Its controls appear in the section as **Region 1**, **Region 2** and so on.
382	
383	A region lasts the whole clip and keeps its place on the clip's picture. It doesn't track anything that moves in the footage. To hide something for part of a clip, [split](/editing/splitting/) the clip first and put the region on the piece that needs it. To follow something across the shot, [animate the region](#animate-a-region).
384	
385	Place on Canvas draws one region and then ends. It needs exactly one selected clip, drawing at the playhead and not on a locked track, with fewer than four regions. Otherwise it beeps, and at four regions the button is greyed.
386	
387	While you're drawing:
388	
389	- You can start the drag outside the picture, which is the way to catch the edge of the frame.
390	- A drag under 6 canvas pixels wide or tall counts as a miss. It beeps and you can draw again.
391	- <kbd>Esc</kbd> or a second press of **Place on Canvas** stops without adding anything. Once focus has moved to a field in the inspector, <kbd>Esc</kbd> no longer reaches the preview, so use the button.
392	- Changing the selection, or moving the playhead off the clip, also stops it.
393	
394	Only one mode that waits for a click or drag on the preview can be on at a time: Place on Canvas, [Zoom to Region](/motion/zoom-to-region/), [Chroma Key's Pick from Canvas](/effects/chroma-key/) and the [qualifier's Pick from Canvas](/color/pick-from-canvas/). Turning one on ends the other.
395	
396	## Add a region without drawing
397	
398	**Add Region** puts a 480 × 270 region at the centre of the clip, as one undo step called Add Region. It's a **Rectangle**, set to **Pixelate** at 100 % **Amount** with 20 px **Feather**. A region you draw takes the same settings, apart from its position and size.
399	
400	The button is greyed at four regions, and the note beside it reads "4 at most". With no regions, the section reads "No obscured regions."
401	
402	The section's header sums up what's on the clip: **none**, the kind when there's one region, or the count, such as **2 regions**.
403	
404	## Choose Pixelate or Blur
405	
406	The pop-up in each **Region** row sets how the region hides what's under it.
407	
408	| Kind | What it does | At 100 % Amount |
409	| --- | --- | --- |
410	| **Pixelate** | Replaces the picture with coarse blocks, destroying the detail. This is the default. | Blocks 64 of the clip's own pixels across |
411	| **Blur** | Softens the picture. | A blur reaching 24 of the clip's own pixels |
412	
413	:::caution
414	Blur at its strongest is still a soft blur, and large text can be read through it. Use **Pixelate** for anything that must not be read.
415	:::
416	
417	Both are measured in the clip's own pixels, so they grow and shrink with the clip. On a 4K recording, a block is half as wide, as a share of the picture, as it is on a 1080p one. Check that what you've hidden stays hidden at the size you'll export.
418	
419	## The region controls
420	
421	Each region has its own group of rows.
422	
423	| Control | What it does | Default | Range | Quick picks |
424	| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
425	| **Region 1** pop-up | The kind, [Pixelate or Blur](#choose-pixelate-or-blur). | Pixelate | | |
426	| **Shape** | The outline of the region. | Rectangle | Rectangle, Ellipse | |
427	| **Amount** | How strongly it hides. At 0 % the region is there and hides nothing. | 100 % | 0 to 100 % | 0, 25, 50, 75, 100 |
428	| **Feather** | How wide the ramp is over the region's edge. At 0 the edge is hard. | 20 px | 0 to 200 px | 0, 10, 20, 40, 80 |
429	| **Center** | Where the region's centre sits, as x and y from the centre of the clip's picture, with y counting down. | 0, 0 | −20,000 to 20,000 px | |
430	| **Size** | The region's width and height. | 480 × 270 | 1 to 20,000 px | Width 120, 240, 480, 960. Height 68, 135, 270, 540 |
431	
432	**Center** and **Size** are in the clip's own pixels, not the canvas's, so 480 × 270 covers less of a 4K recording than of a 1080p one. A region can sit partly or wholly off the clip.
433	
434	**Feather** straddles the outline, half inside and half outside. At 20 px the effect is at full strength only from 10 px inside the outline, so leave a margin around anything that must stay hidden.
435	
436	## Move and resize a region on the canvas
437	
438	Select one clip and its regions draw on the preview as dashed outlines, each with a cross at its centre and eight handles.
439	
440	| To | Do this |
441	| --- | --- |
442	| Move a region | Drag its centre cross. |
443	| Resize a region | Drag one of its handles. The far edge stays where it is. |
444	| Resize about the centre | Hold <kbd>⌥</kbd> while you drag a handle. |
445	| Cancel the drag | Press <kbd>Esc</kbd>. Everything goes back, with no undo step. |
446	
447	Each drag is one undo step, called Move Region or Resize Region. A side stays between 1 and 20,000 of the clip's own pixels.
448	
449	The outlines show only with exactly one clip selected, on an unlocked track, outside [crop mode](/canvas/crop/) and the text editor.
450	
451	The clip's own handles win where they overlap a region's. A drag inside a region, away from its cross and handles, moves the clip. While Place on Canvas or Zoom to Region is on, it takes every press, and the outlines stay drawn underneath.
452	
453	## Remove a region
454	
455	Choose **Remove** in the region's row. It's one undo step, called Remove Region, and the regions after it renumber.
456	
457	**Reset** in the section's header clears every region on the clip. It isn't there while an action is selected. See [Clear and Reset](/motion/edit-an-action/#clear-and-reset).
458	
459	## Animate a region
460	
461	Each region's numbers can change over an [action](/motion/actions/), which is how a region follows something moving across the shot or fades in over a few seconds.
462	
463	With an action selected, the rows and the canvas handles set how the region looks at the action's end:
464	
465	- **Amount**, **Feather**, **Center** and **Size** ramp to the new value along the action's curve.
466	- **Shape** and the kind switch at the action's end. The other regions on the clip keep ramping.
467	
468	With an action selected, the inspector shows the action's end state, so a changed kind or shape reads as the new one straight away. The picture keeps the old one until the action's end.
469	
470	**Add Region**, **Place on Canvas** and **Remove** always change the clip itself, even with an action selected, because three regions can't ramp into four. If an action already animates the regions, it keeps the number it had, so the clip and the action now disagree. All the regions then switch at the action's end instead of ramping, and while the two numbers differ the outlines stay on the preview without their cross and handles.
471	
472	See [Set what an action animates to](/motion/edit-an-action/).
473	
474	## Good to know
475	
476	- **Regions ride with the clip.** They stay on the same part of the picture through a move, a scale, a rotation and a [zoom](/motion/zoom-to-region/). A region drawn on a rotated clip is the box around your drag in the clip's own axes, so it turns with the clip and comes out larger than the rectangle you dragged.
477	- **Cropping can shift a region.** A region is measured from the centre of the cropped picture, so cropping more off one side than the other moves the region across the picture by half the difference. Check your regions after a [crop](/canvas/crop/).
478	- **Overlapping regions.** Where two overlap, whichever hides more wins, and two overlapping blurs add up. So the order of the regions doesn't matter, and there's no way to reorder them.
479	- **Filters and the grade.** A region's colour is graded and filtered like the picture around it. A [Sharpen filter](/effects/filters/) can't bring the hidden detail back. On a clip with a Blur filter, a pixelated region's blocks aren't blurred.
480	- **Pixelate's blocks sit on a grid across the whole picture.** Moving a region doesn't shift them, and its edge can cut through a block.
481	- **Several clips selected.** Any change gives them all the same regions, taken from the first selected clip and replacing what the others had.
482	- **What it works on.** Every clip that draws has the section, text and shapes included. It shows on a [nest](/editing/nests/) clip but has no effect there, so set it on the clips inside. An adjustment clip has no **Picture** sub-tab.
483	- **Missing files.** While a clip's file is missing, its slate shows without the regions.
484	- **Copying regions.** [Paste Attributes](/editing/paste-attributes/) carries a clip's regions, along with the rest of its picture settings.
485	
486	## With an agent
487	
488	`set_video` sets a clip's regions as one list, `obscure`. Each call replaces the whole list, and `[]` clears it. A list of more than four fails with an error, so no region is ever dropped without you knowing. To change a region over time, use `set_action_end`. See [Tools: picture and grade](/mcp/tools-set-video/) and [Tools: animation](/mcp/tools-animation/).
489	
490	## Related
491	
492	- [Spotlight](/effects/spotlight/)
493	- [Filters](/effects/filters/)
494	- [Split clips](/editing/splitting/)
495	- [Actions](/motion/actions/)

497	=================== reflection.mdx
498	---
499	title: Reflection
500	description: Hang a mirrored copy of a clip below itself, and set how strong, how tall and how far away it is and how it fades.
501	---
502	
503	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
504	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
505	
506	A reflection hangs a mirrored copy of a clip under its bottom edge, fading out as it goes, like an object standing on a glossy shelf. Any clip that draws can have one, text and shapes included.
507	
508	<AtAGlance where="Clip tab ▸ Picture ▸ Reflection" tools="set_video" />
509	
510	## Add a reflection
511	
512	<Steps>
513	
514	1. Select the clip and open the **Clip** tab's [**Picture**](/canvas/picture-tab/) sub-tab.
515	
516	2. Open the **Reflection** section and tick **Mirror the layer below itself**.
517	
518	3. Adjust the [rows](#shape-the-reflection) until it looks right.
519	
520	</Steps>
521	
522	Untick the box, or choose **Reset** in the section's header, to take the reflection off. Doing that forgets its settings, so ticking the box again starts from the defaults.
523	
524	While the section is closed, its header shows `off` or the reflection's **Opacity**.
525	
526	:::note
527	The reflection hangs below the clip, so a clip that fills the frame has its reflection off the bottom of the canvas. Scale the clip down or move it up to make room.
528	:::
529	
530	## Shape the reflection
531	
532	The rows are greyed out until the box is ticked.
533	
534	| Row | What it does | Default | Range | Quick picks |
535	| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
536	| **Opacity** | How strong the reflection is where it touches the clip. | 35 % | 0–100 % | 0, 20, 35, 50, 75 |
537	| **Height** | How much of the clip is mirrored, as a share of its cropped height. | 50 % | 0–100 % | 25, 50, 75, 100 |
538	| **Gap** | The space between the clip and its reflection, in the clip's own pixels. | 0 px | 0–200 px | 0, 4, 8, 16, 32 |
539	| **Falloff** | How far the reflection fades on its way down. | 100 % | 0–100 % | 0, 25, 50, 75, 100 |
540	
541	**Height** is a share rather than a size in pixels, so the reflection keeps its proportions when you scale the clip. **Gap** scales with the clip too.
542	
543	**Falloff** fades the reflection in a straight line from its top to the bottom of its **Height**. At 0 % it doesn't fade at all, at 50 % it ends at half its **Opacity**, and at 100 % it reaches transparent exactly at the bottom.
544	
545	At 0 % **Opacity** or 0 % **Height**, nothing is drawn.
546	
547	## What the reflection shows
548	
549	The reflection is a mirror of the clip, not of the frame around it.
550	
551	- It carries what the clip draws, including its crop, rounded corners, grade, filters and spotlight.
552	- It meets what's behind it with the clip's own [blend mode](/canvas/blend-modes/), and the clip's opacity fades it too.
553	- It rotates with the clip.
554	- The clip always draws over its own reflection.
555	- It never shows clips on tracks in front, even ones sitting over the clip.
556	- It casts no shadow of its own.
557	
558	## Animate a reflection
559	
560	All four numbers ramp in an [action](/motion/actions/). The tick box doesn't: ticking or unticking it with an action selected makes the reflection appear or disappear at the action's end.
561	
562	To fade a reflection in, tick it on the clip with **Opacity** at 0 %, add an action, and raise **Opacity** in the action.
563	
564	## Good to know
565	
566	- With several clips selected, the rows show the first clip's reflection, and any edit gives every selected clip all four of those values.
567	- On a [matte track](/canvas/matte-tracks/), a clip's reflection has no effect. It's kept, and applies again when the track stops being a matte.
568	- A [nest](/editing/nests/) clip shows the Reflection section, but a reflection on it has no effect. Put it on the clips inside.
569	- An [adjustment clip](/color/adjustment-clips/) has no Picture tab, and a reflection pasted onto one does nothing.
570	
571	## With an agent
572	
573	An agent sets `reflection` with `set_video`, as an object of `opacity`, `height`, `gap` and `falloff`, and `null` takes the reflection off. `opacity`, `height` and `falloff` run from 0 to 1 rather than as percentages. `gap` isn't held to the field's 200 px limit, so it can be any number of 0 or more. See [Tools: picture and grade](/mcp/tools-set-video/).
574

581	=================== remove-background.mdx
582	---
583	title: Remove Background
584	description: Keep the person in a video or picture and make the rest transparent, with no green screen, upload or key.
585	---
586	
587	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
588	import Shot from '@components/Shot.astro';
589	
590	Remove Background keeps the person in a video or picture and makes the rest transparent, so whatever is on the tracks behind shows through. You don't need a green screen.
591	
592	<AtAGlance
593	  menu="Clip ▸ Remove Background"
594	  where="Clip tab ▸ Picture ▸ Background"
595	  tools={['set_video', 'analyze_cutout', 'get_media_analysis']}
596	  needs="Nothing. The masks are made on your Mac, with no key and no upload."
597	/>
598	
599	<Shot
600	  name="05i-clip-background.inspector"
601	  alt="The Background section of the inspector, open, with its summary reading Analyzing 0 %. Remove background is ticked, Background reads Remove, Edge is at 0.00, Feather is at 0%, Status reads Analyzing 0 %, and an Analyze Now button sits below."
602	/>
603	
604	## Turn it on
605	
606	Select a clip and choose **Clip ▸ Remove Background**, or tick **Remove background** in the Clip tab's **Background** section. The menu item has no keyboard shortcut. Frame Job starts making the [masks](#how-the-masks-are-made) straight away, and you don't need to do anything else. Put whatever should show through on a track behind the clip.
607	
608	It works on clips of a video file that has a picture, freeze frames of one, and image clips. Text, shape, graphic, adjustment and nest clips can't be cut out, and the section appears only when every selected clip can.
609	
610	With several clips selected:
611	
612	| Control | What it does |
613	| --- | --- |
614	| **Clip ▸ Remove Background** | When every clip that can be cut out already is, it turns them all off. Otherwise it turns on the ones without it, and each clip that has it keeps its own values. Selected clips that can't be cut out are left alone. |
615	| **Remove background** checkbox | Ticking it gives each clip without it the defaults. Unticking it removes it from all of them. |
616	
617	The menu item shows a check when every target is cut out, a dash when some are, and nothing when none are. It's dimmed when no selected clip can be cut out. Either way, the change is one undo step, **Remove Background**.
618	
619	The section comes right after **Chroma Key** and is shut by default. Its header reads "off" when no selected clip has Remove Background. Otherwise it reads the [Status](#status), or "on" with several clips selected. **Reset** turns Remove Background off.
620	
621	**Subject**, **Background**, **Edge** and **Feather** stay dimmed until every selected clip has Remove Background on. A selection where only some clips have it keeps them dimmed.
622	
623	## Tune the cut-out
624	
625	### Subject
626	
627	This row shows only when every selected clip is a picture. See [Pictures](#pictures).
628	
629	| Choice | What it keeps |
630	| --- | --- |
631	| **Person** (default) | The person |
632	| **Foreground** | Every foreground subject it finds, whether that's a person, a pet or an object |
633	
634	It reads mixed when the selected pictures differ. A clip of a video file or a freeze frame always keeps the person.
635	
636	### Background
637	
638	**Remove**, the default, draws the subject alone. **Keep** draws the whole clip, but Frame Job still knows where the subject is, so another clip can go behind them. The masks are made either way.
639	
640	**Keep** is how a title goes behind a person in frame, and it's what [Text Behind Subject](/effects/text-behind-subject/) gives a clip with no cut-out.
641	
642	### Edge
643	
644	Pulls the outline in or pushes it out. Below 0 pulls in, and above 0 pushes out. The range is −1 to 1, the default is 0, and the quick picks are −0.5, −0.25, 0, 0.25 and 0.5.
645	
646	A mask is more or less sure of each point in the picture. **Edge** sets how sure it has to be. With **Feather** at 0:
647	
648	| Edge | The outline sits where the mask is |
649	| --- | --- |
650	| −1 | 7/8 sure it's the person |
651	| −0.5 | 3/4 sure |
652	| 0 | Half sure |
653	| 0.5 | 1/4 sure |
654	| 1 | 1/8 sure |
655	
656	Across a band of pixels where the mask fades from background to person, **Edge** at −1 or 1 moves the outline about three eighths of the band's width. Raising **Edge** never removes anything a lower value kept.
657	
658	### Feather
659	
660	How soft the outline is. The range is 0 to 100 %, the default is 0 %, and the quick picks are 0, 10, 25 and 50.
661	
662	### Inside an action
663	
664	With an [action](/motion/edit-an-action/) selected, **Edge** and **Feather** set the value at the action's end and animate toward it. **Background** switches at the action's end, and its row shows "at end".
665	
666	The **Remove background** checkbox, **Subject** and the section's **Reset** always change the clip itself, even with an action selected, and the checkbox and **Subject** rows show ⊘. You can't turn a cut-out off at the end of an action.
667	
668	## How the masks are made
669	
670	A mask is the outline of the subject in one frame. You never start this yourself. When you turn Remove Background on, or change what a cut-out clip plays, Frame Job makes masks for the frames that clip plays, in the background, while you go on working.
671	
672	Masks are made on this Mac with person segmentation from Apple's Vision framework, at its balanced setting. Nothing is uploaded, and no key is needed. They're kept per media in the project's cache, so a frame that's been analysed is never analysed again. See [On-device media analysis](/projects/media-analysis/#person-masks).
673	
674	Until a frame has its mask, the clip draws whole in the preview, as if Remove Background were off. A paused frame redraws by itself once its mask is ready, and a playing preview picks new masks up on its next frame.
675	
676	### Status
677	
678	**Status** says where the clip's masks stand, and why a clip is drawing whole.
679	
680	| Status | What it means |
681	| --- | --- |
682	| **Analyzing N %** | The masks are being made. The figure stops at 99 until they're done. |
683	| **Ready** | Every frame the clip plays has its mask. |
684	| **No person found** | Every frame was looked at and no person is in the clip, so it draws whole. A frame counts as holding a person when at least 0.5 % of its mask is above half. |
685	| **No subject found** | A picture with **Subject** set to **Foreground** was looked at and no subject was found, so it draws whole. |
686	| **Failed:** and the reason | The masks couldn't be made. The media file may be missing or unreadable, or the masks couldn't be written. Fix the cause and choose **Analyze Now**. |
687	| **No picture to analyze** | The clip plays no frame of its file. |
688	| **Off** | Remove Background is off. |
689	| **—** | Several clips are selected. |
690	
691	### Analyze Now
692	
693	Masks start on their own, so you'll mostly want this after a failure. **Analyze Now** asks again for the masks the clip needs, then retries a run that failed. It's enabled only while a clip is analysing or has failed.
694	
695	## Pictures
696	
697	<Shot
698	  name="05k-clip-background-picture.inspector"
699	  alt="The Background section for an image clip. Remove background is ticked, a Subject row reads Foreground above Background, which reads Remove, then Edge, Feather and a Status of Analyzing 0 %."
700	/>
701	
702	A picture gets one mask, made once on this Mac from the picture as the preview draws it, the right way up. When it's done, **Status** goes from Analyzing to **Ready**, or to **No person found** or **No subject found**.
703	
704	**Person** uses the same person segmentation as a video. **Foreground** uses the Vision framework's foreground instance mask, which keeps every foreground subject it finds. If it finds none, **Status** reads **No subject found** and the picture draws whole.
705	
706	## Exports
707	
708	With **Background** on **Remove**, an export draws the subject alone in every frame, GIF and APNG included. It waits until every mask its range needs is made, with no time limit, and the Exporting sheet reads "Preparing" and the file's name until then. You can cancel it while it waits.
709	
710	If a mask can't be made, the export fails with "Clip n's person masks could not be made: …" and writes no file. For a picture with **Subject** set to **Foreground**, the message says "foreground masks".
711	
712	A single frame doesn't wait as long. **File ▸ Save Frame…** (<kbd>⌥⌘E</kbd>) waits up to 30 seconds for the masks it needs. If they aren't ready by then, it saves the frame with the clip whole, and a sheet titled "Saved without Remove Background" names the files drawn whole. An agent's [`render_frame`](/mcp/render-frame/) waits the same 30 seconds, and its reply names any clip it drew whole.
713	
714	## Good to know
715	
716	- Once its masks are made, a clip draws whole only when no frame it plays has a person. If the person leaves the picture for part of a clip, those frames have little or nothing to keep, so what's behind shows through.
717	- The recorder panel can do this for you. See [Polish when a recording lands](/recording/when-it-lands/).
718	
719	## With an agent
720	
721	An agent turns this on with `set_video`, as the checkbox does, and sets the same options there. See [Tools: picture and grade](/mcp/tools-set-video/#cutout).
722	
723	`analyze_cutout` can wait up to 60 seconds for a clip's masks to settle, and it reports the subject's mean centre in the picture, which the app doesn't show. For a video, `get_media_analysis` says which stretches of the file hold a person. See [Tools: reading analysis](/mcp/tools-analysis/).
724
