733	=================== shadow.mdx
734	---
735	title: Shadow
736	description: Add a drop shadow cast by a clip's own shape, and set its colour, strength, softness, direction and distance.
737	---
738	
739	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
740	
741	A drop shadow lifts a clip off what's behind it. It's cast by the clip's own shape: the picture, a text clip's letters, or a shape's outline and fill.
742	
743	<AtAGlance where="Clip tab ▸ Picture ▸ Shadow" tools="set_video" />
744	
745	## Drop shadow
746	
747	Select a clip, open the **Shadow** section in the Clip tab's **Picture** sub-tab, and tick **Drop shadow**. It's off by default, and every clip that draws has it, text, shapes and graphics included. A [nest](/editing/nests/) clip shows the section too, but a shadow set there isn't drawn. Set it on the clips inside.
748	
749	Turning it on gives a soft shadow, down and to the right: black at 50 % with a 12 px blur, at 315° and 8 px away. The other rows stay dimmed until it's on.
750	
751	The section's header reads "off", or the blur in pixels. **Reset** takes the shadow off.
752	
753	The shadow follows what the clip actually draws. A clip with a [key](/effects/chroma-key/) or [Remove Background](/effects/remove-background/) casts the shadow of what's left, and the shadow fades with the clip's [opacity](/canvas/transform/).
754	
755	## Shape the shadow
756	
757	### Color
758	
759	Any colour, black by default. A colour you can see through multiplies with **Opacity**, so the shadow gets fainter than **Opacity** alone says.
760	
761	In an HLG project, shadow colours are lifted with the other drawn colours. See [A project's dynamic range](/hdr/dynamic-range/).
762	
763	### Opacity
764	
765	The shadow's strength. The range is 0 to 100 %, the default is 50 %, and the quick picks are 0, 25, 50, 75 and 100.
766	
767	### Blur
768	
769	How soft the shadow is. The range is 0 to 200 px, the default is 12 px, and the quick picks are 0, 4, 8, 12, 24 and 48.
770	
771	The pixels are the clip's own, so the blur grows when you scale the clip up.
772	
773	### Angle
774	
775	Which way the shadow falls. The range is 0 to 360°, the default is 315°, and the quick picks run every 45°.
776	
777	0° is to the right, and the angle increases counter-clockwise, so 90° is up, 180° is left, 270° is down and 315° is down and to the right.
778	
779	The direction belongs to the canvas, not the clip. Rotating a clip doesn't turn its shadow, so every shadow at the same angle falls the same way.
780	
781	### Distance
782	
783	How far the shadow falls from the clip. The range is 0 to 200 px, the default is 8 px, and the quick picks are 0, 4, 8, 16 and 32.
784	
785	Like **Blur**, it's in the clip's own pixels, so it grows when you scale the clip up.
786	
787	## Animate a shadow
788	
789	With an [action](/motion/edit-an-action/) selected, **Color**, **Opacity**, **Blur**, **Angle** and **Distance** set the value at the action's end and animate toward it. The colour blends through the OKLab colour space. Unticking **Drop shadow** with an action selected turns the shadow off at the action's end.
790	
791	## Good to know
792	
793	- A shadow has no effect on a clip on a [matte track](/canvas/matte-tracks/). The settings are kept and apply again when the track stops being a matte.
794	- A clip with [Behind subject](/effects/text-behind-subject/) on has its shadow cut with it.
795	- A clip with a drop shadow gets no [motion blur](/motion/motion-blur/). It draws sharp.
796	
797	## With an agent
798	
799	An agent sets the shadow with `set_video`, and changing one setting keeps the others. See [Tools: picture and grade](/mcp/tools-set-video/#shadow).
800

806	=================== spotlight.mdx
807	---
808	title: Spotlight
809	description: Dim a clip outside a rectangle or ellipse to point at one part of the picture, and magnify what's inside.
810	---
811	
812	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
813	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
814	
815	A spotlight dims a clip everywhere outside a rectangle or ellipse, so the eye goes to one part of the picture, such as a button in a screen recording. It can also magnify what's inside. Any clip that draws can have one, text and shapes included.
816	
817	<AtAGlance where="Clip tab ▸ Picture ▸ Spotlight" tools="set_video" />
818	
819	## Spotlight a region
820	
821	<Steps>
822	
823	1. Select the clip and open the **Clip** tab's [**Picture**](/canvas/picture-tab/) sub-tab.
824	
825	2. Open the **Spotlight** section and tick **Spotlight a region**. You get a 480 × 270 rectangle at the centre of the picture.
826	
827	3. Set **Center X**, **Center Y**, **Width** and **Height** to [place it](#place-the-spotlight).
828	
829	4. Adjust the other [rows](#the-controls) until it looks right.
830	
831	</Steps>
832	
833	There's no handle for a spotlight on the canvas, so the rows are the only way to place it. It's easier to see the region while you do if you raise **Dim** and lower **Feather** for a moment.
834	
835	Untick the box, or choose **Reset** in the section's header, to take the spotlight off. Doing that forgets its settings, so ticking the box again starts from the defaults.
836	
837	While the section is closed, its header shows `off`, `rectangle` or `ellipse`.
838	
839	## The controls
840	
841	The rows are greyed out until the box is ticked.
842	
843	| Row | What it does | Default | Range | Quick picks |
844	| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
845	| **Shape** | **Rectangle** or **Ellipse**. | Rectangle | | |
846	| **Center X**, **Center Y** | Where the middle of the region sits, measured from the centre of the clip's picture. | 0 px, 0 px | −20,000 to 20,000 px | |
847	| **Width**, **Height** | The size of the region. | 480 × 270 px | 1 to 20,000 px | **Width** 240, 480, 720, 960. **Height** 135, 270, 405, 540 |
848	| **Feather** | How many pixels the edge softens over. 0 is a hard edge. | 40 px | 0–200 px | 0, 10, 20, 40, 80 |
849	| **Dim** | How much darker everything outside the region goes. 0 % changes nothing and 100 % is black. | 60 % | 0–100 % | 0, 30, 60, 80, 100 |
850	| **Zoom** | How much to [magnify](#magnify-the-region) what's inside. 1.00× is no zoom. | 1.00× | 1.00–2.00× | 1, 1.2, 1.5, 2 |
851	
852	## Place the spotlight
853	
854	The centre and size are in the clip's own pixels, measured from the centre of its cropped picture. A positive **Center X** moves the region right and a positive **Center Y** moves it down.
855	
856	Because they belong to the picture, the spotlight stays on the same part of it when you move, scale or rotate the clip. They also don't depend on the canvas, so the default 480 × 270 covers less of a 4K clip than of a 1080p one.
857	
858	The region can sit partly or wholly off the clip.
859	
860	## What gets dimmed
861	
862	:::caution
863	A spotlight dims this clip only. Clips behind it and the canvas around it stay as they are, so to darken the whole frame the clip has to fill it.
864	:::
865	
866	The dim only changes colour. Dimmed parts of the clip stay as solid as they were, so nothing behind shows through, and transparent parts stay transparent.
867	
868	It comes after every colour stage, so the clip's grade and filters don't act on it.
869	
870	## Magnify the region
871	
872	**Zoom** enlarges what's inside the region about its centre. It works with **Dim** at 0 % too, which gives you a magnifier with no darkening.
873	
874	The magnification eases off towards the edge of the region so the picture doesn't tear there. That edge is always wide enough for the zoom to fade out smoothly, so it can be softer than **Feather** makes the edge of the light.
875	
876	The enlarged picture comes from the same frame, so it gets softer as **Zoom** rises.
877	
878	## Animate a spotlight
879	
880	Every number ramps in an [action](/motion/actions/), so a spotlight can slide from one part of the picture to another, grow, or brighten as it goes.
881	
882	Two controls switch rather than ramp:
883	
884	- **Shape** changes at the action's end, and the row shows "at end". The numbers keep ramping.
885	- Ticking or unticking **Spotlight a region** with an action selected makes the spotlight appear or disappear at the action's end.
886	
887	To fade a spotlight in, tick it on the clip with **Dim** at 0 %, add an action, and raise **Dim** in the action.
888	
889	## Good to know
890	
891	- A spotlight lasts as long as the clip. To point at something for a few seconds, [split](/editing/splitting/) the clip around that moment and put the spotlight on the middle piece.
892	- With several clips selected, the rows show the first clip's spotlight, and any edit gives every selected clip all of those values.
893	- On a [matte track](/canvas/matte-tracks/), a clip's spotlight shapes the cut it makes. **Alpha** and **Inverted Alpha** read only transparency, so **Dim** changes nothing there.
894	- A clip's [reflection](/effects/reflection/) shows its spotlight too, mirrored.
895	- A [nest](/editing/nests/) clip shows the Spotlight section, but a spotlight on it has no effect. Put it on the clips inside.
896	- An [adjustment clip](/color/adjustment-clips/) has no Picture tab, and a spotlight pasted onto one does nothing.
897	
898	## With an agent
899	
900	An agent sets `spotlight` with `set_video`, as an object of `shape` (`rect` or `ellipse`), `x`, `y`, `width`, `height`, `feather`, `dim` and `zoom`, and `null` takes the spotlight off. It isn't held to the fields' limits for placing a spotlight: it can set any centre, any size above 0 and any `feather` of 0 or more. `dim` runs from 0 to 1 rather than as a percentage, and `zoom` from 1 to 2. See [Tools: picture and grade](/mcp/tools-set-video/).
901

911	title: Text Behind Subject
912	description: Put a title, shape, picture or graphic behind the person in a clip, so they stand in front of it and the room stays behind it.
913	---
914	
915	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
916	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
917	
918	Text Behind Subject puts a title behind the person in a camera clip or photo. The person stands in front of the title, and the room stays behind it. A shape, picture or graphic can go behind a person the same way.
919	
920	<AtAGlance
921	  menu="Insert ▸ Text Behind Subject"
922	  where="Clip tab ▸ Picture ▸ Behind Subject"
923	  tools={['text_behind_subject', 'set_video']}
924	  needs="Nothing. The masks are made on your Mac, with no key and no upload."

926	
927	## Text behind subject in one step
928	
929	<Steps>
930	
931	1. Move the playhead to where the title should start, over the camera clip or photo.
932	
933	2. If several clips play there, select the one with the person.
934	
935	3. Choose **Insert ▸ Text Behind Subject**. It has no keyboard shortcut.
936	
937	4. The new title is selected, so type your text in the Clip tab's [**Text** sub-tab](/text-and-shapes/text-clips/).
938	
939	</Steps>
940	
941	One **Undo** takes it all back. The step is named **Text Behind Subject**.
942	
943	Here's what the command does:
944	
945	- It adds a track named "Behind Subject" directly above the clip's track, and above any [matte tracks](/canvas/matte-tracks/) in front of it.
946	- It puts a title on that track with the **Title** [preset](/text-and-shapes/text-presets/), running from the playhead for 4 seconds, or to the clip's end if that's sooner.
947	- It puts the title behind the subject.
948	- If the clip had no [Remove Background](/effects/remove-background/), it turns that on with **Background** set to **Keep** and **Subject** set to **Person**, so the picture stays whole and the person still hides the title. A clip that already has a cut-out keeps it.
949	
950	It works with a clip of a video file or a picture that's playing at the playhead, with its picture on, on a shown track that isn't a matte track. Of those, it takes the front-most selected clip, else the front-most with Remove Background on, else the front-most.
951	
952	The item is greyed while a [nest](/editing/nests/) is open, and when no such clip plays at the playhead.
953	
954	## Behind subject by hand
955	
956	Any clip that draws can go behind a subject, except an adjustment clip or a nest clip.
957	
958	<Steps>
959	
960	1. Turn on [Remove Background](/effects/remove-background/) for the camera clip. Set **Background** to **Keep** if you want the room to stay.
961	
962	2. Put the clip you want behind the person on a track in front of the camera clip, and select it.
963	
964	3. In the Clip tab's **Picture** sub-tab, open the **Behind Subject** section and tick **Behind subject**.
965	
966	</Steps>
967	
968	The section comes right after **Transform** and is shut by default, and its header reads "on" or "off". The box is off by default and shows as mixed over a selection that disagrees. Changing it is one undo step, **Behind Subject**, and **Reset** turns it off.
969	
970	With one clip selected and the box on, the section says "No cut-out clip is behind it at the playhead." when nothing cuts the clip there.
971	
972	With an [action](/motion/edit-an-action/) selected, the box sets the action's end, and the clip switches at the action's end. The row shows "at end".
973	
974	The section isn't offered while a nest is open.
975	
976	## What cuts the clip
977	
978	A clip with **Behind subject** on is cut, at every moment, by the subject of every cut-out clip on a track behind it. Any clip with Remove Background on counts, with **Background** set to **Remove** or **Keep**.
979	
980	Track order decides it. A cut-out clip on a track in front of the clip doesn't cut it.
981	
982	Where no mask is drawn yet, or no subject is found, the clip draws whole. See [How the masks are made](/effects/remove-background/#how-the-masks-are-made).
983	
984	## Good to know
985	
986	- A subject inside a nest cuts a top-level title when the nest clip is behind the title. A top-level camera never cuts a title inside a nest, because a nest is one picture to the timeline.
987	- The clip's [shadow](/effects/shadow/) is cut with it.
988	- A clip cut this way gets no [motion blur](/motion/motion-blur/). It draws sharp, and so does the outline that cuts it.
989	
990	## With an agent
991	
992	`text_behind_subject` does what the menu item does, and it can also take the title's text, its start time and the clip to go behind. It works on the top-level timeline only, and it leaves the selection as it was. An agent can also turn `behind_subject` on inside a nest with `set_video`, where the section isn't offered, and it works among the clips of that nest. See [Tools: text, shapes and clip names](/mcp/tools-clip-properties/#text_behind_subject) and [Tools: picture and grade](/mcp/tools-set-video/#behind_subject).
993	
994	## Related

997	- [Text clips](/text-and-shapes/text-clips/)

999	- [Matte tracks](/canvas/matte-tracks/)

1	=================== edit-text-on-canvas.mdx
2	---
3	title: Edit text on the canvas
4	description: Double-click a text clip in the preview to type into it, then apply, add new lines or back out.
5	---
6	
7	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
8	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
9	
10	You can type straight into a text clip in the preview, and see the words wrap where they'll sit in the picture.
11	
12	<AtAGlance
13	  keys={['Return', '⇧Return', 'Esc']}
14	  where="Double-click a text clip in the preview"
15	  tools="set_text"
16	/>
17	
18	## Type on the canvas
19	
20	<Steps>
21	
22	1. Move the playhead so the clip is on the canvas.
23	
24	2. Double-click the clip. The editor opens over it with all the text selected.
25	
26	3. Type. The editor grows and wraps as you go, the way the text will once applied.
27	
28	4. Press <kbd>Return</kbd> to apply.
29	
30	</Steps>
31	
32	The editor uses the clip's own font, tracking and line spacing at the canvas's zoom, so the lines break where they will in the picture. It draws in the interface's own colours, not the clip's, so you can always read what you're typing.
33	
34	**UPPERCASE** text shows as you typed it. A rotated clip's editor stays upright, and the text you apply is the same either way.
35	
36	Opening the editor leaves [crop mode](/canvas/crop/). Double-clicking any other kind of clip enters it.
37	
38	## Apply the text
39	
40	Any of these applies the text and closes the editor:
41	
42	- <kbd>Return</kbd> or keypad <kbd>Enter</kbd>
43	- <kbd>Tab</kbd>, unless Full Keyboard Access is on in System Settings
44	- A click elsewhere in the window, below its title bar
45	
46	Applying is one undo step, **Edit Text**. If the words haven't changed, there's no undo step. After <kbd>Return</kbd> the keys go back to the canvas, so its single-letter keys work again.
47	
48	## Start a new line
49	
50	<kbd>⇧Return</kbd>, <kbd>⌥Return</kbd>, <kbd>⌘Return</kbd> and <kbd>⌃Return</kbd> all start a new line. Caps Lock and <kbd>fn</kbd> don't count, so <kbd>Return</kbd> with either of those still applies.
51	
52	## Leave with Esc
53	
54	Over unchanged text, <kbd>Esc</kbd> closes the editor at once.
55	
56	Over changed text, a sheet asks "Apply your changes to this text?", and reminds you that "Return applies while you type; ⇧Return starts a new line."
57	
58	| Button | What it does |
59	| --- | --- |
60	| **Apply** | Keeps your text and closes the editor. It's the default, on <kbd>Return</kbd>. |
61	| **Revert** | Closes the editor and drops your changes. |
62	| **Cancel** | Goes back to editing. <kbd>Esc</kbd> in the sheet does the same. |
63	
64	While the sheet is up, clicking away doesn't apply the text behind your back.
65	
66	## Use an input method
67	
68	While an input method is composing, <kbd>Return</kbd>, keypad <kbd>Enter</kbd> and <kbd>Esc</kbd> go to the input method, not the editor. They do their usual jobs again once the composition ends.
69	
70	## Good to know
71	
72	- You can only double-click what's on the canvas, and a clip on a [locked track](/timeline/hide-and-lock-tracks/) can't be picked there. To change those words, use **Content** in the [Text sub-tab](/text-and-shapes/text-clips/#write-the-words).
73	- The editor always changes the clip's own words, even with an [action](/motion/actions/) selected. To change the words at an action's end, use **Content**.
74	- On a caption timed word by word, changing the number of words drops the page's timing. See [Text clips](/text-and-shapes/text-clips/#good-to-know).
75	
76	## Related
77	
78	- [Text clips](/text-and-shapes/text-clips/)
79	- [Font and text style](/text-and-shapes/text-style/)
80	- [Text box and wrapping](/text-and-shapes/text-box/)
81	=================== fonts.mdx
82	---
83	title: "Fonts"
84	description: "Which fonts a text clip can use, the faces Frame Job ships with, and what happens when a project's font isn't on this Mac."
85	---
86	
87	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
88	
89	A text clip can use any font installed on your Mac, or one of the faces that come with Frame Job. Both appear in the same list, so there's nothing to set up.
90	
91	<AtAGlance where="Clip tab ▸ Text ▸ Font ▸ Family" />
92	
93	To choose a font, see [Font and text style](/text-and-shapes/text-style/).
94	
95	## Fonts the app ships with
96	
97	These faces are always in the **Family** list. They need no installing, so a project that uses them draws the same on any Mac.
98	
99	| Family | Weights |
100	| --- | --- |
101	| Anton | Regular |
102	| Bebas Neue | Regular |
103	| Darker Grotesque | Light to Black |
104	| IBM Plex Mono | Regular, Medium |
105	| Montserrat | ExtraBold, Black |
106	| Source Sans 3 | ExtraLight to Black |
107	| Source Serif 4 | ExtraLight to Black |
108	
109	All seven are under the SIL Open Font License.
110	
111	## Installed fonts
112	
113	The **Family** list holds every font family on your Mac, in alphabetical order. Frame Job reads it once each time it launches, so a font you install while it's running appears after you quit and reopen it.
114	
115	## When a project's font is missing
116	
117	A project remembers a font by name and doesn't hold the font file. If you open it on a Mac without that font, the project still opens and the **Text** sub-tab still works.
118	
119	- macOS draws the text in a stand-in font.
120	- **Family** shows the first family in the list, which isn't the font the project asked for.
121	- Picking a **Family** or **Style** replaces the missing font on that clip.
122	
123	Until you pick something, the clip keeps the name of its font, so it draws correctly again once the font is installed.
124	
125	:::tip
126	For a project you'll open on more than one Mac, use a font Frame Job ships with, or install the same font on each Mac.
127	:::
128	
129	## Fonts in graphics
130	
131	Graphics work differently. A graphic draws only with the fonts Frame Job ships with and fonts you add to the project, never with the fonts installed on your Mac. A font Frame Job ships with is never packed into a `.fjgraphic` package, because every copy of the app already has it. See [Fonts and pictures in graphics](/graphics/fonts-and-pictures/).
132

138	=================== gradients.mdx
139	---
140	title: "Gradient fills"
141	description: "Fill a rectangle or ellipse with a linear or radial ramp of up to eight colours."
142	---
143	
144	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
145	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
146	
147	A gradient fills a rectangle or ellipse with a ramp of colours in place of a flat fill. Use one for a sky behind a title, or a plate that fades out at one side.
148	
149	<AtAGlance
150	  where="Clip tab ▸ Shape ▸ Gradient"
151	  tools="set_shape"
152	/>
153	
154	## Add a gradient
155	
156	<Steps>
157	
158	1. Select a rectangle or ellipse. The **Shape** sub-tab opens. If you don't have one yet, [add a shape clip](/text-and-shapes/shape-clips/#add-a-shape-clip).
159	
160	2. Open the **Gradient** section. It starts closed, and its header reads "off".
161	
162	3. Tick **Gradient**.
163	
164	4. Set the [kind](#kind), the [angle](#angle) and the colours of the [stops](#stops).
165	
166	</Steps>
167	
168	A new gradient is **Linear**, black to white, at 0°, so it runs from black on the left to white on the right. It's clipped to the shape, rounded corners included.
169	
170	Once it's on, the section's header reads the kind and the number of stops, such as "linear, 2 stops".
171	
172	### The fill and the stroke
173	
174	A gradient covers the [flat fill](/text-and-shapes/shape-settings/#fill-the-shape) but doesn't remove it, so the fill's rows stay live. While both are on, the section says "The gradient covers the Fill colour above; Reset brings it back."
175	
176	The stroke is drawn over the gradient in its own colour.
177	
178	### Turn it off
179	
180	Untick **Gradient** or choose **Reset** in the section's header. Either one brings the flat fill back, or leaves the shape hollow if it had none.
181	
182	Turning the gradient off forgets it. Ticking **Gradient** again starts over at black to white, so use **Edit ▸ Undo** to get a ramp back.
183	
184	## Kind
185	
186	| Kind | How the ramp runs |
187	| --- | --- |
188	| **Linear** | In a straight line across the shape, in the direction of **Angle**. The first and last positions land on the box's edges at every angle. |
189	| **Radial** | Outward from the centre of the box, in an ellipse with the box's proportions. 0 % is the centre and 100 % touches the middle of each side, so a rectangle's corners are past the end of the ramp. |
190	
191	**Kind** starts on **Linear**.
192	
193	## Angle
194	
195	**Angle** points a linear gradient. It runs from 0 to 360°, with quick picks every 45°, and it starts at 0°.
196	
197	0° runs to the right, and the angle turns counter-clockwise.
198	
199	| Angle | The ramp runs |
200	| --- | --- |
201	| 0° | Left to right |
202	| 90° | Bottom to top |
203	| 180° | Right to left |
204	| 270° | Top to bottom |
205	
206	A radial gradient has no direction, so **Angle** is greyed for **Radial**. It keeps its number for when you switch back to **Linear**.
207	
208	## Stops
209	
210	A stop is one colour at one place on the ramp. Each stop has a row, **Stop 1**, **Stop 2** and so on, with three controls.
211	
212	| Control | What it does | Range |
213	| --- | --- | --- |
214	| Swatch | The stop's colour. Lower its opacity in the colour panel to let what's behind show through. | |
215	| Position | How far along the ramp the stop sits. Quick picks 0, 25, 50, 75 and 100. | 0 to 100 % |
216	| **Remove** | Takes the stop off the ramp. Greyed at two stops, because a gradient keeps at least two. | |
217	
218	Rows keep their order when you change a position, so a stop can move past another one. Frame Job sorts the stops by position when it draws, so the order of the rows doesn't change the picture.
219	
220	Past the first and last stops, the end colours carry on to the shape's edge. A ramp whose stops sit at 40 % and 60 % is solid at both sides, with the change in the middle.
221	
222	### Add Stop
223	
224	**Add Stop** puts a new stop in the middle of the widest gap between two stops, in the colour the ramp already has there. The picture doesn't change until you recolour or move the new stop. When two gaps tie, it uses the one nearer 0 %. The new row goes just under the row of the stop at the gap's lower end.
225	
226	A gradient can have up to eight stops. The row says "8 at most", and **Add Stop** is greyed at eight or while the gradient is off.
227	
228	## Good to know
229	
230	- Lines and arrows have no area to fill. The section is greyed for them, and it says "Fills the rectangle or ellipse; a line or arrow keeps its stroke colour." A gradient isn't lost when you switch **Kind** to Line or Arrow, and it's there again when you switch back.
231	- A gradient can't be animated. Its rows always change the clip itself, even while an action is selected. See [Why shape colours don't animate](/text-and-shapes/shape-settings/#why-shape-colours-dont-animate).
232	- With several shapes selected, any change gives them all the same whole gradient, not only the row you changed.
233	- **Opacity** in the **Fill** section doesn't touch a gradient. Use each stop's colour, or **Opacity** in [Transform](/canvas/transform/) to fade the whole shape.
234	
235	## With an agent
236	
237	`set_shape` sets a gradient through its `gradient` key, which holds `kind`, `angle` and `stops`. Each stop is a colour and an `at` from 0 to 1, where the inspector shows 0 to 100 %. Sending `stops` replaces them all, and fewer than 2 or more than 8 is an error that names the count. `{gradient: null}` brings the flat fill back. See [Tools: text, shapes and clip names](/mcp/tools-clip-properties/).
238	
239	## Related
240	
241	- [Shape fill, stroke and size](/text-and-shapes/shape-settings/)
242	- [Shape clips](/text-and-shapes/shape-clips/)
243	- [Backgrounds](/canvas/backgrounds/)
244	=================== image-clips.mdx
245	---
246	title: "Image clips"
247	description: "Put a still picture on the timeline, set how long it stays, and use the same Picture and Color controls as a video clip."
248	---
249	
250	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
251	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
252	
253	An image clip puts a still picture on the timeline: a logo, a photo, a screenshot. It draws like a video clip but has no length of its own, so you decide how long it stays.
254	
255	<AtAGlance
256	  where={['Media tab ▸ drag a picture onto a track or the canvas', 'Clip tab ▸ Picture', 'Clip tab ▸ Color']}
257	  tools={['import_media', 'add_clip']}
258	/>
259	
260	## Place an image
261	
262	<Steps>
263	
264	1. [Import](/projects/import-media/) the picture the way you'd import a movie, with **File ▸ Add Media…** or by dropping it on the Media tab.
265	
266	2. Drag its row onto a track, or onto the preview canvas.
267	
268	</Steps>
269	
270	The picture lands as a five-second clip. A drop on a track puts it at the pointer, and a drop on the canvas puts it at the playhead on a new track in front. See [Add clips to the timeline](/editing/add-clips/) for what stops a drop, and [Insert and overwrite](/editing/insert-and-overwrite/) to make room for it.
271	
272	The picture formats Frame Job can read, and how each one comes in, are on [Supported file formats](/reference/file-formats/).
273	
274	## Length
275	
276	An image clip starts at 5 seconds. A picture has no end to run out of, so you can [trim](/editing/trimming/) it to any length, down to one frame. Drag either edge on the timeline, or type a time into **In** or **Out** in the **Timing** section of the **Clip** sub-tab.
277	
278	There's no footage to retime or turn around, so the **Clip** sub-tab has no **Speed** section and **Timing** has no **Reverse** row.
279	
280	## Starting size
281	
282	A picture bigger than the canvas on either side starts scaled down so all of it shows, while the Document tab's **Fit new clips to canvas** option is on, which it is by default. With the option off it starts at 100 %, its native size, and runs past the edges of the canvas.
283	
284	A picture the same size as the canvas or smaller starts at 100 % either way, because the option never scales a clip up. See [Fit new clips to canvas](/projects/background-and-timecode/#fit-new-clips-to-canvas).
285	
286	## Picture sections
287	
288	An image clip has three sub-tabs: **Picture**, **Color** and **Clip**. There's no **Sound** sub-tab, because a picture has no sound.
289	
290	The **Picture** sub-tab has these sections, in this order:
291	
292	- [Transform](/canvas/transform/)
293	- [Behind Subject](/effects/text-behind-subject/), on the top-level timeline only, so not while a nest is open
294	- [Hide While Silent](/effects/hide-while-silent/)
295	- [Crop](/canvas/crop/)
296	- [Corner Radius](/canvas/corner-radius/)
297	- [Chroma Key](/effects/chroma-key/)
298	- [Background](/effects/remove-background/), which is Remove Background
299	- [Shadow](/effects/shadow/)
300	- [Filters](/effects/filters/)
301	- [Reflection](/effects/reflection/)
302	- [Spotlight](/effects/spotlight/)
303	- [Obscure](/effects/obscure/)
304	
305	That's everything a video clip has but two. The **Layout** section is for a movie clip and the **Cursor** section for a screen recording, so neither shows here.
306	
307	Remove Background works on a picture too, keeping its person or its foreground subject. A picture gets a **Subject** row to choose between them. See [Remove Background](/effects/remove-background/).
308	
309	The [**Color** sub-tab](/color/color-tab/) grades a picture as it grades a movie, with **Light**, **Color**, **Wheels**, **Curves** and **Look**.
310	
311	The **Clip** sub-tab has **Timing** and **Motion presets**, plus **Transition** when the clip overlaps the one before it. To give a still some movement, use a [motion preset](/motion/motion-presets/) or an [action](/motion/actions/).
312	
313	## Good to know
314	
315	- An animated GIF or WebP shows its first frame only.
316	- A picture with transparency keeps it, so what's behind shows through.
317	- A picture more than 8,192 px on its long side is read at 8,192 px.
318	- Opening a PNG, JPEG or HEIC picture with **File ▸ Open…** builds a new project around it instead of adding it to the one you have open. See [Open a project](/projects/open-a-project/).
319	
320	## With an agent
321	
322	`import_media` adds the picture to the media list and `add_clip` places it, five seconds long at the size above. See [Tools: media](/mcp/tools-media/) and [Tools: adding clips](/mcp/tools-adding-clips/).
323	
324	## Related
325	
326	- [Import media](/projects/import-media/)
327	- [Add clips to the timeline](/editing/add-clips/)
328	- [The Picture tab](/canvas/picture-tab/)
329	- [Motion presets](/motion/motion-presets/)
330	- [Supported file formats](/reference/file-formats/)
331	=================== lines-and-arrows.mdx
332	---
333	title: "Lines and arrows"
334	description: "Aim a line or arrow by dragging its ends on the canvas, and put a head on either end."
335	---
336	
337	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
338	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
339	
340	A line or arrow has two ends you can place by hand. Use them to point at a button, underline a word or connect two things on screen.
341	
342	<AtAGlance
343	  where={['Drag a round end handle on the canvas', 'Clip tab ▸ Shape ▸ Arrowheads']}
344	  tools="set_shape"
345	/>
346	
347	To add one, see [Shape clips](/text-and-shapes/shape-clips/#add-a-shape-clip).
348	
349	## Drag an endpoint
350	
351	<Steps>
352	
353	1. Select the line or arrow, with the playhead over it.
354	
355	2. Drag the round handle at either end.
356	
357	</Steps>
358	
359	Only that end moves. The other end stays where it is, and so does the shape's box. The drag is one undo step, "Move Endpoint". Press <kbd>Esc</kbd> during the drag to put the end back, with no undo step.
360	
361	A new line or arrow runs from the bottom-left corner of its box to the top-right corner. The start is the bottom-left end, and the end is the top-right one.
362	
363	## How the box limits an end
364	
365	An end lives inside the shape's box, so it stops at the box's edge however far you drag. To take an end further, make the box bigger first, with the square handles or with **Width** and **Height** in the [Shape section](/text-and-shapes/shape-settings/#set-the-size).
366	
367	An end is kept as a place in the box, not a place on the canvas. When you resize the box, the line stretches with it and each end keeps its place. Rotating the box with the rotation grip turns the line.
368	
369	The edge is also the easy way to get a level line. Drag both ends past the same edge of the box and they stop exactly in line. Nothing draws outside the box, though, so a line along its edge shows only half its stroke.
370	
371	The square handles and the rotation grip work on a line's box as they do on any shape. See [Resize with the handles](/text-and-shapes/shape-clips/#resize-with-the-handles).
372	
373	:::note
374	When an end sits on a corner of the box, its round handle covers the square one there and takes the click. On a new line that's the bottom-left and top-right corners, so use one of the other two corners or a side handle to resize.
375	:::
376	
377	## Set its arrowheads
378	
379	Tick **Arrowhead at start**, **Arrowhead at end** or both in the **Arrowheads** section of the **Shape** sub-tab. A head shows only when **Kind** is **Arrow**, so a Line keeps its boxes ticked but draws no head. The rows are covered on [Shape fill, stroke and size](/text-and-shapes/shape-settings/#add-arrowheads).
380	
381	A head's tip sits exactly on the end, and the line stops at the head's base. A head's length and its width are each four times the stroke's width, so a 6 px stroke gives a head 24 px long and 24 px wide. It takes the stroke's colour.
382	
383	## Good to know
384	
385	- An end can only be placed on the canvas. There's no field for it in the inspector.
386	- An end doesn't snap to the canvas, its centre or other clips.
387	- An [action](/motion/actions/) can't move an end. With an action selected, dragging an end still changes the clip itself. An action can move, scale, rotate or fade the whole line through [Transform](/canvas/transform/).
388	- With several clips selected, only the front-most selected clip shows handles.
389	- A clip on a [locked track](/timeline/hide-and-lock-tracks/) shows no handles.
390	
391	## With an agent
392	
393	An agent can place both ends exactly and set both heads in one `set_shape` call, with `from`, `to`, `arrow_start` and `arrow_end`. An end is two numbers measured across the box, where `[0, 0]` is the top-left corner and `[1, 1]` the bottom-right, so a new line runs from `[0, 1]` to `[1, 0]`. See [Tools: text, shapes and clip names](/mcp/tools-clip-properties/).
394	
395	## Related
396

400	=================== shape-clips.mdx
401	---
402	title: "Shape clips"
403	description: "Add a rectangle, ellipse, line or arrow at the playhead, and resize its box on the canvas."
404	---
405	
406	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
407	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
408	import Shot from '@components/Shot.astro';
409	
410	A shape clip draws a rectangle, an ellipse, a line or an arrow over your video. Use one to frame something, point at it, or put a plate behind a title.
411	
412	<AtAGlance
413	  where={['Add Shape in the timeline bar', 'Clip tab ▸ Shape', 'Drag a shape\'s handles on the canvas']}
414	  tools={['add_shape_clip', 'set_shape']}
415	/>
416	
417	<Shot
418	  name="08-clip-shape.window"
419	  alt="The editor with an ellipse shape clip selected. In the preview a white ellipse outline has an orange frame with handles and a rotation handle, the Ellipse clip is outlined in the timeline, and the inspector shows the Shape sub-tab."
420	/>
421	
422	## Add a shape clip
423	
424	<Steps>
425	
426	1. Move the playhead to where the shape should start.
427	
428	2. Click **Add Shape** in the timeline bar.
429	
430	3. Choose **Rectangle**, **Ellipse**, **Line** or **Arrow**.
431	
432	</Steps>
433	
434	**Add Shape** has no menu item and no key. **Clip ▸ Add Background ▸ Solid Color** also makes a shape clip, a white rectangle the canvas's size on a new track at the back. See [Backgrounds](/canvas/backgrounds/).
435	
436	The shape goes on the front-most track if there's room at the playhead, and otherwise on a new track in front of everything. With a [nest](/editing/nests/) open, it goes in the nest. Adding it is one undo step, named after the kind, such as "Add Rectangle".
437	
438	A new shape:
439	
440	- lasts 5 seconds, and has no source file, so you can [trim](/editing/trimming/) it to any length
441	- is a 320 × 120 px box with a 6 px white stroke and no fill, so it shows up over any footage
442	- is selected, so the **Shape** sub-tab opens on it
443	
444	Everything about how it's drawn is on [Shape fill, stroke and size](/text-and-shapes/shape-settings/).
445	
446	## The four kinds
447	
448	You can change a shape's kind at any time with [**Kind**](/text-and-shapes/shape-settings/#change-the-kind).
449	
450	### Rectangle
451	
452	A rectangle that fills its box. A rounded rectangle is a Rectangle with a [corner radius](/text-and-shapes/shape-settings/#round-a-rectangles-corners), not a separate kind.
453	
454	### Ellipse
455	
456	An ellipse that fills its box. Make the box square for a circle.
457	
458	### Line
459	
460	A straight line. A new line runs diagonally across its box, from bottom left to top right. Drag the round handle at either end to move that end. See [Lines and arrows](/text-and-shapes/lines-and-arrows/).
461	
462	### Arrow
463	
464	A line with an arrowhead. A new arrow runs diagonally across its box like a line, with its head at the end turned on.
465	
466	## Resize with the handles
467	
468	Dragging a shape's handle changes the size of its box, not a scale factor, so the stroke stays the same thickness. The box's new size shows in the **Width** and **Height** fields.
469	
470	| Gesture | What it does |
471	| --- | --- |
472	| Drag a corner handle | Resizes the box and keeps its aspect ratio. |
473	| <kbd>⇧</kbd>-drag a corner handle | Frees the aspect ratio, so width and height move independently. |
474	| Drag a side handle | Changes only the width or only the height. |
475	| <kbd>⌥</kbd>-drag a handle | Resizes about the centre rather than pinning the opposite handle. |
476	
477	The drag holds each side of the box between 4 and 20,000 px.
478	
479	<kbd>⇧</kbd> is special to shapes here. A video or picture has one uniform scale, so <kbd>⇧</kbd> changes nothing on those. For the rest of the canvas gestures, see [Move, scale and rotate](/canvas/move-scale-rotate/).
480	
481	A box resize always changes the clip itself, even with an [action](/motion/actions/) selected. To animate a shape's size, use **Scale** in the [Transform](/canvas/transform/) section, which enlarges the whole drawing, stroke included.
482	
483	## Picture sections
484	
485	A shape clip has three sub-tabs: **Shape**, **Picture** and **Clip**. Its **Picture** sub-tab has these sections, in this order:
486	
487	- [Transform](/canvas/transform/)
488	- [Behind Subject](/effects/text-behind-subject/), on the top-level timeline only, so not while a nest is open
489	- [Hide While Silent](/effects/hide-while-silent/)
490	- [Shadow](/effects/shadow/)
491	- [Filters](/effects/filters/)
492	- [Reflection](/effects/reflection/)
493	- [Spotlight](/effects/spotlight/)
494	- [Obscure](/effects/obscure/)
495	
496	Crop, Corner Radius, Chroma Key and Background aren't offered, and neither is the **Color** sub-tab. To round a shape's corners, use **Corner radius** on the **Shape** sub-tab.
497	
498	## With an agent
499	
500	`add_shape_clip` puts a shape on the track and at the time you name, and can give it its length and look in the same step. It can also make a shape larger than the canvas, which starts scaled to fit when [**Fit new clips to canvas**](/projects/background-and-timecode/#fit-new-clips-to-canvas) is on. An arrow starts with its head on, so pass `arrow_end: false` for a bare diagonal. See [Tools: adding clips](/mcp/tools-adding-clips/#add_shape_clip).
501

510	---
511	title: "Shape fill, stroke and size"
512	description: "Change a shape's kind and box, round its corners, set its stroke and fill, and add arrowheads on the Shape sub-tab."
513	---
514	
515	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
516	import Shot from '@components/Shot.astro';
517	
518	The **Shape** sub-tab sets what a [shape clip](/text-and-shapes/shape-clips/) is and how it's painted. Where it sits, how large it's scaled and how see-through it is as a whole are on the **Picture** sub-tab, in [Transform](/canvas/transform/).
519	
520	<AtAGlance where="Clip tab ▸ Shape" tools="set_shape" />
521	
522	<Shot
523	  name="08-clip-shape.inspector"
524	  alt="The Shape sub-tab for an ellipse. The Shape section is open with Kind set to Ellipse, Width 320 px, Height 120 px and a dimmed Corner radius at 0 px. Below it the closed sections read Stroke 6.0 px, Fill off, Gradient off and Arrowheads none."
525	/>
526	
527	## Change the kind
528	
529	**Kind** switches the shape between **Rectangle**, **Ellipse**, **Line** and **Arrow**. It changes only the kind, so everything else stays as it was.
530	
531	Rows that don't apply to the new kind are greyed, not lost, so flipping the kind back finds them as you left them.
532	
533	| Row | Available for |
534	| --- | --- |
535	| **Corner radius** | Rectangle |
536	| The **Gradient** section | Rectangle, Ellipse |
537	| The **Arrowheads** section | Line, Arrow |
538	
539	A shape switched to **Arrow** keeps its own arrowhead setting, so a rectangle switched to Arrow has no head until you tick one. Only a shape added as an Arrow starts with a head.
540	
541	## Set the size
542	
543	**Width** and **Height** set the shape's box in pixels, from 1 to 20,000 px each. A new shape is 320 × 120 px. A number typed outside the range is brought back to the nearest limit. However large the box is, a shape is drawn at no more than 8,192 px on a side.
544	
545	[Dragging a handle](/text-and-shapes/shape-clips/#resize-with-the-handles) on the canvas changes the same two numbers. **Scale** in [Transform](/canvas/transform/) is different: it enlarges the finished drawing, stroke included.
546	
547	## Round a rectangle's corners
548	
549	**Corner radius** rounds a rectangle's corners, from 0 to 2,000 px, with quick picks at 0, 4, 8, 16, 32 and 64. The default is 0. It's greyed for other kinds.
550	
551	A radius can't go past half the box's shorter side. At that point the short ends are fully round, and a larger number looks the same.
552	
553	The **Shape** section's **Reset** puts the corner radius back to 0, and leaves the kind and the box alone.
554	
555	## Draw an outline
556	
557	The **Stroke** section draws an outline around the shape. A new shape has one.
558	
559	| Control | What it does | Default | Range |
560	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
561	| **Stroke** | Turns the outline on or off. | On | |
562	| **Width** | How thick it is. Quick picks 1, 2, 4, 6, 12 and 24. | 6 px | 0.5 to 200 px |
563	| **Color** | Its colour. | White | |
564	
565	**Width** and **Color** are greyed while the stroke is off. Turning the stroke off forgets its width and colour, so turning it on again gives 6 px white. **Reset** also goes back to 6 px white rather than turning the stroke off.
566	
567	On a rectangle or ellipse the stroke sits inside the box, so a thicker stroke doesn't make the shape bigger.
568	
569	When the section is folded, its header reads the width, such as "6.0 px", or "off".
570	
571	## Fill the shape
572	
573	The **Fill** section paints the inside of a rectangle or ellipse with a flat colour. A new shape has no fill.
574	
575	| Control | What it does | Default | Range |
576	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
577	| **Fill** | Turns the fill on or off. | Off | |
578	| **Color** | The fill's colour. | White, once turned on | |
579	| **Opacity** | How solid the fill is. Quick picks 0, 25, 50, 75 and 100. | 100 % | 0 to 100 % |
580	
581	**Color** and **Opacity** are greyed while the fill is off. Turning the fill off forgets its colour, so turning it on again gives opaque white. **Reset** turns the fill off.
582	
583	**Opacity** belongs to the fill alone, so it doesn't fade the stroke. To fade the whole shape, use **Opacity** in [Transform](/canvas/transform/).
584	
585	When the section is folded, its header reads the fill's opacity, such as "100%", or "off".
586	
587	For a colour ramp in place of a flat colour, see [Gradient fills](/text-and-shapes/gradients/). A gradient covers the fill while it's on, and turning it off brings the fill back.
588	
589	## Add arrowheads
590	
591	The **Arrowheads** section has two separate boxes, **Arrowhead at start** and **Arrowhead at end**. They're available for lines and arrows, and greyed for rectangles and ellipses.
592	
593	:::note
594	Arrowheads are drawn only when **Kind** is **Arrow**. On a Line you can tick the boxes and they're kept, but no head appears until you switch the kind to Arrow.
595	:::
596	
597	When the section is folded, its header reads "both", "start", "end" or "none". See [Lines and arrows](/text-and-shapes/lines-and-arrows/) for moving the ends.
598	
599	A line or arrow is drawn with its stroke, so a Line with **Stroke** off shows nothing. **Fill** paints nothing on a line or arrow, although its rows stay available. The one exception is an Arrow with **Stroke** off, whose heads take the fill colour.
600	
601	## Why shape colours don't animate
602	
603	An [action](/motion/actions/) can't change a shape's kind, stroke, fill, gradient or arrowheads. These rows always change the clip itself, even while an action is selected, and they're marked ⊘ to show it.
604	
605	A shape's position, scale and opacity animate like any clip's. To move or fade a shape, select an action and use the [Transform](/canvas/transform/) rows on the **Picture** sub-tab. See [What an action can animate](/motion/what-can-animate/).
606	
607	## With an agent
608	
609	`set_shape` changes any of these settings in one call and leaves the rest as they are, including a line's two ends. Setting `stroke` or `fill` to `null` removes it. A shape's position and scale aren't part of it: those go through `set_video`. To change a shape inside a nest, see [Editing inside a nest](/mcp/nests/). For every key, see [Tools: text, shapes and clip names](/mcp/tools-clip-properties/#set_shape).
610	
611	## Related

615	- [Gradient fills](/text-and-shapes/gradients/)

617	=================== text-box.mdx
618	---
619	title: "Text box and wrapping"
620	description: "Let a text clip's box fit its words, or set a width and have the words wrap, from the inspector or by dragging on the canvas."
621	---
622	
623	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
624	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
625	
626	A text clip's box decides where its lines break. By default the box fits the words, and only your own line breaks start a new line. Give it a fixed width and the words wrap to fit.
627	
628	<AtAGlance
629	  where={['Clip tab ▸ Text ▸ Box', 'Drag a text clip\'s left or right handle on the canvas']}
630	  tools="set_text"
631	/>
632	
633	## Wrap text at a width
634	
635	<Steps>
636	
637	1. Select the text clip.
638	
639	2. In the inspector's **Clip** tab, open the **Box** section of the **Text** sub-tab.
640	
641	3. Set **Mode** to **Fixed width**. The width starts at 60 % of the canvas width, which is 1,152 px on a 1920-wide canvas.
642	
643	4. Type a **Width**, or drag a [side handle](#drag-the-width-on-the-canvas) on the canvas.
644	
645	</Steps>
646	
647	To go back, set **Mode** to **Auto-size** or choose the section's **Reset**.
648	
649	## The Box section
650	
651	| Control | What it does | Default | Range |
652	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
653	| **Mode** | **Auto-size** lays the text out without wrapping, so the box fits the words. **Fixed width** wraps the words at **Width**. | Auto-size | |
654	| **Width** | The width the words wrap at. It's greyed in Auto-size. | 60 % of the canvas width | 20 to 20,000 px |
655	
656	A number typed outside the range is brought back to the nearest limit. When the section is folded, its header reads "auto", or the width, such as "1152 px".
657	
658	## Drag the width on the canvas
659	
660	Drag a text clip's left or right handle in the preview to set its wrap width. If the box was on Auto-size, it becomes **Fixed width**, starting from the box's current width.
661	
662	The text stays centred on the same point and grows both ways, whichever handle you drag. The drag holds the width between 4 and 20,000 px, so it can go narrower than the 20 px the **Width** field lets you type.
663	
664	The other handles do something different. The corners and the top and bottom handles scale the text uniformly and leave the wrap width alone. See [Move, scale and rotate](/canvas/move-scale-rotate/).
665	
666	## What a fixed width changes
667	
668	- **The height follows the lines.** A fixed width sets only the width, and the box grows taller as the text wraps onto more lines.
669	- **Alignment works across the whole width.** Left, centre and right [alignment](/text-and-shapes/text-style/) line the words up against the width you set, not against the longest line.
670	- **A backdrop fills the whole box.** A [backdrop](/text-and-shapes/text-outline-and-backdrop/) is as wide as **Width** plus its padding, even when the words are shorter. **Width** measures the words, and the padding sits outside it.
671	
672	## Good to know
673	
674	- In Auto-size a long line never wraps, so it can run off the canvas. Press <kbd>⇧Return</kbd> in the [text area](/text-and-shapes/text-clips/) to start a new line yourself.
675	- Text is drawn at no more than 8,192 px on a side, so a box stops growing there whatever **Width** says.
676	- With an [action](/motion/edit-an-action/) selected, **Mode**, **Width** and the side handles set the action's end, like any other text property.
677	
678	## With an agent
679	
680	`set_text` sets the box through `width`: a wrap width in pixels, or `null` to go back to Auto-size. See [Tools: text, shapes and clip names](/mcp/tools-clip-properties/#set_text).
681	
682	## Related

688	=================== text-clips.mdx
689	---
690	title: Text clips
691	description: Add a title to the timeline, type its words, and see what else a text clip can do.
692	---
693	
694	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
695	import Shot from '@components/Shot.astro';
696	
697	A text clip puts words on the canvas: a title, a name strap, a line of explanation. It sits on a track like any other clip, and it has no source file behind it.
698	
699	<AtAGlance
700	  keys="T"
701	  where={['The Add Text button in the timeline bar', 'Clip tab ▸ Text ▸ Content']}
702	  tools={['add_text_clip', 'set_text']}
703	/>
704	
705	<Shot
706	  name="06-clip-text.window"
707	  alt="A title reading Frame Job selected in the preview, with an orange frame and handles around it. Its clip is outlined in the timeline, and the inspector's Clip tab is open on the Text sub-tab."
708	/>
709	
710	## Add a text clip
711	
712	Press <kbd>T</kbd>, or click **Add Text** in the timeline bar, the **Aa** button. There's no menu item for it.
713	
714	The new clip reads "Title" in Source Sans 3 Bold at 72 px, in white, centred on the canvas, and it lasts 5 seconds. For a look sized to your canvas, use a [preset](/text-and-shapes/text-presets/).
715	
716	It lands at the playhead on the front-most track if it fits there, and on a new track in front of everything if it doesn't. Either way it's one undo step, **Add Text**. With a [nest](/editing/nests/) open, the front-most track is the nest's own.
717	
718	The clip comes in selected, so the canvas shows its handles and the **Clip** tab opens on its **Text** sub-tab. If the inspector is showing **Transcript** or **Assistant**, it stays there.
719	
720	## Change the length
721	
722	Five seconds is only where a text clip starts. With no source file to run out of, you can [trim](/editing/trimming/) it to any length.
723	
724	## Write the words
725	
726	There are two places to type:
727	
728	- **On the canvas.** Double-click the clip in the preview. See [Edit text on the canvas](/text-and-shapes/edit-text-on-canvas/).
729	- **In the inspector.** Select the clip and use the **Content** section at the top of the **Text** sub-tab. It's the one Text section that starts open. Its header shows the first line of the text, or "empty".
730	
731	In the **Content** box:
732	
733	| Key | What it does |
734	| --- | --- |
735	| <kbd>Return</kbd> | Applies the text, and the single-letter shortcuts work again |
736	| <kbd>Tab</kbd> | Applies the text the same way, unless Full Keyboard Access is on in System Settings |
737	| <kbd>⇧Return</kbd>, <kbd>⌘Return</kbd>, <kbd>⌥Return</kbd> or <kbd>⌃Return</kbd> | Starts a new line |
738	
739	A click elsewhere in the window, below its title bar, applies the text too. Changing the words is one undo step, **Edit Text**. If they haven't changed, there's no undo step.
740	
741	With an [action](/motion/actions/) selected, **Content** sets the words at that action's end. Words don't ease from one to another, so the text switches when the action ends.
742	
743	## Style the clip
744	
745	The **Text** sub-tab has the rest of a clip's look, and each section has its own page:
746	
747	| Section | Page |
748	| --- | --- |
749	| **Font** and **Style** | [Font and text style](/text-and-shapes/text-style/) |
750	| **Outline** and **Backdrop** | [Text outline and backdrop](/text-and-shapes/text-outline-and-backdrop/) |
751	| **Box** | [Text box and wrapping](/text-and-shapes/text-box/) |
752	| **Reveal** | [Text reveals](/text-and-shapes/text-reveal/) |
753	| **Presets** | [Text presets](/text-and-shapes/text-presets/) |
754	
755	The sub-tab shows only when every selected clip is a text clip. With several selected, a change goes to all of them.
756	
757	## Place it and add effects
758	
759	A text clip also has a **Picture** sub-tab, with these sections in this order:
760	
761	- [Transform](/canvas/transform/), for position, scale, rotation and opacity
762	- [Behind Subject](/effects/text-behind-subject/), which isn't shown while a nest is open
763	- [Hide While Silent](/effects/hide-while-silent/)
764	- [Shadow](/effects/shadow/)
765	- [Filters](/effects/filters/)
766	- [Reflection](/effects/reflection/)
767	- [Spotlight](/effects/spotlight/)
768	- [Obscure](/effects/obscure/)
769	
770	Crop, Corner Radius, Chroma Key and Background aren't offered, because they work on a clip's source pixels. A text clip has no **Color** or **Sound** sub-tab.
771	
772	## With an agent
773	
774	`add_text_clip` needs a track and a time. It can also set the length, 5 seconds if left out, and the words and the whole look in the same call. Unlike <kbd>T</kbd>, it doesn't fall back to a new track: if the clip would overlap another, Frame Job won't add it.
775	
776	`set_text` changes any mix of a clip's words and typography in one undo step. An agent isn't held to the ranges of the inspector's fields, so a size above 800 px is fine, for example. Position and scale go through `set_video`. Word timings sent for a caption must match its number of words, or the call fails and gives both numbers. See [Tools: adding clips](/mcp/tools-adding-clips/) and [Tools: text, shapes and clip names](/mcp/tools-clip-properties/).
777	
778	## Good to know
779	
780	A caption is a text clip too. If one is timed word by word, editing it keeps the timings while the number of words stays the same. Change the number of words and it loses its timing, so its words no longer change as they're spoken, and **Content** notes "Not timed — regenerate to time it again". See [Captions are text clips](/captions/how-captions-work/) and [Edit captions](/captions/edit-captions/).
781	
782	## Related

786	- [Text presets](/text-and-shapes/text-presets/)

788	=================== text-outline-and-backdrop.mdx
789	---
790	title: Text outline and backdrop
791	description: Draw a stroke around a text clip's letters, or put a rounded plate behind them, so the words stay readable over any picture.
792	---
793	
794	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
795	
796	White words get lost over a bright shot. An outline draws a stroke around each letter, and a backdrop puts a rounded plate behind the whole text. You can use either or both.
797	
798	<AtAGlance
799	  where={['Clip tab ▸ Text ▸ Outline', 'Clip tab ▸ Text ▸ Backdrop']}
800	  tools="set_text"
801	/>
802	
803	## Add an outline
804	
805	Select a text clip, click the **Outline** header in the **Text** sub-tab to open the section, and tick **Outline**. You get a 2 px black stroke.
806	
807	| Control | What it does | Default | Range |
808	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
809	| **Width** | The stroke's thickness. Quick picks: 1, 2, 4 and 8. | 2 px | 0 to 40 px |
810	| **Color** | The stroke's colour | Black | |
811	
812	Both are greyed while the outline is off. The section's header shows the width, or "off".
813	
814	The stroke sits on the edge of each letter, half inside and half outside, so a wide outline thins the letters.
815	
816	**Reset** in the section's header turns the outline off.
817	
818	## Add a backdrop
819	
820	Click the **Backdrop** header to open the section, and tick **Backdrop**. You get a black plate at 60 % opacity.
821	
822	| Control | What it does | Default | Range |
823	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
824	| **Fill** | The plate's colour and opacity | Black at 60 % | |
825	| **Padding** | The space between the text and the plate's edge. Quick picks: 0, 8, 12, 24 and 48. | 12 px | 0 to 200 px |
826	| **Radius** | How round the corners are. Quick picks: 0, 4, 8, 16 and 32. | 8 px | 0 to 200 px |
827	
828	All three are greyed while the backdrop is off. The section's header shows the padding, or "off".
829	
830	A radius can't go past half the plate's shorter side, so a large radius makes a pill shape and goes no further.
831	
832	**Reset** in the section's header turns the backdrop off.
833	
834	## Change them during a clip
835	
836	With an [action](/motion/actions/) selected, these controls set the look at that action's end. **Width**, **Padding**, **Radius** and the colours ease towards the new value, and colours [blend in OKLab](/motion/what-can-animate/#colours-blend-in-oklab). Turning an outline or a backdrop on or off switches when the action ends.
837	
838	## With an agent
839	
840	`set_text` sets both. `outline` takes `width` and `color`, and `backdrop` takes `color`, `padding` and `radius`. Send `null` for either to turn it off. An agent isn't held to the ranges above: a width, padding or radius only has to be 0 or more. See [Tools: text, shapes and clip names](/mcp/tools-clip-properties/).
841	
842	## Good to know
843	
844	- Turning an outline or a backdrop off forgets its settings. Turn it on again and it's back to the defaults.
845	- Both make the clip's box bigger. The margin around the words is whichever is larger, the outline's width or the backdrop's padding, not the two added together. The plate fills that whole box.
846	- During a [reveal](/text-and-shapes/text-reveal/), the backdrop is there at full strength from the first frame, and the words arrive on it. An outline comes and goes with its letters.
847

853	=================== text-presets.mdx
854	---
855	title: Text presets
856	description: Give a text clip a ready-made Title, Subtitle, Lower Third or Caption look, sized to your canvas.
857	---
858	
859	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
860	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
861	
862	A preset gives a text clip a finished look with one click: its font, size, alignment, backdrop and position, sized to fit your canvas.
863	
864	<AtAGlance
865	  where="Clip tab ▸ Text ▸ Presets"
866	  tools={['set_text', 'set_video']}
867	/>
868	
869	## Apply a preset
870	
871	<Steps>
872	
873	1. Select one or more text clips.
874	
875	2. Open the **Presets** section at the bottom of the **Text** sub-tab. It starts folded.
876	
877	3. Click **Title**, **Subtitle**, **Lower Third** or **Caption**.
878	
879	</Steps>
880	
881	It's one undo step, named after the preset.
882	
883	## The four presets
884	
885	| Preset | Font | Size | At 1920 × 1080 | Align | Position | Backdrop |
886	| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
887	| **Title** | Source Sans 3 Bold | 9 % | 97 px | Centre | Centre of the canvas | None |
888	| **Subtitle** | Source Sans 3 SemiBold | 5 % | 54 px | Centre | 18 % of the height below centre | None |
889	| **Lower Third** | Source Sans 3 SemiBold | 4.5 % | 49 px | Left | 20 % of the width left of centre, 28 % of the height below it | Black at 55 %, padding 18 px, radius 6 px |
890	| **Caption** | Source Sans 3 Regular | 3.5 % | 38 px | Centre | 38 % of the height below centre | Black at 60 %, padding 12 px, radius 8 px |
891	
892	The position is where the centre of the text's box sits, so a longer name on a **Lower Third** grows both ways from that point.
893	
894	**Title** isn't the look a new text clip starts with. That has the same font at a fixed 72 px, where **Title** works its size out from the canvas.
895	
896	On a canvas taller than wide, **Caption** sits higher, a quarter of the height below centre, clear of a phone's on-screen controls.
897	
898	[Subtitles](/captions/subtitles/) from **File ▸ Generate Captions…** and **File ▸ Import Captions…** use the **Caption** look, and they also wrap at 80 % of the canvas width. The **Caption** button itself leaves the [box](/text-and-shapes/text-box/) as it is.
899	
900	## How a preset fits the canvas
901	
902	Sizes are a share of the canvas's shorter side, and positions a share of its width and height. So a preset fits any canvas, and a vertical 1080 × 1920 canvas gets the same text height as a 1920 × 1080 one. A backdrop's padding and radius stay at the pixel values in the table.
903	
904	The size is worked out once, from the canvas at the moment you click. Changing the canvas afterwards doesn't apply the preset again.
905	
906	## What a preset changes
907	
908	As well as the settings in the table, a preset sets **Vertical** to middle and **Opacity** back to 100 %. **Title** and **Subtitle** take away any backdrop.
909	
910	It leaves everything else alone, including the words, the colour, the outline, tracking, line spacing, **UPPERCASE**, the box, the reveal, scale and rotation.
911	
912	With an [action](/motion/actions/) selected, a preset sets that action's end, like any other field.
913	
914	## With an agent
915	
916	There's no preset tool. An agent sends the same values through `set_text` and `set_video`. See [Tools: text, shapes and clip names](/mcp/tools-clip-properties/).
917	
918	## Related

923	=================== text-reveal.mdx
924	---
925	title: "Text reveals"
926	description: "Make a text clip type on, fade in word by word or rise in line by line, and set how long it takes to arrive and leave."
927	---
928	
929	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
930	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
931	
932	A reveal decides how a text clip's words arrive and leave. It runs from the clip's own first and last frames, so it needs no [action](/motion/actions/) and it moves with the clip.
933	
934	<AtAGlance where="Clip tab ▸ Text ▸ Reveal" tools="set_text" />
935	
936	## Add a reveal
937	
938	<Steps>
939	
940	1. Select the text clip.
941	
942	2. In the inspector's **Clip** tab, open the **Reveal** section of the **Text** sub-tab.
943	
944	3. Choose **Typewriter**, **Word Fade** or **Line Rise** from the **Reveal** pop-up.
945	
946	4. Set [**In** and **Out**](#set-how-long-it-takes) if you want something other than one second in and no exit.
947	
948	</Steps>
949	
950	Switching from one reveal to another keeps the times you set. Choosing **None**, or the section's **Reset**, turns the reveal off and forgets them, so the next reveal starts at 1 s in and 0 s out.
951	
952	When the section is folded, its header reads "off", or the reveal and its **In** time, such as "typewriter · 1.00 s".
953	
954	The preview, a rendered frame and an export all work out each frame the same way, so what you see while scrubbing is what you'll export.
955	
956	## The three reveals
957	
958	### Typewriter
959	
960	The text types on, one character at a time. Spaces and line breaks count as characters, so the typing pauses at them. On the way out it backspaces, and the end of the text goes first.
961	
962	### Word Fade
963	
964	The words fade in one after another. Each word's fade overlaps the next by half, so it reads as a wave across the text rather than one word at a time. On the way out they leave in the same order, so the first word in is the first word out.
965	
966	### Line Rise
967	
968	Each line fades in as it rises into place, starting 35 % of its own height below where it ends up. The top line goes first and the others follow. On the way out each line sinks and fades, again from the top.
969	
970	A line on its way up is cut off at the edge of the text box. Over a [backdrop](/text-and-shapes/text-outline-and-backdrop/) that looks like a mask, and without one the line appears to slide out of nothing.
971	
972	Lines are what the box makes them. In [Auto-size](/text-and-shapes/text-box/) only your own line breaks start a new line, so a single line of text rises all at once.
973	
974	## Set how long it takes
975	
976	| Control | What it does | Default | Range | Quick picks |
977	| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
978	| **In** | How long the arrival takes, from the clip's first frame. | 1 s | 0 to 10 s | 0, 0.25, 0.5, 1, 2 |
979	| **Out** | How long the departure takes, counted back from the clip's last frame. | 0 s | 0 to 10 s | 0, 0.25, 0.5, 1, 2 |
980	
981	- A time of 0 means that end of the reveal doesn't happen. With **In** at 0 the text is whole on the first frame, and with **Out** at 0 it stays whole to the last.
982	- Both times snap to whole frames.
983	- Both rows are greyed while **Reveal** is **None**.
984	- If **In** and **Out** add up to more than the clip's length, the two overlap. The text never shows in full, and a short clip gets a partial reveal.
985	
986	A reveal has no easing control, because the motion is part of the reveal you choose.
987	
988	## Word styles take over
989	
990	On a caption page with a [word style](/captions/word-caption-styles/), the word style decides how the words appear. The **Reveal** section is greyed and notes "Word style wins; the reveal does not apply." The page is drawn without any reveal.
991	
992	## Good to know
993	
994	- **Backdrop and outline.** A backdrop stays at full strength for the whole clip, so the words type or fade onto it. An outline arrives and leaves with its letters.
995	- **Trimming.** **In** and **Out** are measured from the clip's edges, so a trim moves the reveal with the new edge and keeps its length.
996	- **Splitting.** After a [split](/editing/splitting/), the first piece keeps the arrival and loses the departure, and the second keeps the departure and loses the arrival. A piece left with neither has its reveal turned off.
997	- **Transitions.** A reveal starts on the clip's first frame, so a [transition](/motion/transitions/) into a text clip plays over the start of the reveal.
998	- **Nests.** Inside a [nest](/editing/nests/), the text clip's own edges count, not the nest clip's. If the nest clip's edge falls part way through a reveal, the reveal is cut off there.
999	- **Actions.** With an [action](/motion/edit-an-action/) selected, these rows set the action's end. A change of reveal switches at the action's end rather than blending. **In** and **Out** ramp like any number, which shifts the reveal's own timing while it plays, so it's usually better to set them on the clip.
1000	- **Right-to-left text.** Typewriter can show the wrong part of a line when the text is right-to-left or mixes directions.
1001	
1002	## With an agent
1003	
1004	`set_text` sets a reveal through `animation`: `null` turns it off, and `{kind, in, out}` sets it, with a `kind` of `typewriter`, `word_fade` or `line_rise`. On a page with a `word_style`, the word style is what's drawn and `animation` has no effect. See [Tools: text, shapes and clip names](/mcp/tools-clip-properties/#set_text).
1005	
1006	## Related
1007	
1008	- [Text clips](/text-and-shapes/text-clips/)
1009	- [Text box and wrapping](/text-and-shapes/text-box/)
1010	- [Word caption styles](/captions/word-caption-styles/)

1012	=================== text-style.mdx
1013	---
1014	title: Font and text style
1015	description: Choose a text clip's font and size, then set its colour, alignment, capitals, line spacing and letter spacing.
1016	---
1017	
1018	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
1019	
1020	The **Font** and **Style** sections of the **Text** sub-tab set how a text clip's words look. Select a text clip to reach them. Both start folded, so click a header to open its section. The **Font** header shows the size and the **Style** header shows the alignment.
1021	
1022	<AtAGlance
1023	  where={['Clip tab ▸ Text ▸ Font', 'Clip tab ▸ Text ▸ Style']}
1024	  tools="set_text"
1025	/>
1026	
1027	## Choose a font
1028	
1029	**Family** lists every font family installed on your Mac, plus the ones Frame Job ships with: Source Sans 3, Source Serif 4, Montserrat, Anton, Bebas Neue, Darker Grotesque and IBM Plex Mono.
1030	
1031	**Style** lists the faces of that family, such as Regular or SemiBold.
1032	
1033	When you change **Family**, Frame Job keeps the current style if the new family has one of that name. Otherwise it uses Regular, or the family's first style if it has no Regular. Both controls make an undo step called **Font**.
1034	
1035	See [Fonts](/text-and-shapes/fonts/) for more on the faces.
1036	
1037	## Set the size
1038	
1039	**Size** runs from 6 to 800 px, and a new clip starts at 72 px. Type a value or use the quick picks: 24, 36, 48, 72, 96 and 144.
1040	
1041	The size is in canvas pixels, so the same number looks smaller on a larger canvas. For a size worked out from the canvas, use a [preset](/text-and-shapes/text-presets/).
1042	
1043	## Set the colour
1044	
1045	**Color** is white by default. Click its swatch to open the colour panel, and set the colour and its opacity there.
1046	
1047	## Align the text
1048	
1049	| Control | Choices | Default |
1050	| --- | --- | --- |
1051	| **Align** | **L**, **C** or **R** | Centre |
1052	| **Vertical** | Top, middle or bottom of the box | Middle |
1053	
1054	Both make an undo step called **Alignment**.
1055	
1056	With the box on **Auto-size**, the box is as wide as the longest line, so **Align** lines up the shorter lines and a single line doesn't move. In a [fixed-width box](/text-and-shapes/text-box/), it places every line in the box. To move the text itself, drag it on the canvas or use [Transform](/canvas/transform/).
1057	
1058	A text box is always as tall as its words, so **Vertical** moves the text by a pixel or two at most.
1059	
1060	## Show the text in capitals
1061	
1062	Tick **UPPERCASE** to draw the text in capitals. What you typed is kept as you typed it, so unticking the box brings it back. It never changes the number of words, so it's safe on captions timed word by word.
1063	
1064	The [canvas text editor](/text-and-shapes/edit-text-on-canvas/) shows the text as you typed it, not in capitals.
1065	
1066	## Adjust the spacing
1067	
1068	| Control | What it does | Default | Range |
1069	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
1070	| **Line spacing** | The space between lines, as a multiple of the font's line height | 1× | 0.5 to 4× |
1071	| **Tracking** | Extra space between letters. Below 0 pulls them together. | 0 px | −20 to 100 px |
1072	
1073	## Reset the style
1074	
1075	**Reset** in the **Style** section's header puts everything in that section back, in one undo step called **Text Style**:
1076	
1077	- **Color** to white
1078	- **Align** to centre and **Vertical** to middle
1079	- **UPPERCASE** off
1080	- **Line spacing** to 1× and **Tracking** to 0 px
1081	
1082	It shows while something in the section differs from those values and no action is selected. It doesn't touch the font or the size, and the **Font** section has no **Reset** of its own. To put **Size** back to 72 px, right-click its label and choose **Reset to default**.
1083	
1084	## Change the style during a clip
1085	
1086	With an [action](/motion/actions/) selected, these controls set the look at that action's end. **Size**, **Color**, **Line spacing** and **Tracking** ease towards the new value, and colours [blend in OKLab](/motion/what-can-animate/#colours-blend-in-oklab). **Family**, **Style**, **Align**, **Vertical** and **UPPERCASE** switch when the action ends.
1087	
1088	## With an agent
1089	
1090	An agent names a font by its one PostScript name, such as `SourceSans3-Bold`, rather than by family and style. A colour is four numbers from 0 to 1: red, green, blue and opacity. **Align** is `align` (`left`, `center` or `right`), **Vertical** is `valign` (`top`, `middle` or `bottom`), and **UPPERCASE** is `case` (`as_written` or `upper`).
1091	
1092	An agent isn't held to the ranges above: a size or line spacing only has to be above 0, and tracking can be any number. See [Tools: text, shapes and clip names](/mcp/tools-clip-properties/).
1093	
1094	## Good to know
1095	
1096	A project can name a font this Mac doesn't have. The **Text** sub-tab still opens, showing the first family in the list, and the text draws in a substitute until you install the font or choose another.
1097	
1098	## Related
