4	/// The commands that put a clip on the timeline out of nothing rather than
5	/// out of a file already in the Media tab: Add Text (T), the Add Shape menu,
6	/// and — since road map 2's phase 6c — the two BACKGROUND commands.
7	///
8	/// Placement follows the spec §4.1 wording, "at the playhead": the clip goes on
9	/// the FRONT-MOST track if it fits there, and onto a new track above everything
10	/// if it does not. Trying the front track first is what keeps a title sequence
11	/// from growing a track per title; falling back to a new one is what keeps the
12	/// button from ever beeping at a playhead that happens to sit over a clip.
13	/// Both are one undo step either way, because `applyEdit` takes the whole op
14	/// list (`ProjectDocument`).
15	///
16	/// **The two background commands place nothing themselves.** A backdrop goes
17	/// on a NEW back-most track, which is a decision with a source window, a fill
18	/// scale and a `SCALE_MAX` clamp behind it, so the whole of it is one core op
19	/// — `add_background` and `add_blurred_background`, argued at length in
20	/// `core/src/edit_background.rs`'s module doc. What is left here is the menu,
21	/// the open panel, and the one thing the core cannot answer: what should be
22	/// SELECTED afterwards.
23	extension EditorViewController {
24	
25	    /// T, the toolbar's Add Text button, and Clip > Add Text.
26	    @objc func addTextClipAtPlayhead(_ sender: Any?) {
27	        addGeneratedClip(named: "Add Text") { track, at in
28	            .addTextClip(track: track, at: at)
29	        }
30	    }
31	
32	    /// One item of the Add Shape menu. The sender's tag indexes
33	    /// `ShapeKind.allCases` — the same tagging `showAddShapeMenu` writes, so
34	    /// the menu and the enum cannot drift.
35	    @objc func addShapeClipAtPlayhead(_ sender: Any?) {
36	        let kinds = ShapeKind.allCases
37	        let tag = (sender as? NSMenuItem)?.tag ?? 0
38	        let kind = tag >= 0 && tag < kinds.count ? kinds[tag] : .rectangle
39	        addGeneratedClip(named: "Add \(kind.displayName)") { track, at in
40	            .addShapeClip(track: track, at: at, shape: kind)
41	        }
42	    }
43	
44	    /// The shared body: place `make` on the front track, and if the core
45	    /// refuses it there — the overlap rule (§6) is the only reason it can —
46	    /// insert a track above everything and place it there instead.
47	    ///
48	    /// The refusal is detected by applying the op PURELY first, against the
49	    /// document's own handle. That costs one throwaway project value and keeps
50	    /// the fallback out of the undo stack: nothing is registered until the
51	    /// version that works is the one applied.
52	    ///
53	    /// `grouped` is for a caller running OFF-EVENT (a panel's completion):
54	    /// the edit goes through `performGroupedEdit`, else `applyEdit`.
55	    func addGeneratedClip(
56	        named name: String, grouped: Bool = false, _ make: (UInt32, Ticks) -> ReelOp
57	    ) {
58	        guard let document = document else { return }
59	        // The EDITED project throughout, here and in every other command in
60	        // this file that places a clip: with a nest open the front track is
61	        // the NEST's front track, the overlap probe has to be run against the
62	        // nest, and the id set the selection is read back out of is the
63	        // nest's (road map 2's phase 9). `add_media` is the one exception and
64	        // is called out where it happens.
65	        let before = document.editedProject.snapshot
66	        let ops = Self.generatedClipOps(in: document, make)
67	        if grouped {
68	            document.performGroupedEdit(name, ops)
69	        } else {
70	            document.applyEdit(name, ops)
71	        }
72	        selectClips(addedSince: before, in: document)
73	    }
74	
75	    /// The track choice alone, no edit: `make` at the playhead on the
76	    /// edited project's front track when it fits there, else a new track
77	    /// above everything and `make` on it. `insert_graphic` places its clip
78	    /// by it too (spec §11 G-16 (a), G-45 (f)).
79	    static func generatedClipOps(
80	        in document: ProjectDocument, _ make: (UInt32, Ticks) -> ReelOp
81	    ) -> [ReelOp] {
82	        let before = document.editedProject.snapshot
83	        let at = document.playhead
84	        // `.project` on a `try?` collapses three answers into one nil: a
85	        // throw, an identity and a rule's refusal. Either way the front track
86	        // will not take this clip, so all of them take the new-track path.
87	        if let front = before.tracks.last?.id,
88	            (try? document.editedProject.applying(make(front, at))).project != nil
89	        {
90	            return [make(front, at)]
91	        }
92	        // The id of a newly added track is `next_id` from BEFORE the op —
93	        // the documented contract of the one JSON op entry point, since
94	        // `rc_project_apply` returns a project rather than an id.
95	        // Index 0 is the BACK of the stack (§6), so the count is the front.
96	        return [.addTrack(index: before.tracks.count), make(before.nextId, at)]
97	    }
98	
99	    /// Select whatever appeared, so the inspector opens on the new clip's own
100	    /// sections and the canvas draws its handles. Comparing id sets rather
101	    /// than trusting an id we predicted keeps this correct even if the core
102	    /// ever allocates differently — and it is why every command in this file
103	    /// reads the snapshot BEFORE it edits.
104	    ///
105	    /// Nothing added means the core refused or answered an identity —
106	    /// `applyEdit` has already beeped — so the selection stays as
107	    /// `ProjectDocument.clampViewState` left it.
108	    func selectClips(addedSince before: ProjectSnapshot, in document: ProjectDocument) {
109	        let existing = Set(before.clips.map { $0.id })
110	        let added = document.editedProject.snapshot.clips.map { $0.id }
111	            .filter { !existing.contains($0) }
112	        guard !added.isEmpty else { return }
113	        document.selection = Set(added)
114	        viewStateDidChange()
115	    }
116	
117	    // MARK: - Backgrounds (road map 2, phase 6c)
118	
119	    /// Clip ▸ Add Background ▸ Solid Color.
120	    ///
121	    /// **No dialog, and no ellipsis in the title.** The op takes no arguments
122	    /// at all — a canvas-sized white rectangle on a new back-most track,
123	    /// running the timeline's length — and the plate is re-coloured afterwards
124	    /// in the Clip tab's existing Fill row, which is the row that already owns
125	    /// "what colour is this shape". Asking for the colour up front would put a
126	    /// second colour picker in front of the one the inspector already has, and
127	    /// it would leave the interesting case unreachable: a full-canvas GRADIENT
128	    /// is this same plate with a `shape.gradient` on it, so the road map's
129	    /// gradient background is Solid Color followed by the Gradient section and
130	    /// nothing else.
131	    ///
132	    /// White rather than black is the core's choice and its own doc argues it:
133	    /// the canvas is already black, so a black plate is a command that appears
134	    /// to do nothing.
135	    @objc func addSolidColorBackground(_ sender: Any?) {
136	        guard let document = document else {
137	            NSSound.beep()
138	            return
139	        }
140	        let before = document.editedProject.snapshot
141	        document.applyEdit("Add Background", [.addBackground()])
142	        selectClips(addedSince: before, in: document)
143	    }
144	
145	    /// Clip ▸ Add Background ▸ Image… — a picture behind everything, at FILL
146	    /// scale and the timeline's length. Fill and not Fit, which is where
147	    /// `add_clip` would put it: a plate that leaves the canvas showing down
148	    /// one side has failed at the one thing a background is for, and it is
149	    /// the scale `add_blurred_background` gives its copy, so the two
150	    /// commands agree. The phase-6 review is what changed it.
151	    ///
152	    /// A standard `NSOpenPanel` over the image UTIs; `CaptionImporter.swift`
153	    /// is the pattern, down to the reason the edit that follows goes through
154	    /// `performGroupedEdit` rather than `applyEdit`: a panel's completion is
155	    /// OFF-EVENT, and an undo registration made outside an AppKit event lands
156	    /// in the implicit per-event group `NSUndoManager` never closes there,
157	    /// silently merging this edit into whatever came before it
158	    /// (app/CLAUDE.md's undo pitfall).
159	    @objc func addImageBackground(_ sender: Any?) {
160	        guard let document = document, let window = view.window else {
161	            NSSound.beep()
162	            return
163	        }
164	        let panel = NSOpenPanel()
165	        panel.allowsMultipleSelection = false
166	        panel.canChooseDirectories = false
167	        // The whole image family rather than `ProjectDocument.readableTypes`:
168	        // a movie behind the timeline is an ordinary clip on a track the user
169	        // puts where they want it, while a background is by definition the
170	        // thing that runs the WHOLE cut — and the op clamps a timed media to
171	        // its own file's length, so a five-second movie plate would stop where
172	        // its file does; only an image runs the whole timeline.
173	        panel.allowedContentTypes = [.image]
174	        panel.message = "Choose a picture to put behind everything."
175	        panel.beginSheetModal(for: window) { [weak self] response in
176	            guard response == .OK, let url = panel.url else { return }
177	            self?.addImageBackground(from: url, into: document, in: window)
178	        }
179	    }
180	
181	    /// The probe, then the placement. Probing is asynchronous and its answer
182	    /// arrives on the main thread (`MediaImporter.probe`, the seam that keeps
183	    /// `async` confined to that file), so an unreadable picture is reported in
184	    /// a sheet and nothing is placed.
185	    func addImageBackground(
186	        from url: URL, into document: ProjectDocument, in window: NSWindow
187	    ) {
188	        MediaImporter.probe(url: url, mayAsk: true) { [weak self] result in
189	            switch result {
190	            case .failure(let error):
191	                NSAlert(error: error).beginSheetModal(for: window, completionHandler: nil)
192	            case .success(let descriptor):
193	                self?.placeImageBackground(descriptor, into: document, in: window)
194	            }
195	        }
196	    }
197	
198	    /// Two ops in ONE undo step — `add_media` then `add_background {media}` —
199	    /// which needs the id the FIRST one mints, or the id it declined to mint.
200	    ///
201	    /// An op returns a project and never a value (spec §11: one FFI entry
202	    /// point for every op), so the id is learned by applying `add_media`
203	    /// PURELY, against the document's own handle, and reading it off the
204	    /// resulting snapshot: the core appends, so the last entry is the new one.
205	    /// `ProjectDocument.makeProject(around:)` has done exactly this since M1
206	    /// and this is the first use of the technique outside it, so the reason it
207	    /// is sound is worth writing down here as well: `next_id` is a single
208	    /// counter, so the same op applied to the same base mints the same id
209	    /// every time, and the throwaway project the probe applies to and the one
210	    /// the undo step applies to ARE the same base.
211	    ///
212	    /// **The precedent does not carry the whole way, and the review is what
213	    /// found the gap**: `makeProject(around:)` applies `add_media` to a
214	    /// project built empty two lines above it, where the file cannot already
215	    /// be in the list, and this call site is the case where it can be.
216	    /// `backgroundMedia(for:in:)` is that half.
217	    ///
218	    /// The alternative — `importMedia` and then a second edit — is two undo
219	    /// steps for one command, and a ⌘Z that leaves the picture in the media
220	    /// list is the kind of half-undone state this app does not have anywhere
221	    /// else.
222	    func placeImageBackground(
223	        _ descriptor: MediaDescriptor, into document: ProjectDocument, in window: NSWindow
224	    ) {
225	        let before = document.editedProject.snapshot
226	        let add = ReelOp.addMedia(descriptor: descriptor)
227	        let media: UInt32
228	        do {
229	            // The core's own message for a descriptor it refuses — a picture
230	            // past `MEDIA_DIMENSION_MAX`, a rate with a zero term — rather
231	            // than the sentence below, which would report "could not be
232	            // added" and name none of it. A `try?` here spent the one thing
233	            // the core said.
234	            // The DOCUMENT's handle, not the edited one: `add_media` is a
235	            // document-level op sent unscoped (`ReelOp.isDocumentLevel`), so
236	            // the probe that learns the id it will mint has to be run against
237	            // the same project the real op will land in.
238	            guard let id = try Self.backgroundMedia(for: descriptor, in: document.project) else {
239	                let alert = NSAlert()
240	                alert.messageText = "Could Not Add the Picture"
241	                alert.informativeText =
242	                    "“\(descriptor.path)” could not be added to this project's media list."
243	                alert.beginSheetModal(for: window, completionHandler: nil)
244	                return
245	            }
246	            media = id
247	        } catch {
248	            NSAlert(error: error).beginSheetModal(for: window, completionHandler: nil)
249	            return
250	        }
251	        // `add` stays in the list even when it is an identity: `applying(_
252	        // ops:)` runs every later op after an earlier one that changed
253	        // nothing, so one shape works for both cases and the undo step is
254	        // one either way.
255	        document.performGroupedEdit("Add Background", [add, .addBackground(media: media)])
256	        // The thumbnail the Media tab draws, and the filmstrip the timeline
257	        // draws: the import path generates them after every commit and this is
258	        // a commit like any other. Safe to call repeatedly — a cache whose
259	        // marker matches its file is not rebuilt, so a picture already in the
260	        // list costs the pass a stat and a marker read.
261	        document.generateCaches()
262	        selectClips(addedSince: before, in: document)
263	    }
264	
265	    /// The media id `add_background` is to be handed for `descriptor` — the
266	    /// one `add_media` is about to mint, or the one the project already holds
267	    /// for that path.
268	    ///
269	    /// **A file already in the media list is not a failure.** `add_media`
270	    /// deduplicates by path and answers the documented identity (which
271	    /// `ReelProject.applying` answers as `.identity`, with no handle) rather
272	    /// than an error, and its own doc says what a caller does with that
273	    /// answer: "The caller that gets it looks the path up to find the id that
274	    /// is already there" (`core/src/edit_track.rs`). Reading the absent
275	    /// handle as "could not be added" refused two entirely ordinary sequences
276	    /// — Add Background ▸ Image… twice with one picture, and using a picture
277	    /// that is already in the Media tab — with a sentence that is not true,
278	    /// and placed nothing. `commitImport`
279	    /// has absorbed the same identity silently since M1; a duplicate drop into
280	    /// the Media tab is a no-op, and this command owes the file the same
281	    /// reading.
282	    ///
283	    /// The lookup compares against the TRIMMED path, because that is the
284	    /// string the core stored: `add_media` trims before it deduplicates and
285	    /// before it writes `record.path`.
286	    ///
287	    /// Throws the core's own message for a descriptor it refuses; nil only for
288	    /// the case that cannot happen — an identity whose path is in no entry.
289	    static func backgroundMedia(for descriptor: MediaDescriptor, in project: ReelProject) throws
290	        -> UInt32?
291	    {
292	        if let probed = try project.applying(.addMedia(descriptor: descriptor)).project {
293	            return probed.snapshot.media.last?.id
294	        }
295	        let path = descriptor.path.trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespacesAndNewlines)
296	        return project.snapshot.media.first { $0.path == path }?.id
297	    }
298	
299	    /// Clip ▸ Add Blurred Background — the screencast backdrop: the selected
300	    /// clip copied onto a new back-most track, blown up to FILL the canvas and
301	    /// blurred at full strength.
302	    ///
303	    /// One clip, never a selection: the copy is made of that clip's own pixels
304	    /// and plays its own frames, so two selected clips would either have to be
305	    /// chosen between or produce two backdrops, one of which hides the other.
306	    /// The menu item is validated on that, so the beep below is reachable only
307	    /// from a path that skips validation.
308	    ///
309	    /// Everything else is the op's: the dropped audio switch (a copy that kept
310	    /// it would play one recording twice, at roughly +6 dB, and no still frame
311	    /// could see it), the dropped transition, the dropped actions, and the
312	    /// fill scale.
313	    @objc func addBlurredBackground(_ sender: Any?) {
314	        guard let document = document, selectedClips.count == 1,
315	            let clip = selectedClips.first
316	        else {
317	            NSSound.beep()
318	            return
319	        }
320	        let before = document.editedProject.snapshot
321	        document.applyEdit("Add Blurred Background", [.addBlurredBackground(clip: clip.id)])
322	        // The backdrop, not the clip it was made from: what a person does next
323	        // is dial its blur or its scale, and the foreground clip is one click
324	        // away on the timeline. It is also this file's standing rule — every
325	        // command here selects what it created.
326	        selectClips(addedSince: before, in: document)
327	    }
328	
329	    /// The menu arms for the three, answered from `validateUserInterfaceItem`'s
330	    /// default case. Each asks the cheap snapshot question its command's own
331	    /// guard asks, so the menu and the command can never disagree — and
332	    /// without an arm an item falls through to that method's closing
333	    /// `return true` and is live on a timeline where it could only beep.
334	    func validateBackgroundAction(_ action: Selector) -> Bool? {
335	        switch action {
336	        case #selector(addSolidColorBackground(_:)), #selector(addImageBackground(_:)):
337	            // A plate needs a canvas and nothing else. It lands on a track of
338	            // its own, so there is no selection to have and no overlap to
339	            // refuse; the document's existence is all there is to check, and
340	            // `validateUserInterfaceItem` has checked it already.
341	            return true
342	        case #selector(addBlurredBackground(_:)):
343	            guard let snapshot = document?.editedProject.snapshot, selectedClips.count == 1,
344	                let clip = selectedClips.first
345	            else { return false }
346	            // The op's own refusals, asked here so the item DIMS rather than
347	            // raising a sheet.
348	            //
349	            // A NEST first, and it is the one a reader will not expect:
350	            // `sourceSize(of:)` answers for a nest with its frozen canvas, so
351	            // the size test below would wave it through. The op refuses it all
352	            // the same, because a nest clip never becomes a layer — only its
353	            // PLACEMENT folds down, through `Frame::enter` — so the blur the
354	            // copy would carry reaches nothing, and the backdrop comes out
355	            // SHARP at fill scale, at double the render cost, reported as
356	            // success. Refusing there and dimming here are one decision;
357	            // `edit_background.rs`'s module doc argues it.
358	            if case .nest = clip.source { return false }
359	            // Then a source with no pixel size — a text clip, an audio-only
360	            // one — which has nothing to scale to the canvas.
361	            guard let size = snapshot.sourceSize(of: clip), size.width > 0, size.height > 0
362	            else { return false }
363	            return true
364	        default:
365	            return nil
366	        }
367	    }
368	}

# app/CLAUDE.md — Swift app rules

Applies to everything under `app/`. Build/verification commands and the FFI
lockstep are in the root `CLAUDE.md`; the full design is
`designs/spec/` (§3–4 the UI, §7.4–7.8 the platform side; its `README.md` is
the index). The
long form of each entry below — why each file is the shape it is, and the
traps its history turned up — is `designs/adr/app-file-history.md` (the
full history, every size toll and measurement, is archived; see its
"Original" line); this file is what governs a file now. Files
are listed by family; a file with a header comment of its own carries its
detail there.

## File map

**The core's edge.**
- `ReelCore.swift` — with its `ReelCore+<Area>.swift` files, the only files
  that call `rc_*` (spec §11 CJ-8 (l)); a new wrapper goes in the file of its
  area. `ReelCore.swift` holds `ReelProject`
  (handle + lazily decoded `ProjectSnapshot`; `json`, `snapshot` and
  `planJSON` are memoised PER HANDLE, so keep handles rather than minting
  them; so is `sourceMap(_:)`, `rc_project_source_map` decoded and checked
  once per handle and clip, SR-20), timecode, snapping (export presets/sizes/settings are
  `ExportValues.swift`'s, a pure move, HDR H-1), `ReelSpeed.limits` (the
  core's speed range and audio ceiling, typed as `SpeedLimits` in
  `CoreValues.swift` — no Swift file types a speed bound), `ReelColor` (`rc_normalise_color`, G-25) and `ReelAgentSocket` (below);
  `ReelCore+MediaFiles.swift` holds the media files the core reads or writes —
  `ReelContainer` (`rc_container_*`, a WebM/Matroska file's index, #216-R), `ReelCube`,

**Frozen files.** `EditorViewController.swift`, `TimelineView.swift`,
`PreviewCanvasView.swift`, `AgentServer.swift` are **frozen at current
size**: anything adding more than ~50 lines goes in an extension file
(`EditorViewController+<Feature>.swift`, `TimelineView+<Feature>.swift`,
`AgentServer+<Feature>.swift`) or a new `…SheetController`, and the frozen
file keeps only the wiring — a stored property, a closure assignment, a
validator arm, a draw call. The pieces extension files build on are therefore
internal, not private. Pitfalls: a selector declared `@objc` on an extension
needs NO forward in the frozen file (a second declaration is an error); a
command whose body sits at the foot of a non-extension feature file carries
its validator arm there too, or the item falls through to the closing
`return true`; `handleEditorCharacter`'s bare-key `switch` matches in SOURCE
order, so a bare `case "x"` goes BELOW any modified `case "x" where …`; and
`handleEditorKey` refuses while a sheet is attached, because a sheet is
window-modal and the preview panel's forwarded keys would otherwise reach
the key map behind it.

# app/CLAUDE.md — Swift app rules

Applies to everything under `app/`. Build/verification commands and the FFI
lockstep are in the root `CLAUDE.md`; the full design is
`designs/spec/` (§3–4 the UI, §7.4–7.8 the platform side; its `README.md` is
the index). The
long form of each entry below — why each file is the shape it is, and the
traps its history turned up — is `designs/adr/app-file-history.md` (the
full history, every size toll and measurement, is archived; see its
"Original" line); this file is what governs a file now. Files
are listed by family; a file with a header comment of its own carries its
detail there.

## File map

**The core's edge.**
- `ReelCore.swift` — with its `ReelCore+<Area>.swift` files, the only files
  that call `rc_*` (spec §11 CJ-8 (l)); a new wrapper goes in the file of its

**Frozen files.** `EditorViewController.swift`, `TimelineView.swift`,
`PreviewCanvasView.swift`, `AgentServer.swift` are **frozen at current
size**: anything adding more than ~50 lines goes in an extension file
(`EditorViewController+<Feature>.swift`, `TimelineView+<Feature>.swift`,
`AgentServer+<Feature>.swift`) or a new `…SheetController`, and the frozen
file keeps only the wiring — a stored property, a closure assignment, a
validator arm, a draw call. The pieces extension files build on are therefore
internal, not private. Pitfalls: a selector declared `@objc` on an extension
needs NO forward in the frozen file (a second declaration is an error); a
command whose body sits at the foot of a non-extension feature file carries
its validator arm there too, or the item falls through to the closing
`return true`; `handleEditorCharacter`'s bare-key `switch` matches in SOURCE
order, so a bare `case "x"` goes BELOW any modified `case "x" where …`; and
`handleEditorKey` refuses while a sheet is attached, because a sheet is
window-modal and the preview panel's forwarded keys would otherwise reach
the key map behind it.

204	    /// The note's whole rule, as a function of the three things it depends on
205	    /// — the mode, the canvas colour and whether anything draws underneath —
206	    /// so it can be measured without an inspector around it.
207	    ///
208	    /// **The canvas has to be OPAQUE black, not merely black**, and the alpha
209	    /// is the half the first version left out. `blendPremultiplied`'s
210	    /// `(1 - ab)·src` term carries the source through an empty destination:
211	    /// at `ab` = 0 the whole formula reduces to `src` exactly, for all eight
212	    /// modes — the same property `Compositor+Shadow.swift`'s shadow mask relies on.
213	    /// So over a TRANSPARENT canvas `multiply` renders the layer untouched,
214	    /// and a note reading "multiply reads black here" would name the opposite
215	    /// of what is on screen. Between the two the composite is a partial
216	    /// version of the same (`ab` = 0.5 halves a multiply), which neither verb
217	    /// describes either, so anything short of opaque stands the note down.
218	    /// A missing fourth component reads as 1, which is `RGBA.nsColor`'s
219	    /// convention and the only reading under which a three-component colour
220	    /// means what it says.
221	    static func blendTrapNote(_ mode: BlendMode, over background: RGBA, hasLayerBehind: Bool)
222	        -> String?
223	    {
224	        guard mode != .normal, !hasLayerBehind else { return nil }
225	        // A non-black canvas is something to blend against, so the trap is not
226	        // live: `multiply` over a white canvas is the layer itself, which is
227	        // the identity a person can see and reason about.
228	        guard background.prefix(3).allSatisfy({ $0 <= 0.001 }) else { return nil }
229	        guard background.count > 3 ? background[3] >= 0.999 : true else { return nil }
230	        let collapsesToBlack: Set<BlendMode> = [.multiply, .darken, .overlay]
231	        let verb = collapsesToBlack.contains(mode) ? "reads black here" : "changes nothing here"
232	        return "Nothing behind this clip — \(mode.displayName.lowercased()) \(verb)."
233	    }

247	            return false
248	        }
249	        for track in snapshot.tracks.prefix(index) where !track.hidden {
250	            let covered = snapshot.clips(onTrack: track.id).contains { other in
251	                other.enabled.video && other.start < clip.end && other.end > clip.start
252	            }
253	            if covered { return true }
254	        }
255	        return false
256	    }
257	
258	    /// Fit is `min(cw/sw, ch/sh)`, Fill is `max` (§5.3), centred either way.
259	    /// Each clip gets its own op because the scale depends on ITS source size;
260	    /// clips whose size only the renderer knows (text) are skipped.
261	    private func fitOrFill(fill: Bool) {
262	        let canvas = binding.canvas
263	        var ops: [ReelOp] = []
264	        for clip in binding.clips {
265	            guard let source = binding.snapshot.sourceSize(of: clip),
266	                  source.width > 0, source.height > 0
267	            else { continue }
268	            let horizontal = Double(canvas.width) / Double(source.width)
269	            let vertical = Double(canvas.height) / Double(source.height)
270	            let scale = fill ? max(horizontal, vertical) : min(horizontal, vertical)
271	            ops.append(
272	                contentsOf: binding.ops(
273	                    video: VideoPatch(x: 0, y: 0, scale: scale), for: clip))
274	        }
275	        binding.apply(fill ? "Fill Canvas" : "Fit to Canvas", ops)
276	    }
277	}

4	/// The commands that put a clip on the timeline out of nothing rather than
5	/// out of a file already in the Media tab: Add Text (T), the Add Shape menu,
6	/// and — since road map 2's phase 6c — the two BACKGROUND commands.
7	///
8	/// Placement follows the spec §4.1 wording, "at the playhead": the clip goes on
9	/// the FRONT-MOST track if it fits there, and onto a new track above everything
10	/// if it does not. Trying the front track first is what keeps a title sequence
11	/// from growing a track per title; falling back to a new one is what keeps the
12	/// button from ever beeping at a playhead that happens to sit over a clip.
13	/// Both are one undo step either way, because `applyEdit` takes the whole op
14	/// list (`ProjectDocument`).
15	///
16	/// **The two background commands place nothing themselves.** A backdrop goes
17	/// on a NEW back-most track, which is a decision with a source window, a fill
18	/// scale and a `SCALE_MAX` clamp behind it, so the whole of it is one core op
19	/// — `add_background` and `add_blurred_background`, argued at length in
20	/// `core/src/edit_background.rs`'s module doc. What is left here is the menu,
21	/// the open panel, and the one thing the core cannot answer: what should be
22	/// SELECTED afterwards.
23	extension EditorViewController {
24	
25	    /// T, the toolbar's Add Text button, and Clip > Add Text.
26	    @objc func addTextClipAtPlayhead(_ sender: Any?) {
27	        addGeneratedClip(named: "Add Text") { track, at in
28	            .addTextClip(track: track, at: at)
29	        }
30	    }
31	
32	    /// One item of the Add Shape menu. The sender's tag indexes
33	    /// `ShapeKind.allCases` — the same tagging `showAddShapeMenu` writes, so
34	    /// the menu and the enum cannot drift.
35	    @objc func addShapeClipAtPlayhead(_ sender: Any?) {
36	        let kinds = ShapeKind.allCases
37	        let tag = (sender as? NSMenuItem)?.tag ?? 0
38	        let kind = tag >= 0 && tag < kinds.count ? kinds[tag] : .rectangle
39	        addGeneratedClip(named: "Add \(kind.displayName)") { track, at in
40	            .addShapeClip(track: track, at: at, shape: kind)
41	        }
42	    }
43	
44	    /// The shared body: place `make` on the front track, and if the core
45	    /// refuses it there — the overlap rule (§6) is the only reason it can —
46	    /// insert a track above everything and place it there instead.
47	    ///
48	    /// The refusal is detected by applying the op PURELY first, against the
49	    /// document's own handle. That costs one throwaway project value and keeps
50	    /// the fallback out of the undo stack: nothing is registered until the
51	    /// version that works is the one applied.
52	    ///
53	    /// `grouped` is for a caller running OFF-EVENT (a panel's completion):
54	    /// the edit goes through `performGroupedEdit`, else `applyEdit`.
55	    func addGeneratedClip(
56	        named name: String, grouped: Bool = false, _ make: (UInt32, Ticks) -> ReelOp
57	    ) {
58	        guard let document = document else { return }
59	        // The EDITED project throughout, here and in every other command in
60	        // this file that places a clip: with a nest open the front track is
61	        // the NEST's front track, the overlap probe has to be run against the
62	        // nest, and the id set the selection is read back out of is the
63	        // nest's (road map 2's phase 9). `add_media` is the one exception and
64	        // is called out where it happens.
65	        let before = document.editedProject.snapshot
66	        let ops = Self.generatedClipOps(in: document, make)
67	        if grouped {
68	            document.performGroupedEdit(name, ops)
69	        } else {
70	            document.applyEdit(name, ops)
71	        }
72	        selectClips(addedSince: before, in: document)
73	    }
74	
75	    /// The track choice alone, no edit: `make` at the playhead on the
76	    /// edited project's front track when it fits there, else a new track
77	    /// above everything and `make` on it. `insert_graphic` places its clip
78	    /// by it too (spec §11 G-16 (a), G-45 (f)).
79	    static func generatedClipOps(
80	        in document: ProjectDocument, _ make: (UInt32, Ticks) -> ReelOp
81	    ) -> [ReelOp] {
82	        let before = document.editedProject.snapshot
83	        let at = document.playhead
84	        // `.project` on a `try?` collapses three answers into one nil: a
85	        // throw, an identity and a rule's refusal. Either way the front track
86	        // will not take this clip, so all of them take the new-track path.
87	        if let front = before.tracks.last?.id,
88	            (try? document.editedProject.applying(make(front, at))).project != nil
89	        {
90	            return [make(front, at)]
91	        }
92	        // The id of a newly added track is `next_id` from BEFORE the op —
93	        // the documented contract of the one JSON op entry point, since
94	        // `rc_project_apply` returns a project rather than an id.
95	        // Index 0 is the BACK of the stack (§6), so the count is the front.
96	        return [.addTrack(index: before.tracks.count), make(before.nextId, at)]
97	    }
98	
99	    /// Select whatever appeared, so the inspector opens on the new clip's own
100	    /// sections and the canvas draws its handles. Comparing id sets rather
101	    /// than trusting an id we predicted keeps this correct even if the core
102	    /// ever allocates differently — and it is why every command in this file
103	    /// reads the snapshot BEFORE it edits.
104	    ///
105	    /// Nothing added means the core refused or answered an identity —
106	    /// `applyEdit` has already beeped — so the selection stays as
107	    /// `ProjectDocument.clampViewState` left it.
108	    func selectClips(addedSince before: ProjectSnapshot, in document: ProjectDocument) {
109	        let existing = Set(before.clips.map { $0.id })
110	        let added = document.editedProject.snapshot.clips.map { $0.id }
111	            .filter { !existing.contains($0) }
112	        guard !added.isEmpty else { return }
113	        document.selection = Set(added)
114	        viewStateDidChange()
115	    }
116	
117	    // MARK: - Backgrounds (road map 2, phase 6c)
118	
119	    /// Clip ▸ Add Background ▸ Solid Color.
120	    ///
121	    /// **No dialog, and no ellipsis in the title.** The op takes no arguments
122	    /// at all — a canvas-sized white rectangle on a new back-most track,
123	    /// running the timeline's length — and the plate is re-coloured afterwards
124	    /// in the Clip tab's existing Fill row, which is the row that already owns
125	    /// "what colour is this shape". Asking for the colour up front would put a
126	    /// second colour picker in front of the one the inspector already has, and
127	    /// it would leave the interesting case unreachable: a full-canvas GRADIENT
128	    /// is this same plate with a `shape.gradient` on it, so the road map's
129	    /// gradient background is Solid Color followed by the Gradient section and
130	    /// nothing else.
131	    ///
132	    /// White rather than black is the core's choice and its own doc argues it:
133	    /// the canvas is already black, so a black plate is a command that appears
134	    /// to do nothing.
135	    @objc func addSolidColorBackground(_ sender: Any?) {
136	        guard let document = document else {
137	            NSSound.beep()
138	            return
139	        }
140	        let before = document.editedProject.snapshot
141	        document.applyEdit("Add Background", [.addBackground()])
142	        selectClips(addedSince: before, in: document)
143	    }
144	
145	    /// Clip ▸ Add Background ▸ Image… — a picture behind everything, at FILL
146	    /// scale and the timeline's length. Fill and not Fit, which is where
147	    /// `add_clip` would put it: a plate that leaves the canvas showing down
148	    /// one side has failed at the one thing a background is for, and it is
149	    /// the scale `add_blurred_background` gives its copy, so the two
150	    /// commands agree. The phase-6 review is what changed it.
151	    ///
152	    /// A standard `NSOpenPanel` over the image UTIs; `CaptionImporter.swift`
153	    /// is the pattern, down to the reason the edit that follows goes through
154	    /// `performGroupedEdit` rather than `applyEdit`: a panel's completion is
155	    /// OFF-EVENT, and an undo registration made outside an AppKit event lands
156	    /// in the implicit per-event group `NSUndoManager` never closes there,
157	    /// silently merging this edit into whatever came before it
158	    /// (app/CLAUDE.md's undo pitfall).
159	    @objc func addImageBackground(_ sender: Any?) {
160	        guard let document = document, let window = view.window else {
161	            NSSound.beep()
162	            return
163	        }
164	        let panel = NSOpenPanel()
165	        panel.allowsMultipleSelection = false
166	        panel.canChooseDirectories = false
167	        // The whole image family rather than `ProjectDocument.readableTypes`:
168	        // a movie behind the timeline is an ordinary clip on a track the user
169	        // puts where they want it, while a background is by definition the
170	        // thing that runs the WHOLE cut — and the op clamps a timed media to
171	        // its own file's length, so a five-second movie plate would stop where
172	        // its file does; only an image runs the whole timeline.
173	        panel.allowedContentTypes = [.image]
174	        panel.message = "Choose a picture to put behind everything."
175	        panel.beginSheetModal(for: window) { [weak self] response in
176	            guard response == .OK, let url = panel.url else { return }
177	            self?.addImageBackground(from: url, into: document, in: window)
178	        }
179	    }
180	
181	    /// The probe, then the placement. Probing is asynchronous and its answer
182	    /// arrives on the main thread (`MediaImporter.probe`, the seam that keeps
183	    /// `async` confined to that file), so an unreadable picture is reported in
184	    /// a sheet and nothing is placed.
185	    func addImageBackground(
186	        from url: URL, into document: ProjectDocument, in window: NSWindow
187	    ) {
188	        MediaImporter.probe(url: url, mayAsk: true) { [weak self] result in
189	            switch result {
190	            case .failure(let error):
191	                NSAlert(error: error).beginSheetModal(for: window, completionHandler: nil)
192	            case .success(let descriptor):
193	                self?.placeImageBackground(descriptor, into: document, in: window)
194	            }
195	        }
196	    }
197	
198	    /// Two ops in ONE undo step — `add_media` then `add_background {media}` —
199	    /// which needs the id the FIRST one mints, or the id it declined to mint.
200	    ///
201	    /// An op returns a project and never a value (spec §11: one FFI entry
202	    /// point for every op), so the id is learned by applying `add_media`
203	    /// PURELY, against the document's own handle, and reading it off the
204	    /// resulting snapshot: the core appends, so the last entry is the new one.
205	    /// `ProjectDocument.makeProject(around:)` has done exactly this since M1
206	    /// and this is the first use of the technique outside it, so the reason it
207	    /// is sound is worth writing down here as well: `next_id` is a single
208	    /// counter, so the same op applied to the same base mints the same id
209	    /// every time, and the throwaway project the probe applies to and the one
210	    /// the undo step applies to ARE the same base.
211	    ///
212	    /// **The precedent does not carry the whole way, and the review is what
213	    /// found the gap**: `makeProject(around:)` applies `add_media` to a
214	    /// project built empty two lines above it, where the file cannot already
215	    /// be in the list, and this call site is the case where it can be.
216	    /// `backgroundMedia(for:in:)` is that half.
217	    ///
218	    /// The alternative — `importMedia` and then a second edit — is two undo
219	    /// steps for one command, and a ⌘Z that leaves the picture in the media
220	    /// list is the kind of half-undone state this app does not have anywhere
221	    /// else.
222	    func placeImageBackground(
223	        _ descriptor: MediaDescriptor, into document: ProjectDocument, in window: NSWindow
224	    ) {
225	        let before = document.editedProject.snapshot
226	        let add = ReelOp.addMedia(descriptor: descriptor)
227	        let media: UInt32
228	        do {
229	            // The core's own message for a descriptor it refuses — a picture
230	            // past `MEDIA_DIMENSION_MAX`, a rate with a zero term — rather
231	            // than the sentence below, which would report "could not be
232	            // added" and name none of it. A `try?` here spent the one thing
233	            // the core said.
234	            // The DOCUMENT's handle, not the edited one: `add_media` is a
235	            // document-level op sent unscoped (`ReelOp.isDocumentLevel`), so
236	            // the probe that learns the id it will mint has to be run against
237	            // the same project the real op will land in.
238	            guard let id = try Self.backgroundMedia(for: descriptor, in: document.project) else {
239	                let alert = NSAlert()
240	                alert.messageText = "Could Not Add the Picture"
241	                alert.informativeText =
242	                    "“\(descriptor.path)” could not be added to this project's media list."
243	                alert.beginSheetModal(for: window, completionHandler: nil)
244	                return
245	            }
246	            media = id
247	        } catch {
248	            NSAlert(error: error).beginSheetModal(for: window, completionHandler: nil)
249	            return
250	        }
251	        // `add` stays in the list even when it is an identity: `applying(_
252	        // ops:)` runs every later op after an earlier one that changed
253	        // nothing, so one shape works for both cases and the undo step is
254	        // one either way.
255	        document.performGroupedEdit("Add Background", [add, .addBackground(media: media)])
256	        // The thumbnail the Media tab draws, and the filmstrip the timeline
257	        // draws: the import path generates them after every commit and this is
258	        // a commit like any other. Safe to call repeatedly — a cache whose
259	        // marker matches its file is not rebuilt, so a picture already in the
260	        // list costs the pass a stat and a marker read.
261	        document.generateCaches()
262	        selectClips(addedSince: before, in: document)
263	    }
264	
265	    /// The media id `add_background` is to be handed for `descriptor` — the
266	    /// one `add_media` is about to mint, or the one the project already holds
267	    /// for that path.
268	    ///
269	    /// **A file already in the media list is not a failure.** `add_media`
270	    /// deduplicates by path and answers the documented identity (which
271	    /// `ReelProject.applying` answers as `.identity`, with no handle) rather
272	    /// than an error, and its own doc says what a caller does with that
273	    /// answer: "The caller that gets it looks the path up to find the id that
274	    /// is already there" (`core/src/edit_track.rs`). Reading the absent
275	    /// handle as "could not be added" refused two entirely ordinary sequences
276	    /// — Add Background ▸ Image… twice with one picture, and using a picture
277	    /// that is already in the Media tab — with a sentence that is not true,
278	    /// and placed nothing. `commitImport`
279	    /// has absorbed the same identity silently since M1; a duplicate drop into
280	    /// the Media tab is a no-op, and this command owes the file the same
281	    /// reading.
282	    ///
283	    /// The lookup compares against the TRIMMED path, because that is the
284	    /// string the core stored: `add_media` trims before it deduplicates and
285	    /// before it writes `record.path`.
286	    ///
287	    /// Throws the core's own message for a descriptor it refuses; nil only for
288	    /// the case that cannot happen — an identity whose path is in no entry.
289	    static func backgroundMedia(for descriptor: MediaDescriptor, in project: ReelProject) throws
290	        -> UInt32?
291	    {
292	        if let probed = try project.applying(.addMedia(descriptor: descriptor)).project {
293	            return probed.snapshot.media.last?.id
294	        }
295	        let path = descriptor.path.trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespacesAndNewlines)
296	        return project.snapshot.media.first { $0.path == path }?.id
297	    }
298	
299	    /// Clip ▸ Add Blurred Background — the screencast backdrop: the selected
300	    /// clip copied onto a new back-most track, blown up to FILL the canvas and
301	    /// blurred at full strength.
302	    ///
303	    /// One clip, never a selection: the copy is made of that clip's own pixels
304	    /// and plays its own frames, so two selected clips would either have to be
305	    /// chosen between or produce two backdrops, one of which hides the other.
306	    /// The menu item is validated on that, so the beep below is reachable only
307	    /// from a path that skips validation.
308	    ///
309	    /// Everything else is the op's: the dropped audio switch (a copy that kept
310	    /// it would play one recording twice, at roughly +6 dB, and no still frame
311	    /// could see it), the dropped transition, the dropped actions, and the
312	    /// fill scale.
313	    @objc func addBlurredBackground(_ sender: Any?) {
314	        guard let document = document, selectedClips.count == 1,
315	            let clip = selectedClips.first
316	        else {
317	            NSSound.beep()
318	            return
319	        }
320	        let before = document.editedProject.snapshot
321	        document.applyEdit("Add Blurred Background", [.addBlurredBackground(clip: clip.id)])
322	        // The backdrop, not the clip it was made from: what a person does next
323	        // is dial its blur or its scale, and the foreground clip is one click
324	        // away on the timeline. It is also this file's standing rule — every
325	        // command here selects what it created.
326	        selectClips(addedSince: before, in: document)
327	    }
328	
329	    /// The menu arms for the three, answered from `validateUserInterfaceItem`'s
330	    /// default case. Each asks the cheap snapshot question its command's own
331	    /// guard asks, so the menu and the command can never disagree — and
332	    /// without an arm an item falls through to that method's closing
333	    /// `return true` and is live on a timeline where it could only beep.
334	    func validateBackgroundAction(_ action: Selector) -> Bool? {
335	        switch action {
336	        case #selector(addSolidColorBackground(_:)), #selector(addImageBackground(_:)):
337	            // A plate needs a canvas and nothing else. It lands on a track of
338	            // its own, so there is no selection to have and no overlap to
339	            // refuse; the document's existence is all there is to check, and
340	            // `validateUserInterfaceItem` has checked it already.
341	            return true
342	        case #selector(addBlurredBackground(_:)):
343	            guard let snapshot = document?.editedProject.snapshot, selectedClips.count == 1,
344	                let clip = selectedClips.first
345	            else { return false }
346	            // The op's own refusals, asked here so the item DIMS rather than
347	            // raising a sheet.
348	            //
349	            // A NEST first, and it is the one a reader will not expect:
350	            // `sourceSize(of:)` answers for a nest with its frozen canvas, so
351	            // the size test below would wave it through. The op refuses it all
352	            // the same, because a nest clip never becomes a layer — only its
353	            // PLACEMENT folds down, through `Frame::enter` — so the blur the
354	            // copy would carry reaches nothing, and the backdrop comes out
355	            // SHARP at fill scale, at double the render cost, reported as
356	            // success. Refusing there and dimming here are one decision;
357	            // `edit_background.rs`'s module doc argues it.
358	            if case .nest = clip.source { return false }
359	            // Then a source with no pixel size — a text clip, an audio-only
360	            // one — which has nothing to scale to the canvas.
361	            guard let size = snapshot.sourceSize(of: clip), size.width > 0, size.height > 0
362	            else { return false }
363	            return true
364	        default:
365	            return nil
366	        }
367	    }
368	}

# app/CLAUDE.md — Swift app rules

Applies to everything under `app/`. Build/verification commands and the FFI
lockstep are in the root `CLAUDE.md`; the full design is
`designs/spec/` (§3–4 the UI, §7.4–7.8 the platform side; its `README.md` is
the index). The
long form of each entry below — why each file is the shape it is, and the
traps its history turned up — is `designs/adr/app-file-history.md` (the
full history, every size toll and measurement, is archived; see its
"Original" line); this file is what governs a file now. Files
are listed by family; a file with a header comment of its own carries its
detail there.

## File map

**The core's edge.**
- `ReelCore.swift` — with its `ReelCore+<Area>.swift` files, the only files
  that call `rc_*` (spec §11 CJ-8 (l)); a new wrapper goes in the file of its
  area. `ReelCore.swift` holds `ReelProject`
  (handle + lazily decoded `ProjectSnapshot`; `json`, `snapshot` and
  `planJSON` are memoised PER HANDLE, so keep handles rather than minting
  them; so is `sourceMap(_:)`, `rc_project_source_map` decoded and checked
  once per handle and clip, SR-20), timecode, snapping (export presets/sizes/settings are
  `ExportValues.swift`'s, a pure move, HDR H-1), `ReelSpeed.limits` (the
  core's speed range and audio ceiling, typed as `SpeedLimits` in
  `CoreValues.swift` — no Swift file types a speed bound), `ReelColor` (`rc_normalise_color`, G-25) and `ReelAgentSocket` (below);
  `ReelCore+MediaFiles.swift` holds the media files the core reads or writes —
  `ReelContainer` (`rc_container_*`, a WebM/Matroska file's index, #216-R), `ReelCube`,
  `ReelHDR10` (`rc_hdr10_peak`, spec §11 HD-6; `av1Peak`, `rc_hdr10_av1_peak`, HD-18;
  `stillPeak`, `rc_hdr10_still_peak`, HD-20), `ReelAV1` and `ReelWebM` (`rc_webm_*`, the
  `av1_webm` writer, spec §11 CX-15) — `ReelCore+Cursor.swift` holds `ReelCursor`
  (`rc_cursor_open`, `rc_cursor_free`: a cursor file's open, which is its check, spec
  §11 CU-9, CU-15; road map creator-jobs CU1a; and `query`, `rc_cursor_query`'s one
  JSON request, CU2, spec §11 CU-25, and the static `query(_:tracks:project:)`, the
  same call over n tracks with a project (`plan_zooms`, CU-70)) — `ReelCore+Framing.swift`
  holds `SpeakerMatch` and `ReelProject.speakerMatch` (`rc_project_speaker_match`, road map
  creator-jobs VR6b, spec §11 VR-65: the face-to-microphone match Make Vertical's sheet
  confirms) — and `ReelCore+Graphics.swift` the graphics engine's
  wrappers (below), with `ReelGraphicPackage` (`rc_graphic_package_write`, G-46; `read`,
  `rc_graphic_package_read`, G-47), `GraphicLibrary.usage()` (`rc_graphic_library_usage`)
  and `GraphicLibrary.imageCache(limit:)` (`rc_graphic_image_cache`, G-39) — both pure moves
  out of `ReelCore.swift` (road map creator-jobs CJ0d, T15); `ReelCoreError`, `Fps.ffiPair` and `ReelTime`'s
  seconds conversions are `CoreValues.swift`'s (G6 phase 5's toll T2 and speed ramps SR4-0,
  pure moves); the typed patches are `TypedPatches.swift`'s (`VideoPatch`,
  `AudioPatch`, `ClipPatch`, the `ActionPatch` extension; a pure move, B73),
  `TextPatch` (with `case`, `words` and `word_style`) is `TextPatch.swift`'s,
  moved out so it could grow, and `ShapePatch` `ShapePatch.swift`'s (a pure
  move, the toll for `ReelColor`). `VideoPatch.color` is a sparse `ColorPatch`
  (`GradeProps.swift`, which holds `ColorAdjust` (moved out of
  `ProjectSnapshot.swift`, grading-2 G2-0) with its neutrality helpers, and
  `LayerUniforms.apply(tone:)`, and the wheels' `ColorWheel`, `ColorWheels`,
  `ColorWheelPatch`, `ColorWheelsPatch`, `ColorWheelKind` and
  `LayerUniforms.apply(wheels:)` (GR-11)); `VideoPatch.curves` is
  `CurveProps.swift`'s `ColorCurvesPatch`, beside `CurvePoint`,
  `CurveDomain`, `CurveChannel`, `CurveBlend` (a channel blended inside an
  action, spec §11 GR-34; `ColorCurves.blends`, never encoded), `ColorCurves` and
  `LayerUniforms.apply(curves:)` (GR-12, the hue curves GR-32; a
  pure move out of `GradeProps.swift`, grading-4 T4-0); `VideoPatch.qualifier` is
  `QualifierProps.swift`'s `ColorQualifierPatch`, beside `ColorQualifier` (its
  `blur`, `blursSelection` and `selectionSigma`, GR-35), `QualifierUniforms`
  (`blurred`, set only by `drawAdjustment`) and the pick's `QualifierSample`
  (GR-13), so a row writes

**Frozen files.** `EditorViewController.swift`, `TimelineView.swift`,
`PreviewCanvasView.swift`, `AgentServer.swift` are **frozen at current
size**: anything adding more than ~50 lines goes in an extension file
(`EditorViewController+<Feature>.swift`, `TimelineView+<Feature>.swift`,
`AgentServer+<Feature>.swift`) or a new `…SheetController`, and the frozen
file keeps only the wiring — a stored property, a closure assignment, a
validator arm, a draw call. The pieces extension files build on are therefore
internal, not private. Pitfalls: a selector declared `@objc` on an extension
needs NO forward in the frozen file (a second declaration is an error); a
command whose body sits at the foot of a non-extension feature file carries
its validator arm there too, or the item falls through to the closing
`return true`; `handleEditorCharacter`'s bare-key `switch` matches in SOURCE
order, so a bare `case "x"` goes BELOW any modified `case "x" where …`; and
`handleEditorKey` refuses while a sheet is attached, because a sheet is
window-modal and the preview panel's forwarded keys would otherwise reach
the key map behind it.

title: Turn a clip's picture or sound off
description: What it means when one half of a clip is switched off, which commands do it, and how the clip then looks on the timeline.
---

import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

A clip has two halves, its picture and its sound, and each can be switched off while the clip stays where it is. A switched-off half adds nothing to the picture or the mix, and it comes back when the half is switched on again.

<AtAGlance
  menu={['Clip ▸ Detach Audio', 'Clip ▸ Attach Audio']}
  keys={['⌥⌘D', '⇧⌥⌘D']}
  tools="set_enabled"
/>

## Turn a half off

There's no switch for this in the inspector. Commands flip the halves as part of what they do:

| Command | What it switches |
| --- | --- |
| [**Clip ▸ Detach Audio**](/audio/detach-and-attach/) | Turns the clip's sound off and adds a sound-only copy on the track below, with its picture off. |
| [**Clip ▸ Attach Audio**](/audio/detach-and-attach/) | Merges a detached pair back into one clip with its sound on. |
| [**Clip ▸ Switch by Speaker…**](/multicam/switch-by-speaker/) | Can turn off the picture of the camera clips it replaces, and their sound when **Mute the cameras' own sound** is ticked. |

To silence a clip's sound by hand, use **Mute** on the [Sound tab](/audio/sound-tab/). To hide its picture, set its [opacity](/canvas/transform/) to 0 or [hide the track](/timeline/hide-and-lock-tracks/).

## How the clip looks

| Switched off | On the timeline |

editing/paste-attributes.mdx:86:| A movie or still clip | Remove Background with its subject set to Foreground, which only an image clip can take |
editing/slip-and-roll.mdx:25:- A [freeze frame](/speed/freeze-frame/) slips too, which changes the frame it holds. It stops one frame short of the end of its file.
editing/split-at-shot-changes.mdx:31:The command is greyed out until a selected clip shows a video file's picture. Anything else in the selection is left alone: text, an image, a freeze frame, an audio file, a nest, or a clip with its [picture turned off](/editing/enable-picture-and-sound/).
editing/timing-section.mdx:68:If the selection also holds anything else, such as text, a shape, a picture or a freeze frame, there's no Timing section.
editing/trimming.mdx:61:Pictures, freeze frames, text, shapes, graphics, adjustment clips and nests have no file length, so they trim to any length. A trimmed [nest](/editing/nests/) cuts nothing inside it. Trimming its end hides the tail. A nest always plays from its own first frame, so trimming its start moves what's inside along with the new start, rather than cutting into it.
reference/limits.mdx:41:Crop, Corner Radius and Chroma Key work only on video, image and still clips. A nest clip can't take a [blend mode](/canvas/blend-modes/), and Add Blurred Background isn't offered for one.
speed/edit-a-ramped-clip.mdx:3:description: What a speed change, trim, split or freeze frame does to a clip with a speed ramp, and why Frame Job sometimes won't make the edit.
speed/edit-a-ramped-clip.mdx:40:Trims, slips, rolls, splits, freeze frames and transitions all read the ramp, so each cut or held frame is the frame the ramp actually plays at that moment.
speed/freeze-frame.mdx:29:Frame Job splits the clip at the playhead, opens 2 s of empty time there, and fills the gap on the clip's track with a still of that source frame. The rest of the clip picks up after the still. All of this is one undo step, called **Freeze Frame**.
speed/freeze-frame.mdx:84:`freeze_frame` takes the clip, an optional `at` (the playhead if left out) and an optional `duration` (2 s if left out), so it can hold any moment of a clip without moving the playhead, for any length of at least one frame. An `at` outside the clip or a shorter `duration` is an error. `slip` on a freeze frame moves the frame it holds. See [Tools: speed and time](/mcp/tools-speed/).
speed/overview.mdx:28:| Hold one frame still | [Freeze Frame](/speed/freeze-frame/) | A still clip fills a gap opened at the playhead. |
speed/overview.mdx:41:| A still image, a freeze frame, text, a shape or an adjustment clip | No | Stretched or squeezed with the range |
speed/rate-stretch.mdx:45:| The end edge of a still, text, shape, graphic or any other clip | An ordinary trim, with the undo step **Trim Clip** |
speed/reverse.mdx:40:Reverse is for clips of a video or audio file. Text, shapes, graphics, adjustment clips, nests, pictures and freeze frames have no Reverse rows.
speed/reverse.mdx:134:A picture on the timeline looks the same backwards, so it has no Reverse rows and nothing to render. The same goes for a [freeze frame](/speed/freeze-frame/).

## `add_text_clip`

Adds a text clip, a title, as the [**Add Text**](/text-and-shapes/text-clips/#add-a-text-clip) button does. It has no source, so it can be any length. Style it afterwards with `set_text` and place it with `set_video`.

| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `track` | integer | Yes | The track id. |
| `at` | integer | Yes | Where it starts, in ticks. |
| `duration` | integer | No | Its length, in ticks. Default 5 seconds (`3000000`). |
| `text` | object or string | No | A plain string is the words. An object is a `set_text` patch merged over the Title preset. Default: the preset's own placeholder, "Title". |
| `scope` | integer | No | The nest to add it in. |
| `project` | string | No | The project to act on. |

A new clip is the Title preset: 72 px white Source Sans 3 Bold, centred. An object can set anything [`set_text`](/mcp/tools-clip-properties/) can, including `content`, `font`, `size`, `color`, `align`, `valign`, `outline`, `backdrop`, `width`, `animation`, `case`, `words` and `word_style`. See [Patches](/mcp/patches/).

```json
{ "track": 3, "at": 1800000, "text": "Chapter one" }
{ "track": 3, "at": 1800000, "duration": 1200000,
  "text": { "content": "Chapter one", "size": 96, "align": "left" } }
```

It's refused for a duration under one frame, for an unknown key or a bad value in the patch, by name, and when it would break the overlap rule. The undo step is called "Add Text".

## `add_shape_clip`

Adds a rectangle, ellipse, line or arrow drawn over the video, as [**Add Shape**](/text-and-shapes/shape-clips/#add-a-shape-clip) does. Like text, it has no source and can be any length. [`set_shape`](/mcp/tools-clip-properties/) changes it afterwards and `set_video` places it.

| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `track` | integer | Yes | The track id. |
| `at` | integer | Yes | Where it starts, in ticks. |
| `duration` | integer | No | Its length, in ticks. Default 5 seconds (`3000000`). |
| `shape` | object or string | No | A plain string is a kind: `rectangle`, `ellipse`, `line` or `arrow`. An object is a `set_shape` patch merged over the default rectangle. |
| `scope` | integer | No | The nest to add it in. |
| `project` | string | No | The project to act on. |

Leave out `shape` for the default: a 320×120 rectangle, outlined with no fill. An object can set `kind`, `width`, `height`, `stroke`, `fill`, `radius`, `arrow_start`, `arrow_end`, `from`, `to` and `gradient`.

A rounded rectangle is a rectangle with a `radius`, not a kind of its own. An arrow is created with its head on, so pass `arrow_end: false` for a bare diagonal. A box bigger than the canvas gets Fit scale when `fit_new_clips` is on, as oversized footage does.

It's refused for a duration under one frame, for an unknown kind, key or value, by name, and when it would break the overlap rule. The undo step is called "Add Shape".

## `add_background`

Puts a backdrop on a new back-most track, starting at 0 and running the timeline's length, as [**Clip ▸ Add Background**](/canvas/backgrounds/) does. The clip is named "Background".

| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `color` | array of four numbers | No | The plate's colour, as `[r, g, b, a]`, each from 0 to 1. White when left out. |
| `media` | integer | No | A media id to show instead of a colour. `import_media` adds a file. |
| `duration` | integer | No | Its length, in ticks. Default: the whole timeline's length, and never less than one frame. |
| `scope` | integer | No | The nest to add it in. |
| `project` | string | No | The project to act on. |

A full-canvas gradient is this clip with [`set_shape`](/mcp/tools-clip-properties/)'s `gradient` after it.

With `media` the picture goes there at Fill scale, where `add_clip` would Fit it, because a plate that leaves the canvas showing down one side has failed. A video plate stops where its file does, whatever `duration` says. A picture runs the timeline, or for `duration` when you give one.

It answers both `new_tracks` and `new_clips`, and the track holds the lower id.

These are errors, and nothing is added:

- `media` and `color` together
- a `duration` under one frame
- a file with no picture, such as a sound file
- a colour that isn't four numbers from 0 to 1

fixes.pages: effects/text-behind-subject, mcp/tools-clip-properties (text_behind_subject), mcp/tools-adding-clips (add_text_clip; outside my list, but it contradicted text-presets)
fixes.was: The title gets the Title preset, and add_text_clip's default is the Title preset, while text-presets says Title is 9 % of the canvas and not a new clip's look.
fixes.now: The title takes the look a new text clip starts with, 72 px, and left-out text is "Title".
fixes.evidence: app/Sources/BehindSubjectPlan.swift:130 sends plain add_text_clip with content only. core/src/edit_described.rs:57 sets size 72. The 9 % preset is TextPane.swift:501.

fixes.was: Spotlight is 'dimming the canvas' or dims 'everything' outside a shape, while effects/spotlight says it dims this clip only.
fixes.now: It dims the clip outside the shape.
fixes.evidence: Compositor.metal pipeline step 6: the spotlight dim is a light on the layer.

fixes.was: A stretch of the clip where no person was found draws uncut, which contradicts remove-background.
fixes.now: A clip with no person in any frame it plays draws uncut. Once a person is found anywhere, a frame with no person keeps little or nothing.
fixes.evidence: CutoutMasks.swift:154 found(...) is asked per clip window; Compositor+Cutout.swift:40; the same rule in CutoutStatus.swift.

fixes.was: falloff is a fraction of the cropped height, while effects/reflection says it fades across Height.
fixes.now: falloff is how far it fades across height: 0.5 ends at half opacity, 1 reaches transparent at height.
fixes.evidence: Compositor.metal:1979-1981: depth is measured against reflectionHeight, and fade = opacity × (1 − falloff × depth).

fixes.was: arrow_start and arrow_end: 'whether a line or arrow has a head', while lines-and-arrows and shape-settings say only Arrow draws one.
fixes.now: Only an arrow draws a head; a line keeps the setting and shows none.
fixes.evidence: LayerRenderers.swift:379-380: wantsStart and wantsEnd need kind == .arrow.

fixes.was: Add Shape is 'the only way to add a shape clip', and 'these four' buttons have no menu item.
fixes.now: Add Shape is the only way to choose a shape, and Solid Color also makes one. Added an Add Text (Aa) row, added add_text_clip to the page's tools, and dropped the count.
fixes.evidence: addTextClip and showAddShapeMenu appear only in TimelineBar.swift:129-132 and in no AppDelegate*.swift. Solid Color: EditorViewController+AddClips.swift:135-141.

fixes.was: Place on Canvas beeps at four regions, and the modes list had no playhead ending. effects/obscure says the button is greyed and that moving the playhead off the clip stops it.

fixes.evidence: VideoPane+Obscure.swift (enabled: list().count < ObscureProps.max); EditorViewController+ZoomRegion.swift:109-121 and :162 (syncRegionMode, regionTarget).

fixes.was: The nest note named only Blend as greyed.
fixes.now: Blend and Motion Blur are greyed.
fixes.evidence: VideoPane+Transform.swift:118 and :155-157 (motionBlurApplies); set_video also refuses above 0 on a nest clip.

fixes.was: A backdrop is as wide as Width plus its padding.
fixes.now: Width plus its padding on each side.
fixes.evidence: LayerRenderersText.swift:139-145: the inset applies per side, as text-outline-and-backdrop describes.

fixes.was: On an adjustment clip 'any blend mode' is an error, and foreground is 'the picture's foreground object'.

app_defects.title: set_video's own description misstates reflection falloff
app_defects.evidence: app/Sources/AgentCatalog+VideoPatch.swift:251 says 'height and falloff are fractions of the layer's cropped height'. The shader (app/Resources/Shaders/Compositor.metal:1979-1981) measures falloff across the reflection's own height. An agent reading the tool description gets the wrong meaning.

app_defects.title: 'Title preset' names two different looks
app_defects.evidence: add_text_clip and text_behind_subject call the 72 px default 'the Title preset' (AgentCatalog+Clips.swift:109,121-122; AgentCatalog+BehindSubject.swift:17,47; core/src/edit.rs:116).
